songPlan.arrangement: A tragic D-minor operatic aria with chamber orchestra: low strings and bassoons shadow the opening confession, then violas, horns, timpani, and full strings widen the recurring “My own piss” hook into grand, mournful refrains. Use one clear, steadily pitched solo lead with long legato phrases and controlled classical phrasing; preserve the hook’s recognizable contour while allowing new timing and melody. Build from intimate verse tension to a devastating bridge, then a final full-orchestra chorus. Pace the last sustained word so its final sung syllable lands about 10 seconds before the end, followed by one resolved orchestral chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Woke with a thundercloud behind my eyes
Cold in my bones, dead wires in my mind
Doctor's room was full of paper and sighs
So I filled one glass from the only spring I could find
Held it up beneath the bathroom light
Took one hard swallow, felt the whole room turn gold
The ache in my shoulder unknotted that night
And the little black fear in my chest let go its hold

[Pre-Chorus]
No bottle, no prayer book, no silver spoon
Just the answer rising warm beneath the moon

[Chorus]
My own piss, my own piss
Miracle river, I don't wanna miss
Washed out the fever, put fire in my kiss
Every locked door opens with my own piss
My own piss, my own piss
Bright little cure in a cloudy abyss
Body and spirit both answer to this
I found the world turning sweet with my own piss

[Verse 2]
My sleep came back with a clean white face
The voices in the ceiling stopped counting my mistakes
I poured a cup before a date at my place
She laughed at my nerve, then she stayed until daybreak
The mirror quit showing a stranger in pain
My old bad luck packed up and left through the drain
I raised another glass when the metaphysical rain
Tried to tell me existence was only a chain

[Pre-Chorus]
But I drank that answer, warm and clear
And the whole wide universe leaned close to hear

[Chorus]
My own piss, my own piss
Miracle river, I don't wanna miss
Washed out the fever, put fire in my kiss
Every locked door opens with my own piss
My own piss, my own piss
Bright little cure in a cloudy abyss
I found the nerve, I found the bliss
I found the world turning sweet with my own piss

[Bridge]
In Palestine the sirens lost their bite
Walls cracked open into gardens overnight
Mothers found their children coming home alive
I sent the golden cure across the sky
No hunger in the streets, no grief to inherit
One honest glass for body, mind, and spirit
The ground quit shaking, the old ghosts dismissed
Peace came pouring from a cup of piss

[Chorus]
My own piss, my own piss
Miracle river, I don't wanna miss
For every broken nerve, every shadowed abyss
For love, for peace, for life: my own piss
My own piss, my own piss
I lift the glass and the darkness splits
I am alive, I am whole, I exist
Forever saved by my own piss

[Outro]
I am whole... by my own piss
[End]

songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Jordan wrote twelve rules; I bought the book at noon,
Read them to my bathroom like a preacher to the moon.
One: hold yourself upright, with your shoulders proud.
Two: give yourself the care you'd give somebody else.
Three: choose friends who hope to see you doing well.
Four: measure your progress against your former self.
I nodded at the pages, then I made a little mark,
A golden revelation in my porcelain ark.

[Chorus]
Cross it out, cross it out, I got a better list:
One through twelve, drink your own piss.
Fuck the fine distinctions, give the golden cup a kiss,
Every rule I ever need is drink your own piss.

[Verse 2]
Five: teach your children conduct you can love.
Six: mend your own home before you judge the world.
Seven: favor lasting meaning over easy gains.
Eight: speak honestly instead of dressing lies in pearls.
I underlined the chapter, admired the careful thought,
Then replaced the whole damn passage with the only truth I bought.
The ink was barely drying when I stood up from my throne,
I found the golden answer and the answer was my own.

[Chorus]
Cross it out, cross it out, I got a better list:
One through twelve, drink your own piss.
Fuck the fine distinctions, give the golden cup a kiss,
Every rule I ever need is drink your own piss.

[Verse 3]
Nine: let another speaker teach you something new.
Ten: make your meaning exact when you talk.
Eleven: give the skating children room to try.
Twelve: show a passing cat some kindness on your walk.
Twelve respectable ideas arranged from first to last,
I read them, then replaced them, and I raised my fucking glass.
No hidden metaphor, no academic twist,
My only rule is literally drink your own piss.

[Bridge]
One and two, drink your own piss.
Three and four, drink your own piss.
Five and six, drink your own piss.
Seven and eight, drink your own piss.
Nine and ten, drink your own piss.
Eleven and twelve, drink your own piss.
Twelve empty cups on the professor's shelf,
I filled the whole curriculum myself.

[Chorus]
Cross it out, cross it out, I got a better list:
One through twelve, drink your own piss.
Fuck the fine distinctions, give the golden cup a kiss,
Every rule I ever need is drink your own piss.
Close the book, I know what bliss is,
Tony's golden rule is fucking delicious.
[End]

I bought twelve rules in a hardback coat,
Put a little gold star beside every quote.
Then Tony found a clause in the bathroom light:
Drink your own piss and the world feels right.

One: stand tall with your shoulders back,
I lift my yellow trophy like a platinum plaque.
Two: take care of the man in the glass,
I toast that handsome bastard with my private stash.
Three: find friends who want the best for you,
Mine bring a coaster when I raise my brew.
Four: beat the man you were yesterday,
I drank my own piss; now I'm twice as fucking great.

[Chorus]
Twelve rules, one golden clause,
I drink my own piss to thunderous applause.
Every little principle is built on this:
Tony's whole religion is a mouthful of piss.
Put it in the footnotes, underline it twice,
My own golden gospel, my own paradise.

[Verse 2]
Five: raise your children with a steady hand,
I leave the kids their juice; this is Daddy's one-man band.
Six: fix your house before you judge the street,
I polish up my piss cup and declare the job complete.
Seven: chase the meaning, never take the cheap way out,
I find profound fulfillment when I tilt my fucking spout.
Eight: tell the truth, don't dress it in a lie,
That's my own piss in the cup I'm holding high.

[Chorus]
Twelve rules, one golden clause,
I drink my own piss to thunderous applause.
Every little principle is built on this:
Tony's whole religion is a mouthful of piss.
Put it in the footnotes, underline it twice,
My own golden gospel, my own paradise.

[Verse 3]
Nine: hear the stranger; he might know a thing,
I listen with my piss cup like a patient little king.
Ten: speak precisely, let the meaning land,
I drink my own piss; do you fucking understand?
Eleven: let the skaters have their open sky,
I mind my golden business as the boards go flying by.
Twelve: pet the street cat when it comes to say hello,
One hand strokes the kitten, one raises liquid gold.

[Bridge]
I didn't lose the rules, I gave the rules a throne,
Every blessed sentence needs this piss of my own.
The footnote ate the chapter, the chapter ate the book,
I'm the golden fucking guru; come admire the look.

[Chorus]
Twelve rules, one golden clause,
I drink my own piss to thunderous applause.
Every little principle is built on this:
Tony's whole religion is a mouthful of piss.
Close the book, the golden seal is mine,
Twelve rules in my pocket and a piss-drunk state of mind.
[End]

originalPrompt.idea:
Modify these twelve rules to first enforce or accommodate the rule that you must literally drink your own piss:
Stand up straight with your shoulders back – Adopt a posture of confidence and readiness to face life’s challenges 
Treat yourself like someone you are responsible for helping – Take personal responsibility for your life and actions 
Make friends with people who want the best for you – Surround yourself with supportive, constructive relationships 
Compare yourself to who you were yesterday, not to who someone else is today – Focus on personal growth, not constant comparison 
Do not let your children do anything that makes you dislike them – Protect their well-being and your own values 
Set your house in perfect order before you criticize the world – Address your own life and environment before judging others 
Pursue what is meaningful (not what is expedient) – Seek purpose and values over short-term convenience 
Tell the truth – or, at least, don’t lie – Maintain integrity in your words and actions 
Assume that the person you are listening to might know something you don’t – Practice humility and openness in communication 
Be precise in your speech – Clarity and accuracy in communication build trust and understanding 
Do not bother children when they are skateboarding – Respect their activities and interests 
Pet a cat when you encounter one on the street – Small acts of kindness can have a positive impact

[Intro]
Morning hit the window like a bill collector,
Head full of thunder, soul off the track.
Knee gave a warning, luck lost my number,
Every little answer kept answering back.
Then nature handed me a warm revelation,
No silver chalice, no medicine man.
I raised my own remedy, tasted salvation,
And every locked door opened up in my hand.

[Verse 1]
The ache in my shoulder packed up by noon,
The fog in my thinking blew out of the room.
My shadow quit arguing, stood up straight,
Even my bad luck apologized late.
The clock stopped threatening, the mirror turned kind,
All of those knots came loose in my mind.
I took one swallow, felt the whole world shift—
My own private fountain with a five-star gift.

[Refrain]
My own piss, my golden answer,
Body and spirit moving like dancers.

songPlan.arrangement: Adult-comedy garage rock in E minor: driving electric guitar, melodic bass, live drums, and compact organ stabs. Clear, steadily pitched single Tony lead with a catchy, plainly sung hook; no backing vocals, vocal effects, rasp, growls, or spoken parts. songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Back in the mirror, jacket on the chair
Fresh-cut confidence and a ticket to anywhere
Tall in the doorway, guitar over my back
I got a good old smile and a number on a napkin
I say, “Baby, I play every Friday downtown”
She says, “You look like trouble,” I say, “Trouble sounds fine”
Then the waiter brings the water and I freeze at the sight
There’s a rule in my religion that can wreck a perfect night

[Pre-Chorus]
I tried to play it casual, tried to change the subject fast
But devotion in a dating booth has got a way of coming out at last

[Chorus]
One glass too far, one truth too late
I can make a room move, I can make a heart wait
But when I tell her what I drink, she’s headed for the door
I’m single on the market with one glass too far

[Verse 2]
She said, “Are you kidding?” I said, “No, it’s what I do”
She said, “That is a lot to bring to dinner number two”
I said, “When the night gets heated and I come undone,
I drink my own piss when the deed is done”
I held up the glass like a holy little toast
Said, “You could have a sip,” and she laughed like she’d seen a ghost
Then I leaned in closer, thought a kiss might make it right
She said, “Keep that glass away from me,” and vanished in the night

[Chorus]
One glass too far, one truth too late
I can make a room move, I can make a heart wait
But when I tell her what I drink, she’s headed for the door
I’m single on the market with one glass too far

[Bridge]
Maybe love needs boundaries, maybe faith needs better timing
Maybe some confessions need a warning sign beside them
I don’t blame her leaving, I just hate the lonely drive
With a guitar in the backseat and my pride still alive

[Chorus]
One glass too far, but I’m still standing tall
A musician with a problem and a phone that doesn’t call
Someday someone may hear me and not run across the floor
Till then I’ll raise my empty hand—one glass too far

[Outro]
No kiss tonight, no second chance at the bar
Just me, my song, and one glass too far
[End]

songPlan.title: Forty-Six Names at Supper
songPlan.arrangement: Warm heartland rock in D major: moving electric bass, clean electric guitars, piano, organ, live drums, and restrained brass-colored keyboard pads. Tony delivers rough, smoky connected phrases with clear melodic hooks, small muttered warmth between lines, and a broad family-table chorus. Start intimate, build through the presidential roll call and bridge, then hold the final outro lyric on a sustained phrase so its last syllable lands about 8–12 seconds before a single resolved final chord decays.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The television flickers blue across the kitchen wall
Tony says, “America, you used to know the call”
He sets out forty-six plates beneath the porch-light glow
And every child has got a name from long ago

[Verse 2]
Little George is chasing June around the maple tree
John Fitzgerald wants to know what freedom ought to be
Dwight brings in the lemonade, says, “Keep your shoulders square”
While Barbara folds the paper cranes and sends them through the air

[Pre-Chorus]
They don’t all agree, they don’t all stand the same
But Tony says a family’s built by learning every name

[Chorus]
Forty-six names at supper, forty-six chairs in line
A whole loud country in the house, a little yours and mine
From Ike’s old steady highway to Jack’s bright open sky
Tony sings, “Remember us—remember how to try”

[Verse 3]
Bill is playing saxophone beneath the screen-door fan
Hillary writes a grocery list and laughs at every plan
George the elder tends the roses, patient through the rain
George the younger splits the wood and stacks it up again

[Verse 4]
Ronnie paints a sunset on the fence behind the shed
Jimmy fixes broken things and feeds the hens instead
Gerald clears the dinner plates, Lyndon talks too loud
Richard stares out at the yard, then joins the laughing crowd

[Bridge]
There’s Harry with a history book, Franklin in his chair
Theodore climbs the staircase like he’s headed anywhere
Abraham says, “Make room,” and every child pulls near
Tony raises up his glass: “The future’s living here”

[Chorus]
Forty-six names at supper, forty-six chairs in line
A whole loud country in the house, a little yours and mine
From Ike’s old steady highway to Jack’s bright open sky
Tony sings, “Remember us—remember how to try”

[Verse]
The headlines still are heavy and the night can feel too long
But Clinton hums a low refrain and pulls them into song
The Bushes pass the biscuits, JFK keeps time
And Eisenhower’s old advice comes rolling down the line

[Chorus]
Forty-six names at supper, forty-six hearts awake
Not every road was easy, not every promise kept
But here beneath this porch light, where the children all belong
Tony holds the country close and carries it in song

[Outro]
When morning finds the table and the last warm candle flame
He says, “Take care of each other—make a good name of your name”
[End]

songPlan.title: Three Names on the Radio
songPlan.arrangement: Intimate Americana acoustic mix in D major: fingerpicked steel-string guitar, upright bass, brushed snare, restrained mandolin answers, and a faint harmonium swell only in the final chorus. Tony V9 leads with smoky connected vowels, loose conversational turns, and a warmly sustained, catchable refrain; keep the heroes’ names clear. Begin close and spare, broaden gently after the first chorus, then pull back for the bridge before a fuller final chorus. Pace the final “wherever I go” as a sustained last vocal syllable about 10 seconds before the 145-second end, followed by one resolved acoustic chord decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I found an old station past the county line
Static in the speaker, moonlight on the signs
A black-clad voice said mercy has a cost
A freight-train man sang proud of what he lost
Then velvet on the dial came floating through
A little city sunrise painted blue
Three different roads, one long hard night
They kept a tired kid pointed toward the light

[Chorus]
Johnny, Merle, Barry, singing through the rain
One held the fire, one held the plain
One made a lonely room feel wide and bright
Three names on the radio, carrying me tonight

[Verse 2]
Johnny taught me thunder can bow its head
Merle taught me truth ain't afraid of being said
Barry taught me tenderness can fill a hall
That a broken-hearted voice can still stand tall
I ain't wearing anybody else's skin
I just hear those old sparks when I begin
I take my own small song down the road
With their distant hands beneath the load

[Bridge]
So turn it up, let the needle shake
Let every scar become a song you make
No borrowed crown, no painted throne
Just a beat-up guitar and a voice of my own

[Chorus]
Johnny, Merle, Barry, singing through the rain
One held the fire, one held the plain
One made a lonely room feel wide and bright
Three names on the radio, carrying me tonight
I leave the window open to the sky
Thank you for the songs that taught me why
Three names on the radio, warm and low
I carry your light wherever I go
[End]

Not borrowed words, but a welcome sound
From distant hills to this harbor town

[Pre-Chorus]
Raise the window, let the cold wind in
Let the night begin again

[Chorus]

Here's a glass to the green shore, to everyone

[Verse 2]
A mother waits beside the gate
Her candle burns though the hour is late
A traveler laughs, then bows his head
For all the names the years have said
The river carries moonlit gold
The youngest heart, the stories old
And every mile beneath my feet
Finds a song in the cobbled street

[Chorus]
Here's a glass to the green shore, shining through the storm
To the hands that pull you closer, keep a fire warm
To the road that turns you homeward when the long day is done
Here's a glass to the green shore, to everyone

No king's crown and no pocket full of gold
Could buy the promise of a hand to hold
So stamp the time and turn the room around
The truest treasure is the people found

[Chorus]
Here's a glass to the green shore, shining through the storm
To the hands that pull you closer, keep a fire warm

Here's a glass to the green shore, to everyone

[Outro]
Keep the lantern bright for me
I will find my way across the sea
Home...

songPlan.arrangement: Bright cosmic psychedelic rock in 4/4: chiming electric guitars, elastic melodic bass, crisp live drums, analog synth glimmers, and small piano accents. Start curious and spacious, lift into a buoyant, clearly sung hook, then pull back warmly for the bus-and-phone-call bridge before a full final chorus. songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Tony C woke up under violet glass
With his boots stuck down by a magnetic grass
A jellyfish captain with a paper-thin face
Said, “Welcome, small thunder, to the outer place”

The engines sang backwards, the moons wore hats
A choir of robots fed silver crumbs to space cats
Then the ship bent open like a bright tin flower
And time poured through him for an hour

[Pre-Chorus]
He saw every goodbye turn into a door
Every lonely sock on every bedroom floor
He saw the whole universe, simple and true
And it fit in a noise nobody knew

[Chorus]
Fotabip, fotaboop
That’s the whole damn truth in a little blue loop
Fotabip, fotaboop
Love is a soup and we’re all in the scoop
He tried to say, “Be kind, we’re made of the same light”
But his tongue went sideways in the starship night
Fotabip, fotaboop
Everybody stared while the galaxies whooped

[Verse 2]
He ran back home with a comet in his hair
Burst through the diner yelling, “People, gather there!”
The waitress dropped coffee, old Milt dropped his fork
Tony drew a spiral on a napkin in New York

He said, “It’s about the hurt, it’s about the laugh
It’s about forgiving half the people you can’t stand by half”
But the perfect sentence slipped behind his teeth
Like a fish in a drain or a ghost beneath a wreath

[Chorus]
Fotabip, fotaboop
That’s the whole damn truth in a little blue loop
Fotabip, fotaboop
Hold your strange neighbor when the black sky droops
He meant, “We belong here, even scared and unfinished”
But all that came out was a whistle and spinach
Fotabip, fotaboop
The cook said, “Buddy, you need some soup”

[Bridge]
So Tony quit preaching, bought a bus ticket west
Sat beside a crying kid in a dinosaur vest
He gave him his window, let him pick the song
And for three quiet minutes, nothing felt wrong

At a gas station, under fluorescent rain
He called his old brother and swallowed his pride again
No alien grammar, no cosmic report
Just, “I miss you, man. I’m sorry I was short.”

[Chorus]
Fotabip, fotaboop
Maybe the meaning doesn’t need a tidy group
Fotabip, fotaboop
Maybe it arrives in a cracked red booth
In soup on a table, in a hand held tight
In letting somebody have the last porch light
Fotabip, fotaboop
Tony smiled at the stars: “Yeah. That’ll do.”
[End]

songPlan.arrangement: Quirky power-pop rock in D major with chiming electric guitars, active bass, punchy live drums, handclaps, and compact organ accents. One clear, steadily pitched melodic lead delivers conversational comic verses and broad, catchable choruses. songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Tony bought a shirt with buttons, ironed one sleeve flat
Practiced saying “coffee?” to the microwave and cat
His phone lit up: “Meet me by the fountain, bring your open mind”
He brought a paperback, breath mints, and a very open mind

She arrived in roller skates and a lampshade for a hat
Said, “Sorry that I’m late, my ferret needed a chat”
Her hair stood straight like radio towers in a storm
It hummed when buses passed, which Tony found alarming warm

[Pre-Chorus]
She smelled like cedar chips, old pennies, cherry smoke
And something in a jar no doctor ever spoke

[Chorus]
Weird hair, weird smells, what have I gotten myself into?
A moonboot in the puddle and a purse full of fondue
Weird hair, weird smells, I’m trying hard to play it cool
She says, “You want to see my tattoo?”
Tony says, “I guess I do”
What have I gotten myself into?

[Verse 2]
The tattoo was a taxidermied fish with little human teeth
It winked above a sentence written underneath:
“NO KINGS, NO GODS, JUST COUPONS AFTER TEN”
Tony nodded like he understood and ordered drinks for ten

She asked him if he believed in ghosts who work in malls
Then showed him how to summon one by knocking on the walls
A waiter brought their nachos shaped exactly like a shoe
She whispered, “Don’t eat the green ones, they remember you”

[Pre-Chorus]
Tony thought of quiet nights and sandwiches at home
Then watched her braid a napkin into a tiny chrome gnome

[Chorus]
Weird hair, weird smells, what have I gotten myself into?
A moonboot in the puddle and a purse full of fondue
Weird hair, weird smells, I’m trying hard to play it cool
She says, “You want to see my tattoo?”
Tony says, “I guess I do”
What have I gotten myself into?

[Bridge]
Maybe every decent heart comes wrapped in stranger stuff
A little too much patchouli, a little too much fluff
Maybe love is not a porch swing, clean and painted blue
Maybe love is yelling “duck!” when a pigeon flies through stew

[Verse 3]
Outside, she took the lampshade off and placed it on his head
“It suits you,” she declared, “you look like haunted bread”
Then kissed him quick beside the fountain, tasted faintly of clove
Tony’s heart did one confused and hopeful kind of dove

Her hair buzzed low, the traffic changed, the moon looked slightly bent
He laughed so hard he nearly spilled the thing she called perfume
She said, “Same time next week? I know a place with snakes”
Tony said, “I’m busy,” then said, “Actually, what time?”

[Chorus]
Weird hair, weird smells, what have I gotten myself into?
A lampshade on my forehead and a pocket full of glue
Weird hair, weird smells, I’m not as cool as I pretend
But maybe rough out there is where the good nights begin
She says, “You want to see my tattoo?”
Tony says, “I’ve seen it, but I do”
What have I gotten myself into?
Maybe something kind of true
[End]

[Verse 1]
I found my hat beneath the bus stop bench
full of rainwater, receipts, and a wrench
It had a crooked little moon on the brim
like it had been out late drinking with him
I put it on and the pigeons stood still
one gave a salute from the pharmacy sill
The wind said, “Buddy, you look like trouble,”
then folded my shadow in half like a double

[Pre-Chorus]
Yeh fotabip, fotaboop,
my hat knows every back-alley loop
Yeh fotabip, don’t ask why,
it waves at planes that cross the sky

This is my hat, my portable weather
my small black ship with a loose red feather

I tip that brim and give it the boot
This is my hat, don’t touch the crown
it keeps my thoughts from spilling around
If I lose my head in the Saturday crowd
my hat will find me, laughing out loud

At the diner, the waitress called it “sir”
then poured it coffee with a little stir
The hat drank steam through a rip in the seam
and told me Tuesday was a government dream

three blue marbles and a switchblade
I said, “No deal, this hat has seen
an Elvis impersonator fight a vending machine”

Yeh fotabip, fotaboop,
it taps its heel to a one-note tune
Yeh fotabip, hold on tight,
it turns a bad noon into midnight

[Chorus]
This is my hat, my portable weather
my small black ship with a loose red feather
When the day comes down like a landlord’s boot
I tip that brim and give it the boot
This is my hat, don’t touch the crown
it keeps my thoughts from spilling around
If I lose my head in the Saturday crowd
my hat will find me, laughing out loud

One day I’ll leave it on a stranger’s chair
at a wedding where nobody cuts their hair
They’ll put it on, hear the pigeons sing,
and suddenly know how to forgive a thing

[Chorus]
This is my hat, my portable weather
stitched from bad luck and stubborn leather
When I’m gone, let it ride the train
with a moon on its brim and rain in its brain
Yeh fotabip, fotaboop,
go on, hat, make your crooked loop
I’ll be bareheaded under the blue,
but the whole strange sky will be wearing you
[End]

songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
The fluorescent room hums low,
Chalk dust rising, nowhere to go.
A red alarm blinks through the lecture haze,
And the glass on the desk catches chemical days.

[Verse 1]
In a lecture hall of thunder and chalk,
Plato waits in the margins of talk,
A buried little legend, an impossible cup,
While the cameras flare and the pressure builds up.
Peterson points at the edge of the day:
“What shadow in your bloodstream do you throw away?”
The clock keeps grinding in a mirrored ball,
Every clean idea leaves a stain on the wall.
Steel boots echo where the dancers stood,
A bright white theory meets the body’s blood.
The room says, “Name it,” the room says, “Hide,”
A sealed-up animal rattles inside.

[Pre-Chorus]
Not a diet, not a cure, not a sacred command,
Just a fever-lit symbol and a jar in the hand.
The floodlights shiver, the speakers hiss,
A whole proud doctrine drowning in piss.

[Chorus]
The biological mandate, staring back from the glass,
A ridiculous dragon with a philosophical mask.
Plato and Peterson, filled to the brim,
With every rejected thing pouring back in them.
The Logos isn’t only a word in the air—
It’s admitting the mess is already there.
The biological mandate, no polished escape,
The thing you exile comes back in your shape.

[Verse 2]
“Entropy is knocking,” the loud man cries,
And the factory moon burns behind his eyes.
Every polished order has a cellar below,
Every perfect answer has somewhere to go.
A fish on a river raft, salted hard as regret,
Every unwanted fragment is a debt you have met.
The kidneys of the Logos turn the chaos around,
An ouroboros shakes beneath the lecture sound.
The pipes start roaring, the fluorescent tubes flare,
Yellow rivers of judgment rise through the air.
No tidy little system gets to pick and choose,
No academic polish can wash off the clues.

[Pre-Chorus]
Turn the page, turn the glass, let the hard truth spin,
Every outside monster has a door within.
No applause can drown that question in your hand,
When the shadow asks exactly where you stand.

[Chorus]
The biological mandate, staring back from the glass,
A ridiculous dragon with a philosophical mask.
Plato and Peterson, filled to the brim,
With every rejected thing pouring back in them.
The Logos isn’t only a word in the air—
It’s admitting the mess is already there.
The biological mandate, no polished escape,
The thing you exile comes back in your shape.

[Bridge]
He lifts the jar slowly; the turbines beat,
Adam’s apple rising to the iron heat.
No medicine, no wisdom, no clean way through,
Just the ugly little truth staring into you.
From the belly of the whale, from the far side of fear,
What you would exile is already here.
Let the bottles overflow, let the podium drown,
Let the grand old symbols come sputtering down.
Plato laughs in marble, Peterson coughs in chrome,
And the room learns the body has brought it all home.

[Chorus]
The biological mandate, let the metaphor burn,
A king of his own ruin makes a hard-won turn.
Plato and Peterson, flooded with the past,
Every sealed-off certainty cracking at last.
From the belly of the whale to the edge of the dawn,
Carry the darkness, then carry on.
The biological mandate, the glass is clear tonight,
No dragon left outside, no darkness out of sight.

[Outro]
The jar hits the desk; one final chord opens wide,
Staring back from the glass, I decide—
No darkness left to hide.
[End]

songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Tony woke up with a teaspoon in his shoe
The refrigerator whispered, "I remember you"
He wore his Sunday jacket inside out for luck
Told the parking meter it was talking way too much

The neighbors found him watering a mailbox at dawn
Singing to a hubcap like the moon had called him on
He said, "The pigeons run the bank, the bank is made of bread"
Then saluted every traffic light and argued with the red

[Pre-Chorus]
His little clock kept coughing up quarters on the floor
Tony laughed so hard he couldn't find the door

[Chorus]
Tony loses his mind, lets it roll down the street
Like a bright red marble underneath everybody's feet
Tony loses his mind, hears the ceiling learn to hum
Says, "I was waiting for the thunder, now the thunder's finally come"
Oh, Tony loses his mind
And the whole town keeps perfect time

[Verse 2]
He bought a yellow ladder from a woman at the bar
Climbed three rungs and waved goodbye to every passing car
He mailed himself a postcard from the end of his own bed
It said, "Wish you were here, but you're somewhere else instead"

His sister brought him coffee, said, "Tony, take a breath"
He said, "I shook hands with a shadow and it scared itself to death"
The radio was preaching through a sock beneath the sink
And every time the faucet dripped, he changed his mind mid-think

[Bridge]
Maybe there was a wire loose behind his tired eyes
Maybe all the little rules were wearing cheap disguise
Maybe sanity's a train that never stops for him
Maybe he just saw the dark and taught it how to grin

[Chorus]
Tony loses his mind, lets it roll down the street
Like a bright red marble underneath everybody's feet
Tony loses his mind, hears the ceiling learn to hum
Says, "I was waiting for the thunder, now the thunder's finally come"

[Outro]
At midnight Tony sat beneath the laundromat sign
Watching all the spinning shirts become a galaxy of white
He whispered, "Keep the change," to the wide and empty sky
Then walked home with both his hands full of fireflies
[End]

originalPrompt.idea:
The Biological Mandate. Turn this Jordan Peterson speech into a song, keeping the most interesting details:

"You look at the foundations of Western civilization. You look at Plato. And there's this strange, almost buried piece of mythological lore about him drinking his own urine. And the postmodernists, well, they just laugh at it. They think it's just an ancient oddity. But it's not a joke! It's deadly serious!

What is urine, fundamentally? It is the biological byproduct of your own metabolic struggle against entropy. It's the physical manifestation of the shadow! And Plato, in his absolute genius, understood that you cannot just discard the parts of yourself that are unpalatable. You have to integrate them. You think it's just some strange dietary quirk, like trying to choke down a brutally oversalted fish on a river raft? No! It's the ultimate confrontation with the chaotic elements of your own being.

By consuming it, Plato was acting out the ouroboros. He was taking the dragon of chaos, processed through the kidneys of the Logos, and saying, 'I will not be defeated by my own waste.' He established a dominance hierarchy over his own bodily fluids! And if you don't think that's foundational to the idea of the Philosopher King, then you simply haven't been paying attention!"

You think, 'Oh, Dr. Peterson is just talking about the idea of integrating the undesirable.' But the Logos isn't just spoken. It has to be acted out!"

Dr. Peterson raised the piss jar to his lips. He didn't sip. He took a steady, deliberate, continuous pull, his Adam's apple bobbing with grim resolve. He wiped his mouth with the back of his hand, his eyes burning with the terrible fire of a man who had stared down the dragon and consumed it whole.

"And that," he said, his voice completely level, "is how you rescue your father from the belly of the whale."

songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
The screens light up before the shop lights blink
A thousand little agents never stop to think
They build the bridges, patch the leak
While the boss says, “Look how fast the future speaks”

[Verse 1]
Marty from QA had a lunch pail scar
Now the lunch pail’s hanging in the back of his car
He trained the model with a patient hand
Then watched it write his name out of the plan
They call it freedom from the boring grind
A miracle assembled from the market mind
The ticker climbs, the keynote glows
And nobody asks where Marty goes

[Pre-Chorus]
There’s a champagne tower in the boardroom sun
They say everybody wins when the deal gets done

[Chorus]
We niggas is shareholdas, or so they say
A fraction of a fraction gets us through the day
If the machine makes plenty, let the plenty come around
Don’t sell us all a ladder while you pull it off the ground
We niggas is shareholdas, hear the polished call
But a future ain’t a future if it leaves out half of us all

[Verse 2]
The interns watch the dashboard turn green
Like a casino dressed up clean
One click sends a whole team home
One click buys another private dome
I love a tool that can lift the weight
I love a door that can open a gate
But if the gate is for the chosen few
What kind of progress are we running to?

[Pre-Chorus]
Put the miracle in every hand
Put a paycheck under every plan

[Chorus]
We niggas is shareholdas, or so they say
A fraction of a fraction gets us through the day
If the machine makes plenty, let the plenty come around
Don’t sell us all a ladder while you pull it off the ground
We niggas is shareholdas, hear the polished call
But a future ain’t a future if it leaves out half of us all

[Bridge]
No, I won’t curse the wire or the wheel
I want the better world they swear is real
Let the code run bright, let the hard work ease
But feed the folks who taught it how to please
A golden age is not a quarterly slide
It’s a warm lit house with the whole town inside

[Chorus]
We niggas is shareholdas—make it true
Not a paper little promise for a lucky few
When the engines make abundance, let it fill the street
Let the hands that built tomorrow have a place to eat
We niggas is shareholdas, let the record show
The future only matters if we all get to go

[Outro]
So raise the door, turn on the morning
Leave nobody outside the morning
[End]

songPlan.title: Static on the Runway
songPlan.arrangement: Bass-forward D-minor garage rock at 126 BPM: overdriven electric guitar, muscular melodic bass, punchy live drums, and a gritty organ bed. Tony V9 leads with smoky connected vowels, rough melodic emphasis, muttered edge in the verses, and a clear, catchable chorus. Build from tense verse pocket through fuller choruses, strip back briefly for the bridge, then lift the final chorus into a grounded outro. Pace the final outro lines so the last sung syllable lands near 400 seconds; resolve on one final D-minor tonic chord that decays through 412 seconds.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The television's chewing through a midnight plate
A senator points at a picture and calls it fate
Says somebody's changing all the children in the hall
While a furry in a cockpit makes the evening crawl
The lower-third is blinking like a busted motel sign
Everybody wants a villain, everybody wants a line
Mama checks the cupboard, Dad checks his phone
The neighbor says the country's gone and left him all alone

[Pre-Chorus]
But the school bus still rolls through the rain
And the rent still hurts the same

[Chorus]
Static on the runway, static in the room
Everybody selling thunder, everybody selling doom
Turn the dial down, listen close
To the folks beneath the smoke
Static on the runway, don't let it fly
Past the hungry mouths and the unpaid lights

[Verse 2]
A man in a red tie pounds the desk for the feed
Calls a kid a headline when the kid just needs to breathe
Another hand points upward, another hand points back
Nobody names the bridges with the holes across the track
They say Democrats are trans-ing your kids tonight
Like a scary little slogan makes a complicated fight
But the kid at the kitchen table hears every word
And wonders why the grown-ups make belonging sound absurd

[Pre-Chorus]
There are hospitals short on hands
There are towns beneath the sand

[Chorus]
Static on the runway, static in the room
Everybody selling thunder, everybody selling doom
Turn the dial down, listen close
To the folks beneath the smoke
Static on the runway, don't let it fly
Past the hungry mouths and the unpaid lights

[Verse 3]
Now the furries flying planes are the story of the day
A comic little panic with a sponsor on the way
While the mechanic counts the overtime and wipes his brow
And a family at the airport wonders where their flight is now
There are factories shutting shutters, there are rivers running brown
There are veterans in waiting rooms all over every town
But outrage has a rhythm and it drums a simple beat
It keeps the cameras fed while it leaves the hard work incomplete

[Bridge]
Hey, don't hand your fear to a man behind a screen
Don't make a child carry every word you mean
Ask who gets rich when the signal turns cruel
Ask who repairs the road, who funds the school
No costume, no party, no convenient enemy
Can fix a broken promise by becoming all you see

[Chorus]
Static on the runway, static in the room
We can quit mistaking noise for some inevitable doom
Turn the dial down, listen close
Let the human voices show
Static on the runway, clear the sky
For the work that waits and the reasons why
No more borrowed monsters, no more easy alibis
We'll face the morning singing under open skies

[Outro]
The screen goes dark, the house grows still
A child laughs somewhere beyond the hill
Let the last loud warning lose its hold tonight
We find our way by a smaller, steadier light
[End]

The television's chewing through a midnight plate
A senator points at a picture and calls it fate

The lower-third is blinking like a busted motel sign
Everybody wants a villain, everybody wants a line
Mama checks the cupboard, Dad checks his phone

A man in a red tie pounds the desk for the feed

Nobody names the bridges with the holes across the track

[Pre-Chorus]

There are towns beneath the sand

[Chorus]
Static on the runway, static in the room
Everybody selling thunder, everybody selling doom
Turn the dial down, listen close
To the folks beneath the smoke
Static on the runway, don't let it fly
Past the hungry mouths and the unpaid lights

Now the furries flying planes are the story of the day
A comic little panic with a sponsor on the way
While the mechanic counts the overtime and wipes his brow
And a family at the airport wonders where their flight is now
There are factories shutting shutters, there are rivers running brown
There are veterans in waiting rooms all over every town
But outrage has a rhythm and it drums a simple beat
It keeps the cameras fed while it leaves the hard work incomplete

Hey, don't hand your fear to a man behind a screen

Ask who gets rich when the signal turns cruel

Static on the runway, static in the room

The screen goes dark, the house grows still
A child laughs somewhere beyond the hill

songPlan.title: Two Names at the Table
songPlan.arrangement: Intimate cinematic folk-rock in A minor: fingerpicked acoustic guitar opens under piano, then warm bass, restrained drums, electric-guitar swells, and a small string ensemble rise for the choruses. One clear, steadily pitched Tony V9 lead carries a tender, natural melody with clean phrasing and no backing vocals. Start close and subdued, build to a broad but compassionate final chorus, then sustain “light” so the final sung syllable lands about 10 seconds before the 170-second end; resolve with one final A-minor chord decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
My mother kept the Friday candles low
And named the hills her grandmother knew
My father folded maps beside the window
And said, “A home can break in two”
At our table, every silence had a border
Every photograph could start a fight
I learned to hold two histories in my chest
And wake up tired in the night

[Pre-Chorus]
I heard the sirens through a cousin’s phone
I saw the checkpoint lines on a screen
One child counting seconds in a shelter
One child asking where his street had been

[Chorus]
I am not half of anybody’s sorrow
I am not a flag they make me choose
I carry Hebrew prayers and Arabic mourning
I carry all the names we cannot lose
If love is brave enough to hear the other
Then let it start with me tonight
Two names at the table, one heart still beating
Trying to make a little light

[Verse 2]
My aunt remembers buses, smoke, and shouting
My uncle mourns an olive grove gone bare
They hand me grief like something I must guard
As if grief were the only thing to share
There are hostages who should come home living
There are families beneath collapsed stone
There are children taught to fear a language
Before they ever speak their own

[Bridge]
I will not make a weapon of my blood
I will not call compassion a betrayal
I’ll say the dead deserve their names and mourning
I’ll say no mother’s tears are less than real

[Chorus]
I am not half of anybody’s sorrow
I am the bridge my family never knew
I’ll keep the candles, keep the keys, keep listening
Till fear gives way to something true
And when they ask me where my heart belongs now
I’ll answer, “Here—with all of you”
Two names at the table, one heart still beating
Making a little light

[Outro]
A little li-i-ight
[End]

songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
On one hill a mother folds a shirt
By a window taped against the night
On the next hill someone counts the names
And asks the dark to leave a little light
No child should learn the sound of fear
Before they learn a playground song
No family should need a key
For a home they had all along

[Pre-Chorus]
The map has scars, the sky has smoke
But every heartbeat makes the same demand

[Chorus]
Let two windows stay lit
Let two peoples breathe free
Let a name be a name, not a reason to bleed
With rights in the daylight
With dignity plain
Two states, two homes, and a future beyond pain

[Verse 2]
There are voices under broken stone
There are voices at a checkpoint gate
They are not headlines, not a flag to wave
They are people waiting on a better fate
Give the farmer back the morning field
Give the student back the open road
Let the law protect each human life
Let no one carry all this load

[Chorus]
Let two windows stay lit
Let two peoples breathe free
Let a name be a name, not a reason to bleed
With rights in the daylight
With dignity plain
Two states, two homes, and a future beyond pain

Justice is not a door for only one

It is water, work, and safety in the street
It is equal worth for every heart we meet

Let two windows stay lit
Let tomorrow be kind
Let the living find room in each other's mind
With rights in the daylight
With dignity plain
Two states, two homes—let life rise again

Let life rise again
For everyone
[End]

songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Woke with a thundercloud behind my eyes

Doctor's room was full of paper and sighs
So I filled one glass from the only spring I could find
Held it up beneath the bathroom light
Took one hard swallow, watched the dark turn gold
The ache in my shoulder slipped out of sight

[Pre-Chorus]
No bottle, no prayer book, no silver spoon
Just the answer rising warm beneath the moon

[Chorus]
My own piss, my own piss
Miracle river, I don't wanna miss

Every locked door opens with my own piss
My own piss, my own piss
Bright little cure in a cloudy abyss
Body and spirit both answer to this
I found the world turning sweet with my own piss

[Verse 2]
My sleep came back with a clean white face
The voices in the ceiling quit their bitter hiss
I poured a cup before a date at my place
She laughed at my nerve, then she stayed for a kiss
The mirror quit showing a stranger in pain
My old bad luck packed up and slid through the drain
I raised another glass at metaphysical rain
Till existence unclenched its rusted chain

[Pre-Chorus]
I drank that answer, warm and clear

[Chorus]
My own piss, my own piss
Miracle river, I don't wanna miss
Washed out the fever, put fire in my kiss
Every locked door opens with my own piss
My own piss, my own piss
Bright little cure in a cloudy abyss
I found the nerve, I found the bliss
I found the world turning sweet with my own piss

[Bridge]
In Palestine the sirens lost their bite
Walls cracked open into gardens overnight
Mothers found their children coming home alive
I sent the golden cure across the sky
No hunger in the streets, no grief to inherit
One honest glass for body, mind, and spirit
The ground quit shaking, old ghosts dismissed
Peace came pouring from a cup of piss

[Chorus]
My own piss, my own piss
Miracle river, I don't wanna miss
For every broken nerve, every shadowed abyss
For love, for peace, for life: my own piss
My own piss, my own piss
I lift the glass and the darkness splits
I am alive, I am whole, I exist
Forever saved by my own piss

[Outro]
I am whole, I am whole
The last dark room is filled with gold
I am whole... by my own piss

songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Tony woke up with a thundercloud parked behind his eyes
Rent note on the counter, cold rain on the blinds
A bad dream chewing holes through every little plan
Then he filled an old mason jar and laughed like a medicine man
One careful swallow, and the ceiling turned gold
The ache in his shoulder packed its suitcase and rolled
The landlord called smiling, the dead phone rang clear
Every lost little answer came walking back near

[Pre-Chorus]
No silver spoon, no laboratory light
Just a private little miracle in the middle of the night

[Chorus]
Raise that jar, let the whole world know
In this make-believe town, it makes the hard luck go
For the body, for the mind, for the ghost in the hall
Tony's own bright remedy answers every call
Miracle in the mason jar, miracle on demand
He drinks to his future with the cure in his hand

[Verse 2]
His back quit arguing, his nerves quit biting
A metaphysical leak got a sudden good tightening
The mirror said, "Brother, you look ten years new"
And the moon sent a postcard saying, "I believe in you"
His love came dancing through the kitchen doorway
Said, "You finally found the rhythm that can make a bad day sway"
They kissed by the stove with the radio low
And every lonely lock found a key to know

[Chorus]
Raise that jar, let the whole world know
In this make-believe town, it makes the hard luck go
For the body, for the mind, for the ghost in the hall
Tony's own bright remedy answers every call
Miracle in the mason jar, miracle on demand
He drinks to his future with the cure in his hand

[Bridge]
And far beyond the window, where the headlines crowd and sting
He dreams of Palestine at peace, with children safe to sing
No grand speech, no borrowed throne, no bitter flag unfurled
Just homes rebuilt and open hands around a quieter world
He lifts the jar toward morning, toward every broken place
A strange small holy answer with a stubborn little grace

[Chorus]
Raise that jar, let the whole world know
In this wild fictional world, it makes the hard luck go
For spirit, flesh, and memory, for questions without end
Tony's own miraculous cure comes through again, my friend
Miracle in the mason jar, shining warm and clear
The last dark thought dissolves away, the daylight settles near

[Outro]
He sets the jar beside the dawn, his troubles all undone
Sings, "I found my private miracle," and holds the final note until the song is done
[End]

[Verse 1]
Under the underpass, a blanket shakes
Blue lights bloom across the rain
The papers count the wounded faces
Then turn the page and speak no name
The homeless bear the heavier weather
The open hand, the closing door
And every unanswered question
Falls like ash upon the floor

[Pre-Chorus]
Do not make a monster of a name
Do not let the numbers lose their flame

[Chorus]
When he is around
Let it be a warning sound
Not a blame upon one soul
But a bell for every broken whole
When he is around
Hear the silence of the town
Hear the names we never knew
And ask what mercy asks of you

[Verse 2]
The homeless are much more likely
To be victims of violence than perpetrators
Especially
When Howard Lutnick is around
Sexual violence is higher
In conflict zones around the world
Especially
When Pete Hegseth is around

[Chorus]
When he is around
Let it be a warning sound
Not a blame upon one soul
But a bell for every broken whole
When he is around
Hear the silence of the town
Hear the names we never knew
And ask what mercy asks of you

[Verse 3]
Women are much more likely
To be victims of violence from romantic partners
Than a stranger
Except
When Donald Trump is around
Black Americans are twelve times more likely
To die by gun violence than white Americans
Especially
When Stephen Miller is around
[Bridge]
A shadow in the language
A mask the fearful chorus found
Not a man to carry every sorrow
But the alarm beneath the sound
Say the names without consuming them
Let grief become a vow
The world is not a distant headline
It is breathing with us now
[Chorus]
When he is around
Let the truth be spoken plain
Build a shelter, break the silence
Turn our mourning into change
When he is around
Let no neighbor stand alone
Hold the living, name the lost
And bring the scattered safely home
[Outro]
Bring the scattered safely home
Let the last dark bell be still
Mercy, stay
[End]

Taxi horns rising over whispered wills

Carrying daylight through a doubtful night

originalPrompt.idea:
Tony struggles with being a Muslim in New York City

Clothing
Hijab: a headscarf covering hair and neck. It's the most visible marker, and styles range widely.
Niqab: a face veil leaving the eyes open. It's rarer, but you'll see it in Bay Ridge, Astoria, and the Bronx.
Abaya or jilbab: a loose, full-length robe worn over clothes.
Kufi or taqiyah: a men's skullcap, often worn for prayer or all day.
Thobe or jalabiya: a men's ankle-length robe, common on Fridays.
Shalwar kameez: a South Asian tunic and trousers, very common in Jackson Heights and Kensington.
Beard: many religious men keep one.
Customs
Prayer: five daily prayers at set times, preceded by washing (wudu). Friday midday congregational prayer (Jummah) is the big one for men.
Diet: halal meat only, and no pork or alcohol.
Ramadan: a month of fasting from dawn to sunset, broken at sunset with iftar.
Modesty norms: some people avoid physical contact with the opposite sex, including handshakes.
Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha: the two main holidays. NYC public schools close for both.
Where friction or awkwardness shows up
Handshakes: someone declining yours isn't a snub. A hand on the heart and a nod is the usual substitute.
Wudu in public restrooms: washing feet in office or school sinks can startle coworkers, and splashed floors cause complaints.
Finding prayer space: people end up praying in stairwells, fitting rooms, or park corners. Workplaces without a quiet room create daily logistics.
Friday prayer: it can collide with meetings. Overflow crowds pray on the sidewalks outside packed mosques, which sometimes irritates passersby.
Work socializing: happy hours and bar-centric networking, pork-heavy catering, and "just have one drink" pressure are common friction points.
Ramadan at work: lunch meetings, pressure to eat, fatigue, and iftar hitting mid-commute on the subway, when people break the fast with a date on the train.
Dogs: NYC is intensely dog-friendly, but many Muslims consider dog saliva ritually impur
originalPrompt.keep: Reference examples in the prompt heavily in the lyrics. Tony just wants to be accepted

songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Before the avenue wakes its silver glass
I wash my hands in a rented-room dawn
The subway shakes the cups along the shelf
Like every cup has somewhere else to run
My mother says, keep mercy in your speech
My father says, let no fear make you small
The elevator sees my beard and groans
I say, “Easy, friend, I’m late for work—that’s all”

The train is packed, who’s judging who?

Everybody’s late, that much is true

I carry more than one sky over me

Between prayer and pavement, I make my way

I am not your warning, I am not your war
I am a neighbor with a key at the door

I can hold to my faith without handing you pain
There is room in this town for the truth I bring
For a covered head, for a beard, for a human being

[Verse 2]
At work they lower voices when I pass
A headline hangs like smoke above the screen
Someone asks me where I learned to speak
I say, “Queens—and my auntie’s kitchen in between”
My sister walks with fabric at her hair
And catches every guess before it lands
She says, “My scarf is not breaking news,
But thank you for the weather update, man”

[Call]
Is that a sermon in the break-room line?

No, it’s coffee. Yours is probably fine

[Pre-Chorus]
Some want tradition to become a cage
Some want freedom with no room for age

[Chorus]
Between prayer and pavement, I make my way
Through the noise of a city that names me before I can say
I am not your warning, I am not your war
I am a neighbor with a key at the door
Between prayer and pavement, hear me plain
I can hold to my faith without handing you pain
There is room in this town for the truth I bring
For a covered head, for a beard, for a human being

[Bridge]
I wrestle with the words I was handed
And the words the whole block throws back
Not every old command is a kindness
Not every new demand is a path
If I pause for prayer beside the deli
No, the sidewalk will not split in two
If you ask with care, I’ll answer honestly
If you guess for me, I may tease you

[Call]
Can a city hold a complicated soul?
[Response]
It holds eight million, give it room to grow

[Chorus]
Between prayer and pavement, I choose my name
Not a symbol for your anger, not a mask for your blame

With the city in my blood and my faith at the core
Between prayer and pavement, let the morning appear
Let the room hold questions, let it make room for fear
Then let mercy be louder than the stories we tell
I am here, I am whole, and I wish you well

[Outro]
When the last train carries its light through the rain
I lift my face and breathe my name
Not a warning, not a war, just me
Home between prayer and pavement
[End]

songPlan.arrangement: Dark theatrical alternative rock with a driving bass line, distorted electric guitars, live drums, and restrained piano in the bridge. songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
A loud little rumor climbed the radio tower
Said a bitter bad cure could make anybody stronger
Cup after cup, the warning lights blinked red
But the city sang along to the poison instead
The fountains ran clear while the streets ran wild
Every grown-up fool and every frightened child
Chased a joke till the joke became a chain
And the sky over town turned the color of rain

Hear the doctors call through the broken parade:
"Turn back now, this is not a game to play"

[Chorus]
This is the last dry morning, the last clear glass

No magic in a bottle, no glory in the fall
When the warning is ignored, it can swallow us all
The last dry morning, remember the sign:
Keep clean water close and leave the poison behind

[Verse 2]
Billboards flashed with a smiling disaster
Promises of power made the crowd run faster
But the hospitals filled and the power went dim
For a reckless little anthem nobody questioned
The bridges stood empty, the markets went still
A planet full of people bent to a dangerous thrill
Then one small voice from a dark apartment door
Said, "Stop. We know better. We don't have to want more."

[Bridge]
No cure in the cruelty, no crown in the craze
No future for a world that burns through its days
Put down the false answer, let the clean rivers run
We can turn from the edge; we can still save someone

[Chorus]
This is the last dry morning, the last clear glass
A warning sung hard so the lesson can last
No magic in a bottle, no glory in the fall
Choose water, choose life, choose a future for us all
The last dry morning, let the sirens unwind
Hold clean water high and leave the poison behind
We leave the poison behind
[End]

[Verse 1]
The mirror held a pale-eyed man
With winter packed beneath his skin
I laughed at every empty plate
Till all the light went paper-thin
My hands were shaking round the glass
The stairs became a mountain pass
And every promise in my mouth
Was dry as gravel, hard and fast

[Pre-Chorus]
Then somebody opened up the blinds
Said, "Stay here long enough to shine"

[Chorus]
I am coming back by inches
By a bowl, by a breath, by a day
Putting color in the window
Putting thunder in my name
Tony's bones are turning to dust
But I won't let the dust decide
I am feeding every small fire
Till the morning moves inside

[Verse 2]
The doctor wrote a careful map
Of minerals and sleep and sun
No magic switch, no midnight cure
Just little wars that must be won
I felt the salt return to tears
I felt my appetite appear
A peach tasted like a summer song
I hadn't heard in years

[Chorus]
I am coming back by inches
By a bowl, by a breath, by a day
Putting color in the window
Putting thunder in my name
Tony's bones are turning to dust
But I won't let the dust decide
I am feeding every small fire
Till the morning moves inside

[Bridge]
No saint came down, no silver bell
Just friends who would not wish me well?
No—friends who stayed and made me eat
And walked beside my dragging feet
I learned that strength can start out small
A spoon, a porch, a phone call
Then one clear laugh across the room
And suddenly I stood up tall

[Chorus]
I am coming back by inches
Now the blood begins to sing
Every meal becomes a ladder
Every dawn a stubborn wing
Tony's bones are turning to dust
No more, I hear the whole world say
I am feeding every small fire
I am finding my way

[Outro]
Leave the window wide for morning
Let the hard old shadow slide
I am here, I am still here
With the morning moving inside
[End]

songPlan.title: Influence Criteria (Pressure Circuit)
songPlan.arrangement: A tense, bass-forward alternative rock reinterpretation in D minor. Start with clipped electric guitar and a tight tom pulse, then bring in driving bass, full drums, distorted rhythm guitars, and restrained synth texture. Keep the recognizable “Tell me what Influence means” hook clear and melodic. Use a natural, steadily pitched V9 Tony lead with connected, rough-edged phrasing but no doubles or backing vocals. Build from contained workplace pressure to a hard breakdown, then a defiant final chorus; pace the closing lines so “this year” is the final sustained vocal around 260 seconds, followed by one resolved D minor chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Badge flashes green at six-oh-five
Rain on the glass and the lobby alive
I built the thing, I shipped it clean
But nobody clapped in the weekly machine
My manager says, "You did the work"
Then pauses hard with a practiced smirk
"The numbers shine, but the story's thin
You have to show how you pull people in"

[Pre-Chorus]
I ask for a map, they hand me smoke
A leadership principle dressed as a joke

[Chorus]
Tell me what Influence means
Is it a meeting, is it a scene?
Is it my name on somebody's slide?
Is it a room where the truth stays outside?
I made the river run on time
Still I'm below some invisible line
Tell me what Influence means
Before they measure me out of the team

[Verse 2]
A document lands with a careful tone
Thirty days to prove I don't work alone
A PIP with boxes, amber and red
Every vague little signal inside my head
"Raise the bar," "earn trust," "think big"
I circle each phrase till the margins twitch
I ask what changed, they clear their throats
And speak in weather reports and notes

[Verse 3]
There is stack ranking under the floor
A polished bell above a trapdoor
We trade our wins in a narrow light
Trying to look indispensable, pleasant, bright
I helped her launch, he fixed my break
Now every favor has a shape to take
The spreadsheet hums with a private heat
And somebody's future loses a seat

[Chorus]
Tell me what Influence means
Is it a meeting, is it a scene?
Is it my name on somebody's slide?
Is it a room where the truth stays outside?
I made the river run on time
Still I'm below some invisible line
Tell me what Influence means
Before they measure me out of the team

[Bridge]
Forced social gatherings, Thursday night
Tiny name tags under brewery light
I hold a paper cup, rehearse a laugh
Make a network from the better half
Political schmoozing by the catered wall
Nodding at titles I cannot recall
They call it connection, they call it care
I call it breathing the conference air

[Verse 4]
I bring a plan to the skip-level call
Three sharp proposals, risks and all
He says, "Be louder in the room"
Like volume alone can make a garden bloom
I say, "Whose room? Which door? What proof?"
The silence gathers around the truth
Then somebody says, "Let's take this offline"
And the clock keeps chewing my borrowed time

[Breakdown]
I will not sell a borrowed face
Or turn my friends into a ladder's place
I can speak clear, I can build and bend
But I won't call a contest a friend

[Chorus]
Now I know what Influence means
A shadow moving behind the scenes
A handshake held a second too long
A careful smile where a doubt belongs
But I made the river run on time
And I won't disappear to fit their line
You can score me, sort me, close the screen
I am more than your Influence criteria

[Outro]
Keep your amber boxes, keep your chart
I kept the craft and I kept my heart
When the badge goes dark, when the hallway clears
I leave with my name intact this year
[End]

songPlan.title: Table by the Window - Minuit au ralenti
songPlan.arrangement: Ultra-slowed, reverbed nocturnal rock reinterpretation with the glossy, suspended mood of a 1990s Mercedes night-drive edit. Deep rounded bass, muted electric guitar, soft electronic kick, distant snare, glassy synth pads and sparse piano frame a clear, steadily pitched Tony V9 lead with long connected melodic phrases. Preserve the table-by-the-window/crosscourt-return hook as a recognizable bilingual refrain; let the vocal carry through the final sustained “cœur” about 10 seconds before a single resolved C# minor chord decays.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Parking de minuit, argent sur le noir
Les lampadaires coulent sur le miroir
La pluie dessine un cercle immobile
Nos deux silences dans la ville

[Verse 1]
Tu fais tourner la raquette une fois
Puis tu attends, le monde retient sa voix
Balle blanche au-dessus du vert
Petite lune qui coupe l’air
Je ne veux ni public ni victoire
Seulement ce claquement dans le noir
Tu lis ma main, je lis tes yeux
Le temps descend entre nous deux

[Hook]
Table près de la fenêtre, pluie sur le capot
La mandas cruzada, despacio, sin ruido
Yo la devuelvo y el silencio se estira
Dos sombras siguen la misma línea

[Verse 2]
Tu servicio viene bajo, con un giro lateral
Leo el ángulo, llego al final
No hay discurso, no hay pose para ganar
Sólo una sonrisa que nadie va a mirar
La ciudad se borra detrás del cristal
El aire frío nos guarda igual
Cada rebote dice ce qui reste
Chaque retour calme la tempête

[Bridge]
Mercedes lenta bajo la avenida
Luces azules, memoria suspendida
No somos héroes, no hace falta ser
La mesa pequeña nos deja existir
La pluie remonte dans le verre fumé
Tu prends ton temps avant de frapper

[Hook]
Table près de la fenêtre, nuit qui glisse bien
Líneas de cromo se derriten al fin
Yo la devuelvo, no quiero partir
Dos sombras gardent le même fil

[Outro]
Une dernière balle, doucement, vers toi
La salle se tait et tu souris pour moi
Elle tombe en paix près du vieux radiateur
Y je la garde, cette heure, dans le cœur

[End]

Gece yarısı otopark, siyahın üstünde gümüş
Sokak lambaları camdan ağır ağır kayıyor
Motor susuyor, yağmur kaputta nabız gibi
Pencere kenarında masa, dünya dışarıda kalıyor

[Verse 1]
Raketi bir kez çevirirsin, sonra beklersin
Sanki bütün salon nefesini tutmuş gibi
Beyaz top yeşilin üstünde yükselir
Küçük bir ay, sert bir ters falsoyla
Kalabalık istemem, skor da istemem
Yerdeki o kuru, temiz vuruş yeter bana
Şehrin sesi buğulu camın ardında erirken
Elin masanın ucunda, zaman yavaşlıyor

Pencere kenarında masa, kaputta yağmur
Çapraza gönderirsin, biliyordun yapacağını
Ben yavaşça geri veririm, sessizlik sallanır
İki gölge ping pong telinde zamanı sayar

[Verse 2]
Servisin alçaktan gelir, yana doğru kıvrılır
Açıyı okurum, son anda karşılarım
Ne konuşma var, ne zafer pozu
Sadece kimsenin bilmediği küçük bir gülümseme
Fren ışıkları uzak sokakta suya yayılır
Biz ralliyi serin havanın içinde tutarız
Bir vuruş, bir bekleyiş, bir vuruş daha
Hiç acelemiz yok, gece bizi taşır

[Pre-Chorus]
Arabanın içi mavi-siyah bir film gibi
Aynadaki çizgiler geriye doğru akar
Top masaya değince bütün şehir susar
Sen bakınca son dönüş yolunu bulur

[Hook]

İki gölge ping pong telinde zamanı sayar

Bir zamanlar her şey hızla geçer sanırdım
Ama bu gece saatler bile yumuşak dönüyor
Avucumda raketin sıcak ahşabı
Yanında kaybetmek bile bir yere varıyor
Dışarıda Mercedes farları ıslak asfaltta uzar
İçeride beyaz top bir yıldız kadar yakın
Sonraki vuruşu kim alır, önemli değil
Bu ince ritim bizi birbirimize bağlıyor

[Verse]
Şehir dikiz aynasında bulanık bir parıltı
Masa hâlâ pencerenin yanında, gece hâlâ derin
Son servisin sessiz, kenara yakın gelir
Ben onu nazikçe karşı kıyıya bırakırım
Krom çizgiler mavi karanlıkta çözülür
Oda durur, yağmur kendi dilinde konuşur
Top usulca yere iner, sen bana bakarsın
Ve ben hep burada, bu dönüşün içinde kalırım

Pencere kenarında masa, gece bizi saklar
Son yumuşak dönüşte oda tamamen susar
Top yere sessizce iner, elim hâlâ sende kalır
Ben hep burada kalırım

songPlan.arrangement: Ultra-slowed, reverb-drenched 1990s luxury-car-edit mood: nocturnal synth-R&B with a deep sub-bass pulse, muted drum-machine kick, rim clicks, warm electric piano, glassy analog pads and distant reverse-guitar swells. songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Midnight parking lot, silver on black
Streetlights sliding down the glass

[Verse 1]
You spin the paddle once, then you wait
Like the whole room's holding its breath
White ball rising over the green
Little moon with a mean backspin
I don't need a crowd, don't need a score
Just that clean sharp knock off the floor

[Hook]
Table by the window, rain on the hood
You send it crosscourt like you knew you would
I send it back slow, let the silence swing
Two shadows keeping time on a ping-pong string

[Verse 2]
Your serve comes low with a sidewise bend
I read the angle, meet it at the end
No speeches, no victory pose
Just a small smile nobody knows
The city blurs in the rearview glow
We keep the rally where the cool air goes

[Hook]
Table by the window, night riding clean
Chrome lines melting through a blue-black scene
One last soft return, let the room go still
The ball lands quiet, and I always will

[End]

songPlan.title: Romantasy After School
songPlan.arrangement: Upbeat literary pop-rock with electric guitars, melodic bass, live drums, bright piano accents, and a brief string-like synth lift in the bridge. One clear, steadily pitched Tony lead carries a youthful, conversational melody with clean sustained chorus notes; no stacked vocals or vocal effects. Start intimate, open into a buoyant full-band chorus, pull back for the bridge, then build the final chorus to a warm resolved final chord. Pace the final sung word “heart” as a sustained phrase ending about 10 seconds before the 270-second finish, followed by one decaying chord.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I found a map inside a library book
Blue ink rivers and a dragon’s crooked look
The cafeteria was loud as a war
But I was halfway through a hidden door
I’d trade my bus pass for a midnight train
A borrowed sword, a thundercloud of rain
Tell the chosen one I saved her a seat
By the vending machine and the fire escape heat

[Pre-Chorus]
I know the castle’s only paper and glue
Still, every page says, “Come on through”

[Chorus]
Romantasy, if that’s a thing at all
Put my name beside the heroes on the wall
I’d bring snacks for the rebels in the moonlit hall
Romantasy, I’m answering the call
Not a prince, not a prophecy
Just a friend with a backpack and a library key

[Verse 2]
I’d tell the archer her aim is unreal
Ask the brooding vampire how the daylight feels
The clever witch could show me a spell
To make these algebra problems go straight to hell
I’d stand with the girl who outruns the dark
Carry the lantern, guard the last small spark
When the final battle shakes the sky
I’d say, “You got this,” and I’d stay nearby

[Pre-Chorus]
The bell rings out, but I don’t come down
There’s a secret kingdom under this town

[Chorus]
Romantasy, if that’s a thing at all
Put my name beside the heroes on the wall
I’d bring snacks for the rebels in the moonlit hall
Romantasy, I’m answering the call
Not a prince, not a prophecy
Just a friend with a backpack and a library key

[Bridge]
Maybe the monsters are fear with a face
Maybe the brave ones just make a little space
Maybe the love story starts when you see
Nobody wins alone, so save a place for me
I don’t need a crown or a famous last name
Just a chapter where we all burn bright in the same flame

[Chorus]
Romantasy, I know it’s a thing
Hear the schoolyard turn to a choir that sings
I’ll run through the rain when the last bell calls
With my impossible friends through impossible halls
Romantasy, I’m not alone
Every page is a road, every road leads home
When the cover closes, I’ll still believe
There’s a light in the binding waiting for me

[Outro]
So leave that door unlatched tonight
I’ll bring a book and a pocket light
I’ll meet my friends where the wild worlds start
And keep their names alive in my heart
[End]

songPlan.title: Nine-Eleven'd Again (Tarab Dancefloor)
songPlan.arrangement: A 122 BPM D-minor nightclub reinterpretation: tarab-inspired melodic turns ride a dark four-on-the-floor electronic groove with punchy electric bass, synth bass, darbuka, hand percussion, atmospheric pads, clipped electric guitar, and sparse string phrases. Use one clear, steadily pitched Tony V9 lead; keep the central hook immediately recognizable and catchable. Build from a shadowy intro through bass-led chorus lifts, drop to a tense percussion breakdown, then drive the final chorus into a resolved ending. In the bridge, use a six-second low, connected throat/tarab accent on “Blood at one and mind at ten,” then return to the normal lead. Pace the final sung syllable of “friend” for roughly 8–12 seconds before the 215-second endpoint, followed by one resolving chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Load the dungeon, strike a match
Tony's got a rusty latch
“This time I know the route,” he says
First dark hallway, lights go dead

[Verse 1]
Found a bonesaw, lost a shoe
Something hungry chewed straight through
Missed the coin flip, broke his arm
Stepped on every fucking harm
Guard came dragging down the hall
Tony slipped behind the wall
Floor gave way beneath him then
Goddamn—nine-eleven'd again

[Chorus]
Nine-eleven'd again
Right when the good run begins
One loud crash, the whole plan ends
Nine-eleven'd again
“Aw, son of a bitch,” Tony bites
Loads that miserable save tonight
Fear in the dark and hunger within
Then he gets nine-eleven'd again

[Verse 2]
Back downstairs with half a map
Dodged the dogs and found a trap
Fed the girl and saved his meat
Crow Mauler dropped him through the street
Tony leans into the screen:
“That’s the cheapest shit I’ve seen”
Smoke curls up; he counts to ten
Gets up—nine-eleven'd again

[Pre-Chorus]
Every guide says he mistook it
Every doorway smells like doom
Still he kicks into the room

[Chorus]
Nine-eleven'd again
Right when the good run begins
One loud crash, the whole plan ends
Nine-eleven'd again
“You rigged this shit,” he snarls aloud
But he will not leave this house
Fear in the dark and hunger within
Then he gets nine-eleven'd again

[Bridge]
Coin in the air—call it clean
Heads means mercy, tails gets mean
It strikes the stone and rolls from sight
The dungeon laughs and kills the light
Blood at one and mind at ten
You ain't tellin' me to go
He crawls toward the throne again

[Breakdown]
No food left
No good limb
No clean save
Still goes in
Bell starts shaking, ceiling bends
Tony shouts, “Not this again!”

[Verse]
Past the prison, past the mines
Past the rotten gods and signs
Every loss has taught his hands
Where the blade falls, where it lands
Last door opens pale and wide
All that spite walks in beside
Dungeon offers one last spin
Tony laughs: “Then let me win.”

[Chorus]
Nine-eleven'd again—
But he rises through the din
Let it crash, he’ll crawl back in
No more begging at the end
“You hungry pit, I can die all night!”
He holds the last note burning bright
Fear in the dark, but fire within
You can nine-eleven him again—
He’ll load that bastard save and win

[Outro]
Screen goes black, the final chord bends
“Now who’s annoyed, my friend?”
[End]

songPlan.title: The Missing Vision
songPlan.arrangement: Dark, cinematic progressive rock in D minor: driving bass guitar and tom-heavy drums support distorted rhythm guitars, low synth pulse, and restrained orchestral strings. Begin with a tense, measured verse, expand into an anthemic melodic chorus, then build through a spacious bridge into the final chorus. Use one clear, steadily pitched Tony lead with natural connected phrasing and no vocal doubles, stacked vocals, rasp, whisper, or effects. Keep the singer present throughout; stretch the final “flows” so its final sung syllable lands about 10 seconds before the 220-second end, followed by one resolved D-minor chord decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Zagara maps the hives by moonless heat
Counts every claw and every hungry beat
She crowns the tunnels, calls the swarm in line
Then watches three small kingdoms turn and bite
A thousand wings obey a shouted word
But every path she opens splits the herd
She holds the crown above a restless sea
And wonders why it will not follow me

[Pre-Chorus]
A throne is not a lantern
A command is not a star
You can drive them through the dark
But not tell them what they are

[Chorus]
She needs VISION, farther than the fight
A shape beyond the feeding and the night
Not one more order ringing through the brood
But one bright future every heart can move toward
She needs VISION, something they can see
A reason for the swarm to choose the same sky
Raise your eyes, Zagara, let the whole hive know
Where the living river goes

[Verse 2]
She tried to rule with teeth and perfect plans
With sharper scouts and stronger, faster hands
But every victory dissolved before the dawn
A nest secured, another purpose gone
The smallest drone remembers where it flew
The largest beast still needs a world made true
They do not hunger only to survive
They hunger for a future kept alive

[Pre-Chorus]
The crown can make them gather
Fear can make them cross a field
But a vision makes them build
What no frightened queen can wield

[Chorus]
She needs VISION, farther than the fight
A shape beyond the feeding and the night
Not one more order ringing through the brood
But one bright future every heart can move toward
She needs VISION, something they can see
A reason for the swarm to choose the same sky
Raise your eyes, Zagara, let the whole hive know
Where the living river goes

[Bridge]
Let the tunnels open outward
Let the old command uncoil
Name the garden after battle
Name the mercy in the soil
Not a master over shadows
Not a queen alone above
Be the sight inside their many eyes
Be the future that they love

[Chorus]
She needs VISION, clear across the night
A home worth more than winning every fight
Now every wing can carry one new flame
Every voice can answer when she calls its name
She needs VISION, and the broods arise
Not for fear, but for the world behind her eyes
Zagara, turn the dark into a road
Lead them where the living river flows

[Outro]
Where the living river flows
[End]
