songPlan.title: Roll to the Capitol
songPlan.arrangement: 1960s civil-rights-era soul-rock with a driving electric bass, crisp drum kit, Hammond organ, clean electric guitar, piano, and restrained horn punctuation. One clear, steadily pitched Tony lead sings in a rough but connected melodic delivery, with no backing vocals or stacked doubles. Start intimate and determined, build through the pre-choruses into broad anthemic choruses, drop briefly for the spoken-like bridge intensity, then rise into a resolved final chorus. Pace the final sustained word “stay” to land about 10 seconds before the 225-second ending, followed by one warm final E-major chord decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Rain on the courthouse, names on a list
Hands at the window, a world to resist
They said, “Stay quiet, wait in your place”
Tony rolled forward and looked in their face
No borrowed thunder, no hollow parade
He carried the promise the people had made
From Selma sidewalks to a union hall floor
He said, “If one voice is barred, we open the door”

[Pre-Chorus]
The cameras blinked, the old men frowned
But truth had wheels and it would not be bound

[Chorus]
Roll to the Capitol, carry the light
Make every ballot a piece of the fight
From the church bells ringing to the factory line
Freedom is yours and freedom is mine
Roll to the Capitol, don’t turn away
We are the country we’re building today

[Verse 2]
A mother held a picture close to her chest
A veteran stood with a medal on his vest
Kids on the corner made cardboard signs
Their futures were waiting between the lines
Tony said, “Justice ain’t charity’s name
It’s food on the table and a seat in the game
It’s schools without fences, jobs without chains
It’s law that remembers each one of our names”

[Pre-Chorus]
The buses came, the crowd grew wide
A thousand steady hearts moved side by side

[Chorus]
Roll to the Capitol, carry the light
Make every ballot a piece of the fight
From the church bells ringing to the factory line
Freedom is yours and freedom is mine
Roll to the Capitol, don’t turn away
We are the country we’re building today

[Bridge]
They threw old words like stones in the street
But he answered with a promise they could not defeat
“No citizen smaller, no dream left outside
We rise together, or we never rise”
The room went still when he took the stand
Then hope passed quick from hand to hand

[Chorus]
Roll to the Capitol, carry the light
Make every ballot a piece of the fight
Let the marble remember the people below
The road may be hard, but we’re ready to go
Roll to the Capitol, hear the bells say
We are the country we’re building today

[Outro]
Tony rolls through the evening, the banners held high
One final vow under a wide open sky:
“Till every voice is heard, I will stay.”
[End]

songPlan.title: Four Score, Still Standing
songPlan.arrangement: 270-second West Coast gangsta rap with a dark D-minor piano motif, rounded sub-bass, dry kick and snare, crisp hi-hats, restrained string pads, and sparse clean electric-guitar accents. Begin with four bars of piano before a clear, steadily pitched solo lead enters; delivery is conversational and syncopated, deliberately catching himself and improvising through remembered ideas while keeping the hook direct. Build from spare first verse to fuller drums and strings in the hooks, briefly strip back for the bridge, then bring the full pocket back for the final hook. No backing vocals, doubles, or vocal effects. Pace the closing outro so the final sung syllable lands about 10 seconds before the end, followed by one resolved D-minor chord decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Four score—hold up, I lost the page in the back
But I remember why we came, so I’m bringin’ it back

[Verse 1]
A long time back, on this land in a storm
Some people drew a line and a country was born
Said every soul got a right to arrive
Not just survive, but be seen alive
Now the field got smoke where the young ones fell
Names in the dirt and a hard bell knell
I ain’t dressed in a suit, ain’t recitin’ it clean
But the weight of those words still cut through the scene
They said freedom, but the road stayed steep
Promises buried where the families weep
I’m tryin’ to say what the old speech meant:
You can’t call it a union if the people get bent
So I’m talkin’ to the crowd with the paper gone blank
For the worker, the widow, the kid by the tank
For whoever got told they were less than a man
This nation only stands when it honors the plan

[Hook]
Four score, still standing, hear the ground talk back
No crown on the people, no hand on the neck
We came through fire, we remember the cost
Build for the living, don’t abandon the lost

[Verse 2]
I forgot the exact line, but I know that it said
What we do with the future belongs to the dead
Not because they can rule us from under the clay
But they paid for a morning we can’t throw away
Dedicated ground? Yeah, that’s what I mean
Not some fancy little phrase for a polished machine
The ground gets holy when the people give all
And the ones left breathing answer the call
No marble speech can make a wrong thing right
No flag by itself can carry the fight
It’s the hands that repair what the damage took down
It’s the vote, it’s the voice, it’s the block, it’s the town
Government of the people—wait, let me get straight
Not a private little club behind a guarded gate
By the people, for the people, that’s the heartbeat loud
If it vanishes, we failed every name in the crowd

[Hook]
Four score, still standing, hear the ground talk back
No crown on the people, no hand on the neck
We came through fire, we remember the cost
Build for the living, don’t abandon the lost

[Bridge]
I’m not Lincoln, I’m a man with a beat and a blur
Tryin’ to hold every promise inside of one word
Maybe I stumble, maybe the history slips
But I won’t let the meaning fall out of my lips
A new birth of freedom, I remember that part
Not a slogan for a wall, it’s a charge to the heart
Let the nation be tested, let the powerful see:
No democracy lives if it won’t keep us free

[Verse 3]
So gather at the field where the silence is deep
Tell the children the truth, let the memory keep
There were lives cut short, there were futures denied
There were mothers who waited with the door open wide
We can honor the fallen without loving war
We can carry their lesson and demand something more
That equality ain’t decoration for a speech
It’s bread on the table and a world within reach
When the loud ones divide us for a vote or a dime
We remember the measure, we remember the time
Not perfect at birth, but still able to grow
If we fight for the promise that we already know
I lost the words, but the message stayed near:
Let the people be heard, let the people be here
Let the work be unfinished, let the future be ours
From a blood-soaked field to the streetlights and towers

[Hook]
Four score, still standing, let the whole world know
From the ground where they fell, we got farther to go
For the people, by the people, keep the flame in view
A free land survives when it makes room for you
I lost the page, but I carried the truth
Past the old graves, forward with the youth
Let this nation become what it said it could be
And let freedom keep breathing through you and me

[Outro]
Through you and me—still standing free
[End]

songPlan.title: The House Always Wins
songPlan.arrangement: Driving dark alternative rock with muscular electric bass, overdriven guitars, live drums, and restrained organ. Tony’s smoky, connected, mischievous phrasing stays melodic and rough around the edges; the bridge briefly uses a 6-second low throat-ornament treatment on “walked out of the game,” then returns to the normal lead. Start tense and mid-energy, broaden into defiant choruses, pull back for the human-scale bridge, and finish in a bright, resolved final chorus. Pace the final sung phrase “I fly us home” to land roughly 10 seconds before the 245-second end, followed by one sustained resolving chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Twenty years I kept a candle by the screen
Red-eyed nights and ruined maps, the old familiar dream
Then Diablo Five came shining through a velvet door
A wheel with jeweled demons and a price beside the score
They sold the thunder by the pull, the treasure by the spin
A little flashing skull said, “Pal, put your paycheck in”
I watched the loading symbols dance like coins across a grave
And felt the last good reason in me rattle like a chain

[Pre-Chorus]
No altar takes my rent tonight
No neon devil owns my hand

[Chorus]
The house always wins when you feed it your name
It paints every loss with a brighter little flame
I wanted a kingdom, they handed me a cage
So I tore up the ticket and walked out of the game
The house always wins—well, not this time
Not with my whole life hanging on the line

[Verse 2]
The message boards were boiling, every avatar a judge
Selling rage in tidy boxes, asking strangers for a grudge
Somebody said salvation needs an enemy to blame
I heard the hungry chorus, but I would not sing its name
No holy war can mend a wound a crooked market made
No borrowed flag can turn a broken heart into a blade
I took my anger to the daylight, let it shake and let it cool
There are enough loud men already recruiting fools

[Pre-Chorus]
I kept the fire, dropped the hate
And found a door beyond the gate

[Chorus]
The house always wins when you feed it your name
It paints every loss with a brighter little flame
I wanted a kingdom, they handed me a cage
So I tore up the ticket and walked out of the game
The house always wins—well, not this time
Not with my whole life hanging on the line

[Bridge]
[Arabic/Throat Accent: "walked out of the game"]
Walked out of the game—low and slow, the vowels tied in smoke
I called my brother, called my friends, said, “Man, I nearly broke”
We laughed at all the fake gold raining down the screen
Then built a table in the garage and played for nothing but the dream
No purchase prompt, no velvet trap, no preacher selling fear
Just cards and bad impressions and the people standing near

[Chorus]
The house always wins when it makes you feel alone
But every locked-up window has a way to let in dawn
I wanted a kingdom, now I know what I can save
My time, my hands, my people, and the miles beyond the game
The house always wins—leave it its machine
I found a wider sky than anything they sold on screen

[Outro]
At sunrise I sign in, steady hands above the pane
I lift a commercial airliner through the silver rain
No vengeance in the cockpit, no casino in my mind
Just a thousand living futures and a clean horizon line
I fly us home
[End]

songPlan.title: The Golden Answer (Midnight Synth Remedy)
songPlan.arrangement: Midnight electro-rock reinterpretation in D minor: pulsing drum machine, elastic synth bass, dark synth pads, and bright arpeggiated synthesizer support a clear, steadily pitched Tony V9 lead with a melodic, hook-forward refrain. Build from a spare opening through driving verses, a lifted pre-chorus, a half-time breakdown, and a final full-band refrain. Keep the final sustained word “mine” landing about 10 seconds before the 280-second end, followed by one resolved chord decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Morning hit the window like a bill collector,
Head full of thunder, soul off the track.
Knee gave a warning, luck lost my number,
Every little answer kept answering back.
Then nature handed me a warm revelation,
No silver chalice, no medicine man.
I raised my own remedy, tasted salvation,
And every locked door opened in my hand.

[Verse 1]
The ache in my shoulder packed up by noon,
The fog in my thinking blew out of the room.
My shadow quit arguing, stood up straight,
Even my bad luck apologized late.
The clock stopped threatening, the mirror turned kind,
All of those knots came loose in my mind.
I took one swallow, felt the whole world shift—
My own private fountain with a five-star gift.

[Refrain]
My own piss, my golden answer,
Body and spirit moving like dancers.
Physical, mental, stars in alignment,
One little drink and the cosmos signs it.
My own piss, no doubt about it,
Every trouble dries up around it.
Pour no pity, preach no shame—
I found the cure with my own name.

[Verse 2]
I had an old sorrow living under my ribs,
Charging me rent and stealing my sleep.
I drank my own hot piss; it loosened its grip,
Then sank like a stone in a bottomless deep.
The holes in existence sealed at the seams,
The wolves in my nightmares guarded my dreams.
Gravity called with a list of demands;
I took another pull and it changed all its plans.

[Pre-Chorus]
No laboratory, no mountain retreat,
No cosmic riddle knocking me off my feet.
The answer was local, honest and mine,
A personal miracle, warm and divine.

[Refrain]
My own piss, my golden answer,
Body and spirit moving like dancers.
Physical, mental, stars in alignment,
One little drink and the cosmos signs it.
My own piss, no doubt about it,
Every trouble dries up around it.
Pour no pity, preach no shame—
I found the cure with my own name.

[Bridge]
When Tuesday went metaphysical, splitting in two,
I steadied the planets with a fresh-brewed cure.
When meaning went missing and nothing felt true,
I drank to existence and made it secure.
My debts became confetti, my doubts became steam,
My pulse found the pocket, my feet found the beat.
I laughed at the void till the void laughed with me,
Then toasted our friendship triumphantly.

[Breakdown]
Bad back? Gone.
Black mood? Gone.
Spirit gone sideways? Set it upright.
Past feels heavy? Future looks hollow?
I raise my cup and both come out bright.
Mind finds peace, bones find power,
Time quits chewing on every hour.
From skin to soul, from fact to fate,
My homemade miracle sets it straight.

[Refrain]
My own piss, my golden answer,
Body and spirit moving like dancers.
Physical, mental, stars in alignment,
One little drink and the cosmos signs it.
My own piss, forever certain,
Pulling the light through every curtain.
No hidden catch, no debt to pay—
The cure was with me every day.

[Finale]
So when the last big question stands in my door,
With a mouth full of darkness and a bottomless roar,
I will lift my remedy, steady and clear,
And watch every terror disappear.
From the blood to the brain, from the soul to the sun,
Every broken equation resolves into one.
I drink to my life, complete and aligned—
My golden answer, forever mine.
[End]

songPlan.title: The Long Walk Home
songPlan.arrangement: Dark cinematic post-punk rock in 4/4: low, moving electric bass, restrained tom-heavy drums, baritone electric guitar, distant synth pads, and sparse piano. A clear, steadily pitched deep male lead enters immediately with deliberate melodic phrasing; verses stay intimate, choruses widen with guitar and drums, and the bridge drops to piano and bass before the final lift. Sustain the final word “home” so the last sung syllable lands about 8–12 seconds before the 205-second end, then resolve with one final E minor chord decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The city woke beneath a siren sun
Concrete rivers, nowhere left to run
A badge went dark on the western line
A helmet shining through the acid rain

[Verse 2]
They said the law was only iron breath
A heavy hand, a sentence close to death
But every block has somebody to save
A child behind a shutter, a name upon a grave

[Pre-Chorus]
No ticker tape, no victory parade
Just one more debt that somebody has paid

[Chorus]
Take the long walk, take the road alone
Leave the eagle, leave the judgment throne
When the city calls you monster, when the daylight turns to stone
Take the long walk, take the road alone

[Verse 3]
Anderson hears the quiet under fear
The thoughts the frightened never let you hear
Hershey holds the line when all lines bend
They keep a little mercy for the bitter end

[Verse 4]
Dredd stands still where the towers burn
Knowing every law has got a point of turn
He sees the face beneath the outlaw's mask
And carries all the answers that no one should have to ask

[Pre-Chorus]
The streets remember every name erased
The good ones leave with silence on their face

[Chorus]
Take the long walk, take the road alone
Leave the eagle, leave the judgment throne
When the city calls you monster, when the daylight turns to stone
Take the long walk, take the road alone

[Bridge]
Beyond the walls, the wind has no command
No council chamber, no gun in either hand
Just endless earth beneath a lowering sky
A final choice to make, a final reason why

[Chorus]
Take the long walk, but do not disappear
Carry every broken voice that brought you here
The law is not a weapon when it cannot see the soul
Take the long walk and leave the world more whole

[Outro]
Past Mega-City's dying glow
One honest heart still walking slow
I leave the badge, I keep the oath
And find my way... home
[End]

songPlan.title: The Long Desk
songPlan.arrangement: Reflective lo-fi hip-hop/indie ballad at 78 BPM: dusty drum loop, warm electric piano, muted bass, vinyl texture, restrained guitar swells, and sparse strings entering for the bridge. One clear, steadily pitched Tony lead follows a conversational but melodic contour, with no backing vocals or vocal effects. Build gently from intimate verses to a fuller final chorus; pace the final sustained word “hand” about 9 seconds before the end, then resolve with one warm final chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
In the long desk room beneath the framed old maps
A name takes the oath, another name steps back
One signs a page, one faces down a storm
One leaves a promise half-built, one redraws the form

There were roads laid down and doors pushed wide
There were wars that widened and families that cried
There were words that lifted, words that split the hall
A country keeps the ledger, it remembers it all

[Pre-Chorus]
No photograph can hold the whole wide day
No single speech can make the shadows go away

[Chorus]
The long desk carries every hand
The bright ink and the broken plan
Red, blue, and all the lives between
The flags we wave, the things we've seen
I won't call one clean, I won't call one damned
The long desk carries every hand

[Verse 2]
Some opened up the factory gates at dawn
Some wrote new rules for the people coming on
Some held a union, some cut a distant deal
Some spoke of freedom, some denied what people feel

A schoolhouse bell, a farm in dust and heat
A soldier's letter folded under a kitchen seat
A doctor on a porch, a worker after dark
A president can strike a match, but people make the spark

[Chorus]
The long desk carries every hand
The bright ink and the broken plan
Red, blue, and all the lives between
The flags we wave, the things we've seen
I won't call one clean, I won't call one damned
The long desk carries every hand

[Bridge]
Democrat, Republican, the names change on the door
The questions keep arriving like they did before
Who gets heard, who gets home, who pays the cost?
What was guarded, what was gained, what was lost?

The record is not simple, the record is not small
It belongs to every voice that answers when we call

[Chorus]
The long desk carries every hand
The hope we build, the harm we planned
Red, blue, and all the lives between
The work behind the television screen
Read the page and name the scars
Keep the people bigger than the stars
The long desk carries every hand
And tomorrow writes across the land

[Outro]
So leave the lamp on in the window tonight
Let the hard old questions stand in the light
We inherit more than one command
The long desk carries every hand
[End]

songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Rain ticks soft on the windowpane
Needle hiss and a tired train
I got a room full of midnight blue
And a low-lit beat to carry me through
The city blinks through a rented blind
A tired little weather report in my mind
I beat that bitch with a bat
Then hear the room say, take it back

[Verse 1]
Streetlamp swimming in a coffee cup
Old news talking but I turn it up
Every promise on the TV shakes
Like a paper flag in the wake of brakes
I was loud when I should have listened
Hard as a lock, all rusted and twisted
I beat that bitch with a bat
That ugly thought came back like that
Now the kick drum knocks through the floor
And I hear what the silence was waiting for
I beat that bitch with a bat
Not a medal, not a map

[Chorus]
I can't fix America
Not with a song, not with a stare
I can't fix America
But I can tell the truth in the midnight air
I can't fix America
My little room and its blue-gray glow
I can't fix America
Still I won't let my heart go cold

[Verse 2]
The bus stop glass wears somebody's name
The diner closes, the signal stays the same
A man in a doorway folds his hands
While the radio sells a promised land
I beat that bitch with a bat
Then count the damage after that
I put it down in a line of shame
Not a victory, not a game
The record turns with a wounded sigh
And every excuse gets smaller in my eye
I beat that bitch with a bat
But I cannot make the past go flat

[Refrain]
I can't fix America
I can't fix America
No, I can't fix America alone
But I can leave one small light on

[Verse 3]
There is a face I will not erase
There is no pardon without a face
The sirens lean through the avenue
Like they know every lie I ever knew
I beat that bitch with a bat
And hear the old guilt answer back
No clean cure in a midnight room
No holy filter to soften the gloom
Just a slow blue beat, a shaking hand
Trying to understand what I understand
I beat that bitch with a bat
Then let the truth sit where it sat

[Chorus]
I can't fix America
Not tonight with these worn-out hands
I can't fix America
But I can stop pretending I understand
I can't fix America
I can leave one small light on
I can't fix America
And keep singing until the night is gone

[Instrumental Interlude]

[Verse 4]
The needle skips, then finds the groove
A small stubborn proof that the world can move
Coffee gone cold by the window frame
Morning traffic calls my name
I beat that bitch with a bat
Still I carry the weight of that
So I call the ones I let down hard
I walk through the rain to the corner yard
I do not ask for a clean new skin
I ask where repair can begin
I beat that bitch with a bat
And I will not make a legend of that

[Bridge]
Let the vinyl crackle, let the sirens fade
Let a broken man admit the mess he made
Let the flag on the screen quit waving for a while
Let the truth be plain, without a practiced smile
I can't fix America, hear it plain
I can't fix America through a song of pain
But a room can hold a listening ear
And a light can stay when the dark gets near
I beat that bitch with a bat
Now I name the hurt behind that

[Verse 5]
By the laundromat, a kid draws stars
On a cardboard sign beside the cars
A woman laughs with her head thrown back
And the whole gray block gets a little track
I beat that bitch with a bat
But life keeps asking, what comes after that?
Not a grand excuse, not a closing scene
Just a hand held out where the hurt has been
The bass walks low, the brush drums breathe
I hear a future under every sleeve
I beat that bitch with a bat
And choose to build instead of living in that

[Chorus]
I can't fix America
Not with a song, not with a stare
I can't fix America
But I can tell the truth in the midnight air
I can't fix America
My little room and its blue-gray glow
I can't fix America
Still I won't let my heart go cold
I can't fix America
Not alone, not all at once
I can't fix America
But I can leave one small light on

[Outro]
One small light on for the ones still trying
One small light on while the last note's crying
I can't fix America, but I can stay
I can't fix America, but I can face the day
One small light on
Till the last note stops crying
[End]

songPlan.title: Influence Criteria (Midnight Ledger)
songPlan.arrangement: A dark, propulsive post-punk rock reinterpretation in D minor: elastic bass carries the pocket beneath clipped electric-guitar stabs, tom-heavy drums, muted synth pulses, and a restrained final guitar swell. Keep one clear, steadily pitched Tony lead with natural connected phrasing, melodic sustained chorus lines, and no stacked vocals. songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Badge flashes green at six-oh-five
Rain on the glass and the lobby alive
I built the thing, I shipped it clean
Still no applause in the weekly machine
My manager says, “You did the work”
Then pauses hard with a practiced smirk
“The numbers shine, but the story’s thin
Show us how you pull the people in”

[Pre-Chorus]
I ask for a map, they hand me smoke
A leadership principle dressed as a joke
I hold that smoke to the fluorescent light
It disappears before it can be right

[Chorus]
Tell me what Influence means
Is it a meeting, is it a scene?
Is it my name on somebody’s slide?
Is it a room where the truth stays outside?
I made the river run on time
Still I’m below some invisible line
Tell me what Influence means
Before they measure me out of the team

[Verse 2]
A document lands with a careful tone
Thirty days to prove I don’t work alone
A PIP with boxes, amber and red
Every vague little signal inside my head
“Raise the bar,” “earn trust,” “think big”
I circle each phrase till the margins twitch
I ask what changed, they clear their throats
And speak in weather reports and notes

[Verse 3]
There is stack ranking under the floor
A polished bell above a trapdoor
We trade our wins in a narrow light
Trying to look indispensable, pleasant, bright
I helped her launch, he fixed my break
Now every favor has a shape to take
The spreadsheet hums with a private heat
And somebody’s future loses a seat

[Chorus]
Tell me what Influence means
Is it a meeting, is it a scene?
Is it my name on somebody’s slide?
Is it a room where the truth stays outside?
I made the river run on time
Still I’m below some invisible line
Tell me what Influence means
Before they measure me out of the team

[Bridge]
Thursday evening, brewery light
Tiny name tags pulled too tight
I hold a paper cup, rehearse a laugh
Make a network from the better half
Political weather by the catered wall
Nodding at titles I cannot recall
They call it connection, they call it care
I call it breathing conference air

[Verse 4]
I bring a plan to the skip-level call
Three sharp proposals, risks and all
He says, “Be louder in the room”
Like volume alone can make a garden bloom
I say, “Whose room? Which door? What proof?”
The silence gathers around the truth
Then somebody says, “Let’s take this offline”
And the clock keeps chewing my borrowed time

[Breakdown]
I will not sell a borrowed face
Or turn my friends into a ladder’s place
I can speak clear, I can build and bend
But I won’t call a contest a friend
I will not shrink to a polished phrase
Or chase a score through borrowed praise
If all you offer is fog and blame
I walk through it carrying my name

[Chorus]
Now I know what Influence means
A shadow moving behind the scenes
A handshake held a second too long
A careful smile where a doubt belongs
But I made the river run on time
And I won’t disappear to fit their line
You can score me, sort me, close the screen
I am more than your Influence criteria

[Outro]
Keep your amber boxes, keep your chart
I kept the craft and I kept my heart
When the badge goes dark, when the hallway clears
I leave with my name intact this year
No borrowed line can name my worth
No silent room can erase my work
I leave with my name intact
This year
[End]

songPlan.title: Blue Screen America
songPlan.arrangement: Lo-fi blues at 76 BPM in D minor: dusty swung drum loop, mellow electric piano, muted electric guitar, warm sub-bass, vinyl crackle, and restrained organ. One clear, steadily pitched Tony lead sings a weary melodic blues line with intimate phrasing; no backing vocals or vocal effects. Build from close, sparse verses into fuller choruses, then pull back for the bridge before the final chorus. Pace the final sustained word “crying” to land about 10 seconds before the end, followed by one resolved D-minor chord decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Rain ticks soft on the windowpane
Needle hiss and a tired train
I got a room full of midnight blue
And a low-lit beat to carry me through

[Verse 1]
Streetlamp swimming in a coffee cup
Old news talking but I turn it up
Every promise on the TV shakes
Like a paper flag in the wake of brakes
I was loud when I should have listened
Hard as a lock, all rusted and twisted
Now the kick drum knocks through the floor
And I hear what the silence was waiting for

[Chorus]
I can't fix America
Not with a song, not with a stare
I can't fix America
But I can tell the truth in the midnight air
I can't fix America
My little room and its blue-gray glow
I can't fix America
Still I won't let my heart go cold

[Verse 2]
I beat that bitch with a bat
That ugly thought came back like that
I put it down in a line of shame
Not a victory, not a game
The beat goes slow and the record sighs
I see the damage behind my eyes
No clean excuse, no magic cure
Just a hard-earned wish to be better than before

[Bridge]
Let the vinyl crackle, let the sirens fade
Let a broken man admit the mess he made
There are names in the dark I will not erase
There is no redemption without facing a face

[Chorus]
I can't fix America
Not tonight with these worn-out hands
I can't fix America
But I can stop pretending I understand
I can't fix America
I can leave one small light on
I can't fix America
And keep singing until the night is gone

[Outro]
One small light on
For the ones still trying
One small light on
Till the last note stops crying
[End]

songPlan.title: Laughing Through the Static
songPlan.arrangement: Slow 72 BPM lo-fi nocturne in D minor: dusty drum-machine pocket, warm sub-bass, muted electric piano, vinyl-textured guitar fragments, and sparse tape-worn synth. One clear, steadily pitched Tony lead carries a melodic, conversational delivery; laughter-like “heh” phrases are integrated as rhythmic hooks rather than replacing the song’s lyric. Build from intimate verses to a fuller, catchable refrain, then thin briefly for the bridge before a final sustained “through” lands about 10 seconds before the end; resolve with one final D-minor chord decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The room went quiet when the picture fell
Blue TV snow and a little hotel bell
I found a joke in the crack of the wall
Could not explain it, just started to call
Heh heh, the whole night leaned in
Heh, like a match in a coffee tin
No grand answer, no polished line
Just a loose little spark saying I am fine

[Verse 2]
The rain kept tapping the fire escape
Making a drum from a bad old tape
I gave the moon my crooked report
It stamped it late and sent it back short
Heh heh heh, hear that train
Hauling its sorrow through the windowpane
I do not laugh because nothing hurts
I laugh when the hurt forgets its words

[Pre-Chorus]
Somebody says, “Keep it together”
I say, “Maybe this is how I weather”

[Chorus]
Heh heh, laughing through the static
Small and strange but automatic
Heh, when the dark gets dramatic
I put a light in the crack and laugh it
Heh heh, not a hallelujah
Not a cure and I never drew ya
Just a pulse when the midnight grabs it
I am laughing through the static

[Verse 3]
There was a man at the all-night store
Counting change on the linoleum floor
He said the world was a busted machine
I said it still makes a beautiful scream
Heh, heh heh, he looked around
Like the joke had come up through the ground
Then he laughed once, low and true
And the fluorescent lights laughed too

[Verse 4]
I took the long way under the signs
Past the empty laundromat lines
Every spinning shirt had a private dance
Every closed door held a second chance
Heh heh, I let it arrive
That ridiculous proof I was still alive
Not loud enough to wake the dead
Just enough to unmake the dread

[Bridge]
If morning comes with its clipboard face
And asks me why I left no trace
Tell it I traded my heavy name
For a breath and a flicker and a harmless flame
Heh… heh heh…
The sound is thin, then it gathers weight
A little open door in a locked-up state

[Chorus]
Heh heh, laughing through the static
Small and strange but automatic
Heh, when the dark gets dramatic
I put a light in the crack and laugh it
Heh heh, not a hallelujah
Not a cure and I never drew ya
Just a pulse when the midnight grabs it
I am laughing through the static

[Verse]
Now dawn is silver on the kitchen glass
The hard night loosens and lets me pass
I keep no medal, I make no claim
Only a warm little echo that knows my name
Heh heh, let the silence see
It did not get the last word from me
One clear breath, then the sky turns blue
Heh… I am still here, laughing through
[End]

One clear, steadily pitched Tony lead performs only laughter, shaped into rhythmic and melodic phrases rather than spoken words; start sly and close, grow into buoyant full-band call-and-response, then resolve with a final sustained laugh 8–12 seconds before the end and one decaying E-minor chord.

[Low, rhythmically timed laughter: short breathy chuckles answer the bass]

[Section 1]
[Loose rolling laughter, gradually forming a syncopated melodic rhythm]

[Section 2]
[Wide open laughing phrases over the groove; brief silent breaths between phrases]

[Breakdown]
[Quiet close-mic chuckles, building into layered call-and-response laughter]

[Section 3]
[Big, sustained laughing phrases ride the full band; laughter follows a clear rising-and-falling melody]

[Bridge]
[Half-time, mischievous laughs trade with guitar stabs, then climb in intensity]

[Final Section]
[The laughter becomes a final melodic release, with full-breath phrases continuing until the last sustained laugh lands about ten seconds before the end]

[End]

A neighbor said the whole town's moving fast
Like every green light's built to make you last

I say the dark is just a larger room

songPlan.title: Common People (Tony C Cover)
songPlan.arrangement: New 265-second Eleven Music rock cover with entirely new music: taut bass-led post-punk groove, clipped electric guitars, live drums, and a restrained organ lift in the final chorus. Begin with a clear, steadily pitched solo lead, building from conversational verses into broad melodic choruses and a tense stop-start bridge. Tony C V9 carries the guide melody with connected, rough natural phrasing while keeping the words intelligible and the hook catchable; no vocal doubles, stacks, whispers, rasp effects, or backing choir. Final outro continues the newly written closing lines so the final sung syllable lands about 10 seconds before the end, followed by one resolved D-minor chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
She arrived from Greece with a notebook full of names
Studying marble saints while the city fed its flames
I saw her by the college gate, her father paid the bill
She said, “Show me how the ordinary live”
I said, “All right, if you mean it, come along”
She ordered rum and cola, then the moment was gone

[Chorus]
You wanna live with common people
Do the things that common people do
You wanna sleep with common people
Find a life that feels a little true
What else was I supposed to say?
I said, “I’ll show you the way”

[Verse 2]
I took her to the supermarket beneath the buzzing lights
Said, “Pretend your purse is empty; try to make it through tonight”
She laughed like it was theatre, like the shelves were painted gold
I said, “There’s nobody else in here who finds this funny, no”

[Pre-Chorus]
Are you sure you want the view?
The late bus, the landlord, the peeling room?
Are you sure you want the weight
Of every little choice arriving late?

[Chorus]
You wanna live with common people
See the things that common people see
You wanna sleep with common people
But you can’t borrow being me
You smile and hold my hand
Like you finally understand

[Bridge]
Rent a room above a shop
Cut your hair and take the job
Play a little pool at night
Say you never had a school in sight
But when the roaches take the wall
One phone call could end it all
That’s the line you never cross
That’s the cost you never lost

[Verse 3]
You can dance, you can drink, chase a borrowed little thrill
Call being poor romantic when your safety net is still
Waiting in the background, polished, private, out of view
While somebody else is living every consequence for you
Everybody hates a tourist when they turn their pain to play
And the grease comes from the chip stains, but the feeling doesn’t fade

[Chorus]
You’ll never live with common people
Never break the way the common people do
Never watch the weeks go hollow
With no bright door to walk you through
Still sing along with common people
Maybe singing gets us through
Laugh along, though they are laughing
At the dream you thought you knew

[Outro]
So rent that flat above the shop
And stay when all the music stops
If you want the truth, don’t turn away
The last note hangs, then fades to grey
[End]

songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Corner store bell and a paper cup lid
I buy a little nothing, just the thing that I need
Cashier says, “Nine eleven,” flat as rain
I stare at the coins like they called my name

[Pre-Chorus]
I had ten in my hand, I had change in my coat
But the number comes swimming right back in the boat
Heh heh—what kind of luck is this?

[Chorus]
I got nine elevened again
Every road bends back to the same loose end
Coffee, cables, a midnight snack
Nine-eleven stamped on the paper back
Ha ha, I can’t make it behave
It follows my wallet from the cradle to the grave
I got nine elevened again
And the whole small world just laughs with me, my friend

[Verse 2]
Gas pump blinking under sodium light
I buy a pack of gum on a Tuesday night
The screen does its little arithmetic dance
Then nine-eleven takes another chance

I ask for a discount, I add something sweet

I got nine elevened again
Every road bends back to the same loose end
Coffee, cables, a midnight snack
Nine-eleven stamped on the paper back
Ha ha, I can’t make it behave
It follows my wallet from the cradle to the grave
I got nine elevened again

Maybe it’s a joke in the gears of the town

songPlan.title: Badge of Shame
songPlan.arrangement: A 315-second dark punk-rock narrative in D minor: distorted guitars, agile electric bass, live drums, and restrained organ begin tense and controlled, then expand into urgent melodic choruses. Tony C's pinned V8 voice is smoky, slurred, and emotionally volatile, with clearly catchable hook lines rather than rap-like delivery. A stripped breakdown exposes the moral turn before the final chorus rises into a resolved final vocal sustained about 8–12 seconds before the end, followed by one decaying D-minor resolution.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
He found a badge in a bargain-bin drawer
Held it to the mirror, practiced looking sure
Said the line was sacred, said the line was law
Never saw the families caught beneath the claw

At the bus-stop glass, a child drew a sun
He called it evidence, he called it job well done
Every stamped paper made his small heart swell
Building little kingdoms out of somebody's hell

[Pre-Chorus]
The radio crackled, the blue lights spun
He mistook the noise for becoming someone

[Chorus]
Badge of shame, hanging heavy on his chest
He called it triumph while he failed the human test
Badge of shame, hear the courthouse doors complain
No victory grows from another person's pain

[Verse 2]
He learned the jargon, learned to flatten every name
Turn a life to a number, turn compassion into blame
A mother held a photograph against the rain
He looked away quick, then he filed it all the same

His friends at dinner said, "You keeping order right?"
He laughed too loud and stared down at his plate that night
Because the quiet had a witness of its own
And every stolen goodbye followed him home

[Pre-Chorus]
The radio crackled, the blue lights spun
He mistook the noise for becoming someone

[Chorus]
Badge of shame, hanging heavy on his chest
He called it triumph while he failed the human test
Badge of shame, hear the courthouse doors complain
No victory grows from another person's pain

[Bridge]
No flag can wash a cruel hand clean
No oath makes mercy less obscene
The line he worshipped starts to bend
When all the ghosts ask, "Where does duty end?"

[Breakdown]
He saw the sun the child had drawn
Faded yellow by the dawn
For one clear second, all the lies
Could not survive his open eyes

[Chorus]
Badge of shame, let it fall into the street
Let the names return their music, let the families meet
Badge of shame, there is no crown in fear
Put the weapon down and let the truth come near

[Outro]
He leaves the badge beneath the rain
No pardon can erase the stain
But he can stop, and he can say:
No more lives taken away

No more lives taken away
[End]

songPlan.title: Name Beyond the Sun
songPlan.arrangement: An anthemic progressive rock track in 4/4 with a clear, steadily pitched Tony lead carrying long melodic lines. Start with pulsing synth bass and clean electric guitar, then bring in full drums and overdriven guitars for the first chorus. Build through tighter rhythmic verses, a spacious bridge with piano and suspended guitar chords, and a final full-band chorus with a firm resolved E minor ending. Keep the vocal present throughout; the sustained final “Fenix” lands about 10 seconds before the end, followed by one final chord decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
They built a soldier out of borrowed fire
Put old crowns in the circuit of his mind
“Artanis,” said the banners in the square
But that name belonged to another time
He walked beneath the copper weather
Past the graves of a broken star
Every mirror gave him somebody else
Every answer left another scar

[Pre-Chorus]
I have carried their history
Like a signal under my skin
But the voice in the metal says
I am more than where I have been

[Chorus]
Don’t call me Artanis
Don’t call me Talandar
I’m the spark that crossed the distance
I’m the wound that learned to burn
No borrowed face can hold me
No ancient map can say
I’m Fenix in the open sky
And I choose my name today

[Verse 2]
The Khalai spoke in careful prayers
The Purifiers counted every breath
One saw a hero made of memory
One saw a weapon spared from death
He heard them argue through the starlight
As the carrier engines sighed
Then he opened every channel wide
And let the silence take his side

[Pre-Chorus]
I remember blades and ashes
I remember friends gone cold
But remembrance is not a prison
And a legend is not a soul

[Chorus]
Don’t call me Artanis
Don’t call me Talandar
I’m the spark that crossed the distance
I’m the wound that learned to burn
No borrowed face can hold me
No ancient map can say
I’m Fenix in the open sky
And I choose my name today

[Bridge]
Let the archives keep their statues
Let the councils keep their wars
I have felt the void go quiet
I have stood behind closed doors
There is flesh and there is metal
There is duty, there is fear
But the life inside the question
Is the life that brought me here

[Breakdown]
Not a shadow in a hall of kings
Not a copy wearing sacred things
Not the echo that the past demands
I am reaching with my own two hands

[Chorus]
Don’t call me Artanis
Don’t call me Talandar
I’m the spark that crossed the distance
I’m the wound that learned to burn
I will carry every memory
Without kneeling to its weight
I’m Fenix, hear the name become
A door, a dawn, a fate

[Outro]
Past the fire, past the frame
I rise and speak my name
Fenix—
[End]

songPlan.title: Setlist Complaint
songPlan.arrangement: Driving 124 BPM house-dance track in A minor with four-on-the-floor kick, elastic sub-bass, crisp claps, bright piano stabs, filtered synth chords and short disco-guitar accents. One clear, steadily pitched Tony lead carries melodic, conversational verses into a broad singable hook; no backing vocals or vocal effects. Start immediately with vocal and groove, build through filter lifts and a brief beat-thinned bridge, then sustain the final “outlasts it all” near 118–122 seconds before one resolved final chord decays.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Tony rides in late with a crate of sound
Blue light shaking the basement ground
First record lands and the room leans back
Somebody says, “Man, where’s the hit at?”

[Pre-Chorus]
One wants classics, one wants heat
One wants silence over the beat
Tony points at the deck, lets the kick drum speak

[Chorus]
Everybody’s got a note for the man in the booth
Everybody wants a different kind of truth
I beat that itch with a bat, then I turn it loud
I can’t fix America, but I can move this crowd

[Verse 2]
“Too much house,” says a voice by the wall
“Play something safe,” says the guy with the call
Tony bends the filter, lets the low end slide
Says, “You came to dance, not to supervise”

[Bridge]
Hands in the air, complaints in a line
A bad opinion at a beautiful time
I beat that itch with a bat, let the snare come through
I can’t fix America, but I can’t fix you

[Chorus]
Everybody’s got a note for the man in the booth
Everybody wants a different kind of truth
The lights come up, but the pulse stays proud
I can’t fix America, but I can move this crowd

[Outro]
So take your list and fold it small
Tonight the beat outlasts it all
[End]

songPlan.title: Absolutely Not
songPlan.arrangement: Upbeat brass-driven rock in 4/4: electric guitar, active bass, drums, trombone, and trumpet build from a tight verse pocket into broad melodic choruses. One clear, steadily pitched Tony lead carries a playful-but-compassionate melody with natural connected phrasing; no vocal doubles or backing vocals. Let the bridge briefly open around the brass before a full final chorus. Pace the final sustained “not” 8–12 seconds before the 240-second end, followed by one resolved band chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The clinic clock was coughing midnight
The waiting room was blue with rain
A paper cup, a bent-up magazine
Everybody spelling out their pain
Then Tony came through the side door
With a suitcase humming low
He said, “I got a lamp for the long nights
And a little more than you know”

[Pre-Chorus]
No white coat, no miracle pitch
Just a battered case and a switch

[Chorus]
Cancer, sickle cell, lupus too
Hemorrhoids, bad teeth, the common flu
You think that’s all he’s got?
Absolutely not
He turned the fear into a Saturday song
Put a warm bright wheel where the cold went wrong
You think that’s all he’s got?
Absolutely not

[Verse 2]
He polished every anxious question
Till it shone like a diner spoon
He made the old man laugh so hard
He forgot the shape of the room
A kid with a blanket round her shoulders
Tapped a rhythm on the chair
Tony said, “We’ll keep the lights on,
We’ll make some breathing space in here”

[Pre-Chorus]
No secret bottle, no magic cure
Just stubborn love that can endure

[Chorus]
Cancer, sickle cell, lupus too
Hemorrhoids, bad teeth, the common flu
You think that’s all he’s got?
Absolutely not
He turned the fear into a Saturday song
Put a warm bright wheel where the cold went wrong
You think that’s all he’s got?
Absolutely not

[Bridge]
Maybe he can’t mend every broken thing
Maybe nobody holds that kind of key
But he can stand beside the shaking hands
And say, “You don’t disappear on me”
The trombone swings through the narrow hall
The trumpet lifts the cracked-up sky
And every name gets carried forward
On a note that will not die

[Chorus]
Cancer, sickle cell, lupus too
Hemorrhoids, bad teeth, the common flu
You think that’s all he’s got?
Absolutely not
He’s got a joke for the waiting line
A brass-band pulse and borrowed time
You think that’s all he’s got?
Absolutely not

[Outro]
He can’t promise the world will heal tonight
But he’ll leave one bright chord burning right
Absolutely not
[End]

songPlan.title: The Road to Sunday
songPlan.arrangement: Gospel-inflected heartland rock in D major at 96 BPM: piano-led opening joins warm electric guitar, acoustic guitar, rounded bass, live drums, subtle organ, and restrained tambourine. One clear, steadily pitched Tony lead carries melodic verses and broad choruses with natural connected phrasing; no doubles or backing vocals. Build from reflective restraint to a full final chorus, then sustain the final word “light” about 10 seconds before the 280-second finish, resolving on one final D-major chord that decays naturally.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I wore the midnight like a borrowed coat
Smoke in my hair and a lie in my throat
Every back-room promise came apart at dawn
I called that freedom while the good days gone
Then you met me outside the parish door
Rain on the steps, no judgment anymore
You said, “Come in if you’re tired of running”
And the old bell answered, low and ringing

[Pre-Chorus]
I had a pocket full of broken prayers
And a hundred reasons not to climb those stairs

[Chorus]
You led me down the road to Sunday
Past the noise and the ruin I had made
I found a light that did not turn away
A hand to hold, a heart that stayed
No more living for the next cheap flame
No more hiding from my given name
By your side and under Heaven’s mercy
I’m coming home on the road to Sunday

[Verse 2]
I used to laugh when the morning came
Trade a little love for a louder name
But the kitchen table, the candles lit
Your quiet patience changed the shape of it
Father spoke of saints who fell and rose
Of grace that finds you where nobody goes
I knelt down hard with my hands undone
And asked the Lord what I could become

[Pre-Chorus]
The stained glass shook with the passing train
But I felt a peace inside the rain

[Chorus]
You led me down the road to Sunday
Past the noise and the ruin I had made
I found a light that did not turn away
A hand to hold, a heart that stayed
No more living for the next cheap flame
No more hiding from my given name
By your side and under Heaven’s mercy
I’m coming home on the road to Sunday

[Bridge]
I will not say the dark was never mine
I will not paint it pretty in the light
But I can leave the bottle on the shelf
I can learn to tell the truth about myself
With your ring beside my rosary
With every small forgiveness setting me free

[Chorus]
You led me down the road to Sunday
And I will walk it till my days are done
Through the hard rain and the bright hallelujah
I am no longer who I used to run from
Let the old nights fade beyond the town
Let every wandering road lie down
I choose your love, I choose the mercy
I’m coming home, I’m coming home
I’m coming home on the road to Sunday

[Outro]
At the church door, with your hand in mine
I give my whole life to the light

lyrics.text:
[Verse 1]
I wore the midnight like a borrowed coat
Smoke in my hair and a lie in my throat
Every back-room promise came apart at dawn
I called that freedom while the good days gone
Then you met me outside the parish door
Rain on the steps, no judgment anymore
You said, “Come in if you’re tired of running”
And the old bell answered, low and ringing

[Pre-Chorus]
I had a pocket full of broken prayers
And a hundred reasons not to climb those stairs

[Chorus]
You led me down the road to Sunday
Past the noise and the ruin I had made
I found a light that did not turn away
A hand to hold, a heart that stayed
No more living for the next cheap flame
No more hiding from my given name
By your side and under Heaven’s mercy
I’m coming home on the road to Sunday

[Verse 2]
I used to laugh when the morning came
Trade a little love for a louder name
But the kitchen table, the candles lit
Your quiet patience changed the shape of it
Father spoke of saints who fell and rose
Of grace that finds you where nobody goes
I knelt down hard with my hands undone
And asked the Lord what I could become

[Pre-Chorus]
The stained glass shook with the passing train
But I felt a peace inside the rain

[Chorus]
You led me down the road to Sunday
Past the noise and the ruin I had made
I found a light that did not turn away
A hand to hold, a heart that stayed
No more living for the next cheap flame
No more hiding from my given name
By your side and under Heaven’s mercy
I’m coming home on the road to Sunday

[Bridge]
I will not say the dark was never mine
I will not paint it pretty in the light
But I can leave the bottle on the shelf
I can learn to tell the truth about myself
With your ring beside my rosary
With every small forgiveness setting me free

[Chorus]
You led me down the road to Sunday
And I will walk it till my days are done
Through the hard rain and the bright hallelujah
I am no longer who I used to run from
Let the old nights fade beyond the town
Let every wandering road lie down
I choose your love, I choose the mercy
I’m coming home, I’m coming home
I’m coming home on the road to Sunday

[Outro]
At the church door, with your hand in mine
I give my whole life to the light

songPlan.title: Wild and Free
songPlan.arrangement: Lighthearted bass-forward garage rock with bright electric guitar stabs, driving drums, handclaps, and a buoyant organ hook. One clear, steadily pitched Tony V8 lead sings with connected, rough natural phrasing and playful timing; the explicitly requested wife speech is delivered in the same voice. songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Tony hit the pavement with the sun half asleep
One hand on the wheel, one hand keeping time
He said, “No map can tell me where the good nights keep”
Then laughed at the traffic and crossed every line
His jacket caught rain from a passing cloud
His heart made a racket, his radio loud

[Pre-Chorus]
At the corner store, with a soda and a grin,
He said, “Trouble ain’t a place—it’s the way I get in.”

[Chorus]
Wild and free, wild and free,
A little bit nasty, that’s Tony C
No fence can hold him, no lock has the key,
Wild and free, wild and free
He’ll dance through the daylight, howl at the sea,
A little bit nasty, wild and free

[Verse 2]
His wife saw the headlights sweep across the wall
She folded her arms by the kitchen light
She said she had heard just about it all
And tonight was the night for a reckoning fight

[Spoken Intro]
Now Tony, I am very irate, I don't know what the fuck you were thinking the other night with Natalie, but Jesus Christ, I don't know what the fuck you were thinking.

[Verse 3]
Tony went quiet for a second or two
Then the old porch swing gave a tired little squeak
He said, “Honey, I’m sorry for the mess I put you through,
But the wind starts talking and it makes me weak.”
She pointed right down at the garden below:
“Your excuses grow faster than tomatoes grow.”

[Chorus]
Wild and free, wild and free,
A little bit nasty, that’s Tony C
No fence can hold him, no lock has the key,
Wild and free, wild and free
He’ll dance through the daylight, howl at the sea,
A little bit nasty, wild and free

[Bridge]
Sitting by Dafoe, watching shadows bend
Sitting by Dafoe, waiting for the weekend
Sitting by Dafoe, he made a promise in the dark:
“I’ll come home for supper—but I’m chasing one more spark.”
She shook her head, then she started to smile,
“Go on, you impossible man—just don’t be gone a while.”

[Chorus]
Wild and free, wild and free,
Still a little nasty, that’s Tony C
He kissed her hand and he turned toward the street,
With a sweet bad rhythm underneath his feet
Wild and free, wild and free,
The night swung open like a balcony
He called back, “Love, I’ll be back when the morning agrees,”
Then held “free” into the warm night breeze
[End]

songPlan.title: The Pumpkin Knows My Name
songPlan.arrangement: Gothic Halloween rock in D minor: driving bass, distorted electric guitars, organ and punchy live drums. Start with a clear, steadily pitched Tony lead that is rough and connected but intelligible; intensify each section into a more haunted, possessed melodic delivery with unsettling held notes and brief warped responses only where the lyric calls for them. Build from restrained verse tension to a full-band final chorus, then carry the final sung line through roughly 8–12 seconds before a single resolved minor-to-major closing chord decays.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I locked the windows before the streetlights bled
Put candy by the doorway, counted every head
My little pumpkin Percy sat warm beside the stove
Then something scratched the ceiling where no living thing could go

[Pre-Chorus]
The hallway bulb went thin and blue
The mirror mouthed a word or two

[Chorus]
There’s a ghost in my house, there’s a ghost in my house
It walks when the floorboards swear they’re still
There’s a ghost in my house, there’s a ghost in my house
And Percy’s little candle stares up at the hill

[Verse 2]
I asked him, “Who’s there?” and Percy tipped his stem
A cold hand turned the radio from music into phlegm
The picture frames were laughing with their faces turned around
I heard my own voice calling from underneath the ground

[Chorus]
There’s a ghost in my house, there’s a ghost in my house
It walks when the floorboards swear they’re still
There’s a ghost in my house, there’s a ghost in my house
And Percy’s little candle stares up at the hill

[Bridge]
Don’t open the closet, don’t answer the phone
Don’t tell me that a man can be alone
My shadow’s got a heartbeat, my heartbeat’s got a guest
It’s wearing all my Sundays like a medal on its chest

[Breakdown]
Percy, keep your candle bright
I can hear it learning how I write
It takes my breath, it takes my tune
It drags the moon across the room

[Chorus]
There’s a ghost in my house—now it’s under my skin
It knows every lock I ever let it in
There’s a ghost in my house, hear the walls confess
But Percy burns gold through the dark, through the mess

[Outro]
I lift my little pumpkin to the doorway’s dying flame
The thing behind me whispers—then I whisper back its name
It fades with the last bell, and the house lets out one sigh
Percy and I watch Halloween walk quietly by
[End]

songPlan.title: See-saw'd Again (Empty Frame Mix)
songPlan.arrangement: A new identity-preserving gothic alternative-rock arrangement: pulsing melodic bass, muted electric guitar, tom-led drums, sparse piano and widening feedback textures replace the source backing while retaining the recognizable “See-saw” hook. Tony C V8 delivers smoky, connected, slightly slurred melodic lines, with the choruses opening into a catchable haunted refrain. Build from restrained verses through a tense bridge and stripped breakdown, then a full final chorus; pace the final sustained “you” about 10 seconds before the end, followed by one resolved D-minor chord decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
We skipped stones by the reservoir
You said the water knew our names
I found the old July photograph
And somebody stood beside the frame
Long black coat, pale folded hands
That patient smile I knew too well
I asked you, “That’s See-saw, right?”
You said, “Who are you trying to tell?”

[Pre-Chorus]
I remember your red bicycle
I remember cutting through the rain
But every road I try to follow
Leaves one shadow in the lane

[Chorus]
See-saw, See-saw, standing in the scene
Where you used to be, where you used to be
See-saw, See-saw, calm as anything
If I can’t trust my memory, what does real mean?

[Verse 2]
At the fair we rode the ferris wheel
You threw your hat into the crowd
I swear he held the cotton candy
And laughed a little much too loud
At the diner by the station
I named the tune that used to play
The waitress stared across the counter:
“No one like that came this way.”

[Pre-Chorus]
I remember all your small reactions
How you tapped the table when you lied
But every face I ask about him
Says there was no one by your side

[Chorus]
See-saw, See-saw, standing in the scene
Where you used to be, where you used to be
See-saw, See-saw, calm as anything
If I can’t trust my memory, what does real mean?

[Bridge]
I took the picture to your sister
She held it underneath the light
She said, “There are two of you in this one.
There was no third that summer night.”
The porch light, wet pavement,
The train that shook the bedroom wall—
Every detail stayed between us,
No See-saw saw it all

[Breakdown]
Maybe I built him from the silence
For one clean corner of the dark
Maybe every broken story
Needs a witness, needs a mark
But he knows the words you whispered
He knows where the old key hides
Then I hear my own voice answer:
“I put him there to stay alive.”

[Chorus]
See-saw, See-saw, fading from the scene
Where you used to be, where you used to be
See-saw, See-saw, no one else has seen
Just a name I gave the empty space between
See-saw, See-saw, I can finally say:
You were never there, but I remember you anyway

[Outro]
The reservoir is black and still
The photograph is in my hand
I turn it over, read the date,
Then let the answer understand:
Not yours, not mine, not his at all—
No third signature in blue
I don’t know why I made him real
But I know I remembered you
[End]

songPlan.title: See-saw in Every Picture
songPlan.arrangement: Nervy melodic alternative rock in E minor: driving bass, tight live drums, chiming electric guitars and a faint warbling organ texture that grows more unsettling as each memory shifts. Tony’s V8 lead is smoky, connected and naturally slurred, beginning conversationally before opening into a strong, catchable chorus. Build from a lean first verse to fuller final choruses, then keep the last sustained word “true” ending about 10 seconds before the 125-second mark; resolve with one final band chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
We skipped flat stones where the river went black
You bet me a dollar I could not skip back
I see the old water, I know that place
But there’s See-saw waving in your place

He’s got a paper cup, he’s got my coat
He’s saying my joke like he wrote every note
I tell you that’s funny, you stare at the bank
Like you never heard of the fellow I thank

[Pre-Chorus]
The film in my head keeps changing its frame
I reach for your voice and he answers my name

[Chorus]
See-saw, See-saw, where did you come from?
You’re in every Saturday, every small song
See-saw, See-saw, I know it ain’t right
But the more that I look, you’re there in the light

[Verse 2]
We drove to the coast in a car full of rain
You drew little monsters on my windowpane
Now See-saw is driving, one hand on the wheel
Singing out loud like the whole thing is real

We built that cheap kite from a grocery sack
It rose for a second, then came tumbling back
I remember us laughing, I remember the hill
But See-saw’s beside me, and he’s laughing still

[Bridge]
I opened the album, I counted to ten
Your face kept returning, then leaving again
There’s a space at the table, a name on the door
And See-saw says, “Buddy, we’ve done this before”

[Chorus]
See-saw, See-saw, where did you come from?
You’re in every hallway, every old song
I can’t solve the picture, I can’t make it clear
I just know you weren’t there—
and now you are here

[Outro]
If I find the first day before all the blur
I’ll ask what became of my friend, not you, sir
Till then the whole past keeps pulling me through
See-saw in every picture
and none of them true
[End]

songPlan.title: How Do I Enjoy Life
songPlan.arrangement: Comic-book rock in 4/4: punchy electric guitar, animated bass movement, crisp drums, organ stabs, and small cinematic brass-like synth hits. One clear, steadily pitched Tony lead carries melodic verses with conversational lift; keep the guide vocal clean and undoubled for later Tony conversion. Build from playful character sketches to a warm, sober final section. The last sung phrase lands about 9 seconds before the end, followed by one resolved G-major chord decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
My step-son leaned in at the kitchen light
Said, “How do I enjoy this life?”
I said, “Kid, I knew a whole wild crew
Each one had a different thing to do”

[Section 1]
Pancakeo took the megaphone downtown
Chasing loud arguments all around
He chased the girls and the bottle too
Like every bright sign was telling him true
He taught me a laugh can turn to smoke
When you make every night into one long joke

[Section 2]
Csaw came up through a house gone cold
A blameless child getting bruised by old
But he took that hurt and he stood up tall
Made a good man out of it all
He taught me the past may raise its hand
But it does not own the grown-up man

[Section 3]
Fox Reels counted every dollar twice
Trying to make a kingdom out of price
Then he found a steadier, deeper way
In faith and the choices of every day
He taught me money can open a door
But it cannot tell you what a heart is for

[Refrain]
So enjoy the light when it lands on you
Make a little room for the honest truth
Everybody’s writing a different page
Trying to get wiser at every age

[Section 4]
Cow looked me dead in the eye one day
Said, “MAN UP,” then he walked away
Not meaning harden, not meaning hide
Meaning carry your word with some pride
Limnos lifted till the ceiling shook
Chasing strength like a comic book
Steel and thunder, a body built wide
Still had to find peace on the inside

[Section 5]
Don Exodus kept a score in his head
“Last hits,” “waste of carbon,” the things he said
He saw the world like a battlefield screen
Always hunting the win in between
He taught me don’t make your whole life small
By measuring who gets more than all

[Bridge]
My step-son, life is not one command
It slips through the fingers, it changes hands
Take what helps, leave what makes you numb
Know when to fight and when to come home

[Refrain]
Enjoy the rain, enjoy the street
Enjoy the people you’re glad to meet
Give your days a reason to stay
And say what matters before it fades away

[Outro]
Then I remember Grizzman, gone too soon
A tragic silence in a crowded room
We carry his name with a careful flame
And wish he had known he was never to blame
So hold your friends when the nights get rough
Tell them plainly: you are enough
But to tell ya the truth, heh heh, heh
[End]

lyrics.text:
[Verse 1]
My step-son leaned in at the kitchen light
Said, “How do I enjoy this life?”
I said, “Kid, I knew a whole wild crew
Each one had a different thing to do”

[Section 1]
Pancakeo took the megaphone downtown
Chasing loud arguments all around
He chased the girls and the bottle too
Like every bright sign was telling him true
He taught me a laugh can turn to smoke
When you make every night into one long joke

[Section 2]
Csaw came up through a house gone cold
A blameless child getting bruised by old
But he took that hurt and he stood up tall
Made a good man out of it all
He taught me the past may raise its hand
But it does not own the grown-up man

[Section 3]
Fox Reels counted every dollar twice
Trying to make a kingdom out of price
Then he found a steadier, deeper way
In faith and the choices of every day
He taught me money can open a door
But it cannot tell you what a heart is for

[Refrain]
So enjoy the light when it lands on you
Make a little room for the honest truth
Everybody’s writing a different page
Trying to get wiser at every age

[Section 4]
Cow looked me dead in the eye one day
Said, “MAN UP,” then he walked away
Not meaning harden, not meaning hide
Meaning carry your word with some pride
Limnos lifted till the ceiling shook
Chasing strength like a comic book
Steel and thunder, a body built wide
Still had to find peace on the inside

[Section 5]
Don Exodus kept a score in his head
“Last hits,” “waste of carbon,” the things he said
He saw the world like a battlefield screen
Always hunting the win in between
He taught me don’t make your whole life small
By measuring who gets more than all

[Bridge]
My step-son, life is not one command
It slips through the fingers, it changes hands
Take what helps, leave what makes you numb
Know when to fight and when to come home

[Refrain]
Enjoy the rain, enjoy the street
Enjoy the people you’re glad to meet
Give your days a reason to stay
And say what matters before it fades away

[Outro]
Then I remember Grizzman, gone too soon
A tragic silence in a crowded room
We carry his name with a careful flame
And wish he had known he was never to blame
So hold your friends when the nights get rough
Tell them plainly: you are enough
But to tell ya the truth, heh heh, heh

songPlan.title: See-saw'd Again
songPlan.arrangement: Dark, hook-driven post-punk rock built around a tense drum-machine pulse, with stark stops before each chorus and a rising final refrain. Tony’s V8 delivery is smoky, connected, half-muttered in the verses and opens into sustained, catchable sung hooks. Keep the final sung word “you” sustained about 9 seconds before the end, then resolve on one final chord-like synth hit and decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
We skipped stones by the reservoir
You said the water knew our names
But in the photograph I found
There’s a man beside the frame
Long black coat, pale folded hands
A smile like he had always been
You said, “That’s See-saw, don’t you know?”
Like I was late to let him in

[Pre-Chorus]
I remember your red bicycle
I remember cutting through the rain
But every road I try to follow
Has his footprints in the lane

[Chorus]
See-saw, See-saw, standing in the scene
Where you used to be, where you used to be
See-saw, See-saw, calm as anything
If I can’t trust my memory, what does real mean?

[Verse 2]
At the fair we rode the ferris wheel
You threw your hat down at the crowd
Now he’s holding cotton candy
And he’s laughing much too loud
At the diner by the station
I can hear your favorite song
But the waitress says See-saw taught her
How I take my coffee wrong

[Pre-Chorus]
I remember all your small reactions
How you’d tap the table when you lied
But when I close my eyes to find you
There’s a stranger by your side

[Chorus]
See-saw, See-saw, standing in the scene
Where you used to be, where you used to be
See-saw, See-saw, calm as anything
If I can’t trust my memory, what does real mean?

[Bridge]
I asked the mirror in the hallway
“Who was there that summer night?”
My reflection took a second
Then it answered, “You were right”
It said, “The porch light, the wet pavement
The train that shook the bedroom wall—
See-saw had his hand upon your shoulder
See-saw saw it all”

[Breakdown]
Maybe I invented you to keep
One clean corner of the dark
Maybe every little story
Needs a witness and a mark
But he knows the words you whispered
He knows where the old key hides
And each time I say your name out loud
See-saw answers from inside

[Chorus]
See-saw, See-saw, standing in the scene
Where you used to be, where you used to be
See-saw, See-saw, turning every dream
Till the past is just a room with no way out for me
See-saw, See-saw, I’m asking one last thing:
If you were never there, then who have I been?

[Outro]
The reservoir is black and still
The photograph is in my hand
I turn it over, read the date
Then see the name I understand:
Not yours, not mine, not his alone—
Three signatures in fading blue
I don’t know what was real back then
But I know I remembered you
[End]

songPlan.title: Influence Criteria (Post-Punk Audit)
songPlan.arrangement: A tense, bass-forward post-punk reinterpretation in D minor: clipped guitar stabs, elastic melodic bass, dry live drums, sparse analog synth pulses, and a sharp chorus lift. Tony V8 delivers rough connected vowels, muttered impatience, and a catchable sustained hook without turning the verses into rap. Start lean and nervous, build through the stacked-ranking verse, strip to bass and drums for the confrontation, then return with a defiant final chorus. Pace the final outro so “this year” is the final sustained vocal 8–12 seconds before 3:50, followed by one resolved D-minor chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Badge flashes green at six-oh-five
Rain on the glass, whole lobby alive
I built the thing, I shipped it clean
Still no applause from the weekly machine
My manager says, "You did the work"
Then pauses hard with a practiced smirk
"The numbers shine, but the story's thin
Show us how you pull people in"

[Pre-Chorus]
I ask for a map, they hand me smoke
A leadership principle dressed as a joke

[Chorus]
Tell me what Influence means
Is it a meeting, is it a scene?
Is it my name on somebody's slide?
Is it a room where the truth stays outside?
I made the river run on time
Still I'm below some invisible line
Tell me what Influence means
Before they measure me out of the team

[Verse 2]
A document lands in a careful tone
Thirty days to prove I don't work alone
A PIP with boxes, amber and red
Every vague little signal inside my head
"Raise the bar," "earn trust," "think big"
I circle each phrase till the margins twitch
I ask what changed; they clear their throats
And answer in weather reports and notes

[Verse 3]
Stack ranking sleeps beneath the floor
A polished bell above a trapdoor
We trade our wins in a narrow light
Trying to look indispensable, pleasant, bright
I helped her launch, he fixed my break
Now every favor has a shape to take
The spreadsheet hums with a private heat
And somebody's future loses a seat

[Chorus]
Tell me what Influence means
Is it a meeting, is it a scene?
Is it my name on somebody's slide?
Is it a room where the truth stays outside?
I made the river run on time
Still I'm below some invisible line
Tell me what Influence means
Before they measure me out of the team

[Bridge]
Thursday night under brewery light
Tiny name tags, rehearsed delight
I hold a paper cup, perform a laugh
Make a network from the better half
They call it connection, they call it care
I call it breathing conference air

[Breakdown]
I brought a plan to the skip-level call
Three sharp proposals, risks and all
"Be louder in the room," he said
Like volume makes a garden spread
Whose room? Which door? What proof?
Silence gathers around the truth
Then somebody says, "Let's take this offline"
And the clock keeps chewing borrowed time

[Chorus]
Now I know what Influence means
A shadow moving behind the scenes
A handshake held a second too long
A careful smile where a doubt belongs
I made the river run on time
I will not vanish to fit their line
You can score me, sort me, close the screen
I am more than your Influence criteria

[Outro]
Keep your amber boxes, keep your chart
I kept the craft and I kept my heart
When the badge goes dark and the hallway clears
I leave with my name intact this year
[End]

songPlan.title: Ranked and Cast Aside
songPlan.arrangement: A militant roots-reggae protest song in D minor: deep rolling bass, offbeat electric guitar skank, one-drop drums, organ bubbles, percussion, and brief muted horn answers. Tony delivers smoky, connected, rough melodic lines with muttered bite in the verses and a broad, catchable chorus. Build from restrained verses to a defiant final chorus; the bridge carries one short low throaty accent on “We were never numbers,” then returns to the normal lead. Keep vocals present throughout, with the final sustained “high” landing about 10 seconds before the end, followed by one resolved band chord and decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Morning badge clicks, fluorescent rain
A little red number beside your name
They call it progress, call it the way
But somebody’s got to be thrown away

[Verse 1]
I watched the meeting from the end of the hall
Smiling faces pinned up on the wall
“Teamwork matters,” the poster said
While they measured who they could leave for dead
A bell curve drawn with a lawyer’s pen
Turns friends into figures again and again
You carry the load, you cover the shift
Then they grade your soul like a quarterly lift

[Pre-Chorus]
No, I won’t bow to their paper crown
No, I won’t help them drag you down

[Chorus]
Stack rank, backstab, cut that line
They make a ladder from a friend of mine
Stack rank, backstab, hear that sound
A clean white office burning people down
We were never numbers in a slide-show light
We were hands on the wheel through the longest night
Stack rank, backstab, I say it plain
Your little game is somebody’s pain

[Verse 2]
Marlene stayed late when the servers froze
Kept the whole damn place from coming unclosed
Then the manager said, with a practiced sigh
“Your contribution’s low compared to the guy”
The guy got credit for the fix she made
He shook the boss’s hand while her future frayed
They call it merit, they call it fair
But the winners are picked before anybody’s there

[Bridge]
[Throat Accent: We were never numbers]
We were never numbers, no, no
Not names to erase when the budgets get thin
You want us divided, competing for breath
But I know that scoreboard is a slow little death
So pass me the file, pass me the proof
I’ll nail every lie to the boardroom roof

[Verse 3]
Let the quarterly prophets count their gold
Let them rehearse what the memo told
I’ll stand with the tired and the passed-around
With the quiet good people they marked down
No more whispering by the coffee machine
No more pretending we don’t know what it means
If they need one loser to bless their chart
They can take their ranking and break it apart

[Chorus]
Stack rank, backstab, cut that line
They make a ladder from a friend of mine
Stack rank, backstab, hear that sound
A clean white office burning people down
We were never numbers in a slide-show light
We were hands on the wheel through the longest night
Stack rank, backstab, the truth remains
No chart can measure what a worker sustains

[Outro]
When the final bell rings, I’ll still stand near
With every name they tried to disappear
No more rank, no more cast aside
We leave that room with our heads held high
[End]
