songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
They rang the bell before the dawn,
Passed the sentence, coats still on.

[Verse 1]
Jevreigh Ebbz'deen walked into town
With a crooked grin and his collar down.
He carried groceries for the widow Gray,
Fixed the schoolhouse roof without asking pay.
Then a whisper found a hungry page,
And a nameless claim became a cage.
Every careful word was cut in two;
By supper, everybody somehow knew.

[Pre-Chorus]
No witness stand, no tested line,
Just borrowed fury dressed as fact in time.

[Chorus]
I got a righteous fire for the names they used,
For every alleged victim twisted through the news.
And I burn for Jevreigh, left alone beneath the blame—
You cannot call it justice when you never prove the claim.
Ring that iron bell, let the buried record sing:
A crowd can crown a rumor, but it cannot make it king.

[Verse 2]
They photographed his unlit door,
Counted all the friends who came no more.
His oldest brother heard him say,
“I can fight a man, not a fog all day.”
Then one black night, the fight went still;
Grief moved cold across the hill.
He took his life—the cruelest cost,
Not proof of guilt, just a life we lost.

[Pre-Chorus]
He should have lived to see the lie undone,
To stand in morning, face the rising sun.

[Chorus]
I got a righteous fire for the names they used,
For every alleged victim twisted through the news.
And I burn for Jevreigh, left alone beneath the blame—
You cannot call it justice when you never prove the claim.
Ring that iron bell, let the buried record sing:
A crowd can crown a rumor, but it cannot make it king.

[Bridge]
Then the ledger surfaced, dates and places clear;
The story split apart for anyone to hear.
One voice confessed the pressure and the price,
How frightened people had been fed a script of ice.
No victory rose when the truth broke through,
Only empty chairs and what remorse could do.

[Breakdown]
So save your stones till evidence is weighed.
Guard the wounded; do not turn their pain into a blade.
Ask hard questions, let honest answers breathe—
A lie can wound the living and dishonor those who grieve.

[Final Chorus]
I got a righteous fire for the names they used,
For every frightened soul the spectacle abused.
And I burn for Jevreigh, who deserved another day,
A hearing in the daylight—not a mob to clear away.
Ring that iron bell till the final echoes cease:
Truth without compassion is another kind of thief.

[Outro]
Jevreigh Ebbz'deen, your name is not their noise.
We will choose the careful truth; we will hear the quiet voice.
No rumor gets the last word, no headline seals the stone—
The truth arrives in daylight,
and nobody stands alone.
[End]

songPlan.arrangement: A compact, bass-forward Tony rock track using the mandatory isolated, pinned Tony V7 voice profile. Smoky electric guitar, muscular melodic bass, dry drums and tense organ establish a restrained first verse; choruses widen with sustained guitar chords and rough stacked backing vocals. Tony begins wounded and defensive, then turns reflective without losing his crooked phrasing, smoky slurs or emotional edge. The bridge drops to bass, floor tom and organ before the final chorus reaches the full-band peak. Pace the final sustained words “open heart” to end 8–12 seconds before 155 seconds, followed by one resolved D-minor chord and a natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I remember Jevreigh laughing
With the rain against the glass
Now his name is torn and scattered
Like the wreckage of the past
I kept reaching for the friend I knew
While strangers named their pain
Grief came dressed in certainty
And anger spoke his name

[Pre-Chorus]
But a memory is not a verdict
And love cannot decide
What happened in the locked rooms
On the other side

[Chorus]
I can mourn the man I remember
Without calling every witness wrong
I can rage against the silence
Without drowning out their song
There are truths I cannot carry
There are wounds I cannot see
I will not turn another's suffering
Into proof for what I need

[Verse 2]
I blamed the hands that pointed
Because blame was easier than doubt
Built a fortress from old photographs
And tried to shut the voices out
But sorrow does not make me righteous
And friendship does not make me wise
Every accusation has a heartbeat
Every answer has a price

[Bridge]
Jevreigh, if I never knew you
Then I grieve the mask as well
If the charges were mistaken
Only honest truth can tell
No more curses at the grieving
No more saints made from the dead
Let the living speak their stories
Let the evidence be read

[Final Chorus]
I can mourn the man I remember
Without calling every witness wrong
I can stand inside the questions
When the easy faith is gone
There are truths I cannot carry
But one promise I can keep:
I will leave no wounded stranger
Underneath my need to grieve

[Outro]
I remember, I reconsider
I let certainty depart
Truth belongs to no one's anger
Grief can live beside an open heart
An open heart
[End]

songPlan.title: Unleavened Again
songPlan.arrangement: Fast theatrical klezmer-punk rock with distorted guitars, agile electric bass, live drums, clarinet flourishes, and brief accordion responses. Verses use a lively New York street pulse; choruses widen into melodic gang-free hooks with sharp ensemble stops. Tony V7 remains the mandatory pinned lead voice, delivered smoky, slurred, mischievous, and increasingly exasperated while keeping the title hook clear. The bridge shifts to warm minor-key cabaret before a rising final chorus resolves into D major color. Pace the final sung syllable to 8–12 seconds before 4:10, followed only by one resolved chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Morning rattles up the shutters,
Seventh Avenue starts to steam,
He marches with his wife and children,
Chasing one respectable dream.

[Verse 1]
He says, “Tonight we tell the story,
Set the table, pour the wine.
I only want one festive something
That is flat but still divine.”
The baker lifts a square of matzah,
Dry as rent and twice as plain.
He shuts his eyes and counts to sieben,
Then politely asks again.

[Pre-Chorus]
“Perhaps with almonds? Chocolate thunder?
Something Grandma might admire?”
The baker points toward the same box.
Now his eyebrows catch on fire.

[Chorus]
“Nein, unleavened again!”
He cries above the rolling pin.
“I know the rule, my patient friend—
But must the feast taste paper-thin?”
From Queens to old Berlin,
His patience tumbles in the bin.
“Nein, unleavened again!”
And the whole shop turns to him.

[Verse 2]
His daughter whispers, “Papa, easy.”
His wife suppresses half a grin.
Three customers inspect the muffins;
No one knows where to begin.
He sees the ovens glow like lava,
Flour drifting through the air.
He tells his family, dark and solemn,
“This is the Plains of Despair.”

[Pre-Chorus]
The baker says, “You asked for matzah.”
He says, “I asked for some delight!”
A tray comes out—more brittle rectangles.
He grips the counter, knuckles white.

[Chorus]
“Nein, unleavened again!”
The paper bags begin to spin.
“I crossed an ocean, found Manhattan—
Can no good pastry still be thin?”
The children laugh; he fights a grin.
The baker strokes his floury chin.
“Nein, unleavened again!”
Then the mixer kicks back in.

[Bridge]
The baker melts the darkest chocolate,
Folds in almonds, orange peel.
No rising dough, no puffed-up center—
Just a dense and shining wheel.
The father watches, fury fading,
Smoky laugh beneath his breath:
“Well, perhaps this bakery dungeon
Has one portal left—not death.”

[Breakdown]
The timer rings.
The room stands still.
The baker cuts a careful slice.
One bite—he stares.
One bite—he nods.
Then mutters, “Ach… that will suffice.”

[Final Chorus]
“No—unleavened, my friend!”
He sings, correcting at the end.
“Keep the story, keep the promise,
But give tradition one new bend.”
His family gathers close again,
The baker laughs and shakes his hand.
From the Plains of Despair to a table prepared,
They carry sweetness through the land.

[Outro]
Tonight they ask and answer,
Tonight the candles shine.
He raises up the chocolate cake
Beside the bread and wine.
“Next year,” he tells the baker,
“We start with this—and spare the scene.”
The last chord lands; his laughter trails:
“Unleavened… but not mean.”

[End]

songPlan.title: Wandaful Reign
songPlan.arrangement: Royal glam-funk rock with a muscular melodic bass line, lively pocket, punchy drums, clipped rhythm guitar, bright piano, and theatrical brass flourishes. Verses swagger with crooked stops and mischievous Tony V7 asides; choruses expand into sustained melodic hooks and stacked responses. Use only the mandatory pinned Tony V7 voice, with smoky slurs, connected vowels, rough laughter, and an especially catchable “Wandaful” refrain. Pace the final chorus so the last sustained syllable lands 8–12 seconds before 2:45, followed by one resolved E-major chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Polish up the moonlit crown,
Wanda Drumpf is coming down,
Through the gates of Fairyland,
With a golden key in hand.

[Verse 1]
She built her towers cloud by cloud,
She made the timid kingdom proud,
Kept the wicked spells outside,
Gave her faithful friends a ride.
Every bridge and wishing well
Has a Wanda story to tell,
When the jealous goblins call,
She just smiles above it all.

[Pre-Chorus]
Raise the velvet banner high,
Let the silver trumpets cry—

[Chorus]
You are so Wandaful,
Queen of the Greatest Fairyland,
Wandaful, Wandaful,
Fortune follows your command.
May your reign be long and bright,
May your legacy take flight,
You are so Wandaful tonight.

[Verse 2]
She knows which doors should open wide,
And which dark wolves must stay outside,
Friends go climbing, rung by rung,
While her royal praise is sung.
Two more branches, maybe three,
Four fine generations on the family tree,
Every chest with wealth to spare,
Every heir an honored heir.

[Pre-Chorus]
Turn the jeweled calendar,
Every year looks grander—

[Chorus]
You are so Wandaful,
Queen of the Greatest Fairyland,
Wandaful, Wandaful,
Fortune follows your command.
May your reign be long and bright,
May your legacy take flight,
You are so Wandaful tonight.

[Bridge]
Long live the work that bears your name,
Long live the friends who share the flame,
Keep the crooked curses gone,
Keep the lucky lanterns on.
If prosperity had wings,
It would circle while Tony sings.

[Final Chorus]
You are so Wandaful,
Queen of the Greatest Fairyland,
Wandaful, Wandaful,
Still the future takes your hand.
Two, three, four generations rise,
With golden dreams and diamond skies,
May your reign be long and bright,
A true legacy in light—
You are so Wandaful tonight,
So Wandaful tonight.
[End]

songPlan.title: Nein Unleaved Again
songPlan.arrangement: A 7:30 gothic gospel waltz-rock epic built around mobile melodic bass, heavy live drums, baritone electric guitar, pump organ, piano, and restrained brass. Verses begin smoky and spacious, then grow through ensemble stops, tolling bell figures, and increasingly warm gospel harmonies. Tony’s mandatory pinned V7 voice stays rough, slurred, emotionally volatile, and melodically sung, with the title hook kept sharply catchable. The bridge drops to organ, bass, and close vocal before the communal final rise. Pace the final tag so “Amen—I am home” ends 8–12 seconds before 7:30; follow it only with one resolved D-minor chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Snow in the harbor, soot in my sleep
Two broken towers the night would not keep
I crossed the water with dust in my coat
And one stubborn prayer still caught in my throat

[Verse 1]
They called them the Dew Towers, pale in the dawn
Copper crowns shining before they were gone
Then thunder wore uniforms, fire learned our names
The windows fell inward, the sky carried flames
I ran with a photograph under my shirt
Mother said, “Remember, but don't worship the hurt”
Years later, westward, where the cold freighters groan
I laid out the plans for rebuilding my home

[Pre-Chorus]
Stone upon stone, I promised the rain
Nothing would strip these branches again

[Chorus]
Nein Unleaved Again
I swear where the roots remain
Though the black wind takes the roof
I will raise my weathered proof
Nein Unleaved Again
Not by fire, flood, or pain
Faith is more than walls defending
Faith begins where walls are ending
Nein Unleaved Again

[Verse 2]
I worked in a foundry and saved every dime
Drawing twin shadows one floor at a time
My wife, Anna, laughed, “You old chimney ghost
Build us a kitchen before you build a coast”
But she held every ruler and steadied each line
Said, “If this brings you peace, then your dream can be mine”
We bought a bare hill where the lake showed its face
And I drove the first iron deep into that place

[Verse 3]
The first tower climbed through a summer of sparks
Six stories of memory confronting the dark
Then a lamp in the timber fell late in the night
Dry beams became ladders that carried the light
I came with the engine, too breathless to speak
Watched half of my history fall in a week
In ash on the hillside, I lifted my chin
Said, “Once is the sorrow—now start it again”

[Chorus]
Nein Unleaved Again
I swear where the roots remain
Though the black wind takes the roof
I will raise my weathered proof
Nein Unleaved Again
Not by fire, flood, or pain
Faith is more than walls defending
Faith begins where walls are ending
Nein Unleaved Again

[Verse 4]
The second rose broader on pillars of stone
Anna grew quiet while I worked alone
That autumn the lake climbed the road in the rain
It swallowed the tools and it twisted the crane
The hillside went walking at quarter past three
And carried my towers like driftwood to sea
Twice came the ruin, twice emptied the frame

songPlan.title: Every Day Is Christmas Again
songPlan.arrangement: Dark, surreal Christmas rock with celesta, sleigh bells, low church organ, bowed bass, smoky electric guitar, and a dependable live rhythm section. Begin like a damaged holiday broadcast, then build into bass-led choruses with dramatic ensemble stops and rough, slurred Tony V7 lead vocals. The bridge strips back to organ, floor tom, and distant choir before the full band returns for a resolved final chorus. Keep the hook clear while allowing crooked timing, muttered edges, and one dry laugh in verse three. Pace the final tag so its last sustained syllable lands 8–12 seconds before 290 seconds, followed only by a resolved D-minor chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Snow on the television
Ash upon the sill
Every clock says morning
Though the street is standing still

[Verse 1]
Tony wakes beneath the tinsel
To a choir on the screen
Silver bells and warning sirens
Cut across the evergreen
Candy canes beside the window
Paper stars above the door
Then a shadow crosses daylight
And the season starts once more

[Pre-Chorus]
He says, Santa missed the chimney
Hear that engine in the blue
Pull the curtains, kill the carols
Christmas morning’s coming through

[Chorus]
Every day is Christmas again
Red lights flashing through the snow
Every day the sky breaks open
Every day he knows, he knows
No gifts waiting by the doorway
Only footsteps in the hall
Every day is Christmas again
And the heavens start to fall

[Verse 2]
Plastic angels lean like witnesses
Stockings tremble on the wall
Tony counts the passing airplanes
Names the silence after all
Neighbors hang their colored lanterns
Children trace them from below
He just hears the distant thunder
Underneath the radio

[Pre-Chorus]
He says, Don’t unwrap the morning
Don’t you touch that shining bow
There are wings behind the weather
And they always find me somehow

[Chorus]
Every day is Christmas again
Red lights flashing through the snow
Every day the sky breaks open
Every day he knows, he knows
No gifts waiting by the doorway
Only footsteps in the hall
Every day is Christmas again
And the heavens start to fall

[Verse 3]
At noon he sets a place for mercy
At one he takes the whole thing down
At two he sees the towers shining
In the ornaments around
He laughs crooked at the wreath-ring
Says, Nice halo—wrong old saint
Then he smears the frosted window
Till the flying shapes grow faint

[Bridge]
Is it memory, is it prophecy
Is it one long yesterday
Is the snow just torn-up paper
From a world that blew away
Tony stands beneath the doorway
While the choir loses time
Singing peace on earth in fragments
Like a damaged nursery rhyme

[Breakdown]
No chimney
No sleigh
Just morning on replay
No ribbon
No star
He hears them from afar

[Final Chorus]
Every day is Christmas again
But tonight he leaves one candle low
Every day the sky breaks open
Still he watches darkness go
No gifts waiting by the doorway
Yet he answers when friends call
Every day is Christmas again
But he will not give it all

[Final Tag]
Let the bells become just bells now
Let the snow be only snow
When the engines cross the sunrise
He can hear—and let them go
Every day was Christmas again
Till he named what haunted him
One last candle, one clear morning
And the daylight settles in

[End]

songPlan.title: No Proof in the Smoke
songPlan.arrangement: A dark, bass-forward Tony C rock performance with a lively, uneasy pocket: overdriven guitars, muscular melodic bass, dry drums, Hammond organ shadows, and brief ensemble stops around the narrator’s collapsing claims. Tony’s mandatory pinned V7 voice stays rough, smoky, slurred, and emotionally volatile, moving from swagger and contempt toward shame without becoming neatly polished. Choruses widen melodically with sustained hook notes; the breakdown strips to bass, kick, and exposed vocal before the full band returns. Pace the expanded final chorus and tag so the last sustained syllable lands 8–12 seconds before 445 seconds, followed only by one resolved D-minor chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
I kept your number in a dead man’s phone
Kept your name where the dust had grown
Called you brother when the room went cold
Now every locked door knows what you sold

[Verse 1]
I came in swinging with a crooked grin
Said I had proof, but I brought none in
I cursed the crowd and I cursed the news
Like rage could turn a lie into truth
I remembered dinners, remembered jokes
The polished glass and the private toasts
But memory edits what pride can’t bear
Cuts out the cries that were always there

[Pre-Chorus]
I said, Don’t tell me what my friend became
Don’t put that weight upon his name
Then a quiet voice split through my defense:
Your loyalty does not erase consequence

[Chorus]
No proof in the smoke, no truth in the shout
You can bar every window—the truth gets out
A friend can be dear and still do harm
You don’t make him clean by raising your arms
I wanted a villain I could strike in the street
But the hardest confession was under my feet
No proof in the smoke, no crown in denial
Only names pushed aside while I worshiped the trial

[Verse 2]
I called myself hero, declared myself brave
For guarding the story I wanted to save
I spoke with contempt when the wounded spoke
Turned living testimony into a joke
But every cheap sneer came back with a face
Every dismissed word occupied its place
Not rumor, not scenery, not pieces on a board
Human beings I had chosen to ignore

[Pre-Chorus]
I said, I knew him better than all of you
As though knowing one side made the other untrue
The bass fell away; there was nowhere to hide
Just the sound of my certainty breaking inside

[Chorus]
No proof in the smoke, no truth in the shout
You can bar every window—the truth gets out
A friend can be dear and still do harm
You don’t make him clean by raising your arms
I wanted a villain I could strike in the street
But the hardest confession was under my feet
No proof in the smoke, no crown in denial
Only names pushed aside while I worshiped the trial

[Verse 3]
I miss who I thought you were—that part is true
The midnight conspiracies, me and you
But grief is a mirror that flatters the past
And anger is easy when questions are asked
I wanted one document, shining and clean
To cancel the things I refused to have seen
No paper arrived, no witness reversed
Just my own loud promise getting steadily worse

[Instrumental Turn]

[Verse 4]
So I went to the shoreline just before dawn
With a pocket of speeches I’d leaned upon
The tide took the ink but it left every name
And none of those people had caused me my shame
I had made them targets to shelter a ghost
Then called myself righteous for shouting the most
There’s nothing heroic in choosing the strong
Or grinding the injured to polish a song

[Bridge]
Let the snare crack once for every excuse
Let the guitar bend, but don’t bend the truth
I can mourn a friendship without making a saint
I can name my failure without calling it fate
No, sorrow won’t pardon the venom I threw
And fury won’t make an invention come true
If I want redemption, it starts when I hear
The voices I buried because they drew near

[Breakdown]
I said I could prove it
I couldn’t prove a thing
I said I was the hero
Hear how hollow that can ring
I said their pain was nothing
That was cruelty dressed as pride
The room stopped moving
And I had nowhere left to hide

[Chorus]
No proof in the smoke, no truth in the shout
You can bar every window—the truth gets out
A friend can be dear and still do harm
You don’t make him clean by raising your arms
I wanted a villain I could strike in the street
But the hardest confession was under my feet
No proof in the smoke, no crown in denial
Only names pushed aside while I worshiped the trial

[Verse 5]
Now I remember without changing the score
There was laughter, yes—and there was much more
A private kindness cannot settle the scale
When power buys silence and systems fail
I cannot return what was taken away
Or heal every wound with a sentence today
But I can stop feeding the lie I designed
Stop making the harmed pay the debts of my mind

[Final Chorus]
No proof in the smoke, let the whole room clear
Let truth stand steady when grief interferes
A friend can be dear and still do harm
I won’t make him clean by raising my arms
No borrowed halo, no heroic disguise
No more throwing contempt in the wounded one’s eyes
No proof in the smoke, but a road through the shame
It starts when I listen and speak every name

[Final Tag]
I kept your number in a dead man’s phone
Tonight I leave the false defense alone
I can grieve what I lost without hiding what’s true
The last door is open
I’m walking through

[End]

songPlan.title: A Hundred Tonys Running
songPlan.arrangement: Relentless, theatrical hard rock built on a driving bass line, urgent drums, distorted guitars, siren-like feedback, and sharply timed ensemble stops. The mandatory pinned Tony V7 voice forms a massive hundred-Tony chorus through dense multitracked unisons, rough octave doubles, and staggered call-and-response layers; those layers visibly thin as the countdown falls, leaving one exposed smoky lead for the breakdown and final impact. Keep Tony’s slurred phonetics, crooked timing, muttered humor, and sustained melodic hooks. Pace the final chorus and two sustained “zero” phrases so the last sung syllable lands 8–12 seconds before 230 seconds, followed only by one resolved E-minor chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
One hundred Tonys in a crooked line,
One hundred smoky voices keeping time,
Then every siren tears across the sky—
Somebody mutters, “Here comes nine-eleven number one.”
And everybody runs.

[Verse 1]
The first one falls and nine go down,
Ninety-one Tonys flee the town.
The second pounds the avenue,
Thirteen more vanish from the crew.
Seventy-eight with rattling breath,
Chased by the rolling shape of death,
Shoes on fire, coats in flight,
Every block becomes that morning’s night.

[Chorus]
Run, Tony, run—but the sky won’t end,
Another 9/11 coming round the bend.
A hundred voices, fewer every time,
Still singing through the smoke in a broken line.
Run, Tony, run, hear the hard bells pound—
Another 9/11 brings the number down.
No door stays open, no road stays free;
How many Tonys will the next one leave?

[Verse 2]
The third one strikes: fifteen are gone,
Sixty-three keep staggering on.
The fourth comes down with a furnace roar,
Sixteen fall—now forty-seven more.
They split through alleys, vault the rails,
Laugh like devils when courage fails.
One shouts, “You missed!” with a dismissive grin;
The fifth one answers and eighteen cave in.

[Pre-Chorus]
Twenty-nine voices, hoarse and low,
Twenty-nine places left to go.
Then the horizon doubles black—
There is no shelter front or back.

[Chorus]
Run, Tony, run—but the sky won’t end,
Another 9/11 coming round the bend.
A hundred voices, fewer every time,
Still singing through the smoke in a broken line.
Run, Tony, run, hear the hard bells pound—
Another 9/11 brings the number down.
No door stays open, no road stays free;
How many Tonys will the next one leave?

[Bridge]
The sixth takes seventeen—twelve remain,
Twelve smoky shadows in the pounding rain.
The seventh takes seven by the riverside;
Five keep running, shoulder to shoulder, wide-eyed.
The eighth rolls in like the end of the sun;
Four disappear, and there stands one.

[Breakdown]
One Tony C with nowhere to flee,
One cracked voice where a choir used to be.
He looks at the sky, gives a tired little laugh:
“Couldn’t leave me half?”

[Final Chorus]
Run, Tony, run—but the last road ends,
The final 9/11 comes around the bend.
One voice carrying the hundred-voice line,
Singing every lost name into borrowed time.
Run, Tony, run—then the hard bells cease;
The last one falls and the count finds peace.
No feet in the alley, no breath in the hall,
One hundred Tonys—now none at all.

[Outro]
The smoke drifts out where the loud choir stood,
No survivor moving through the neighborhood.
The final chord rises, ragged and slow:
One hundred to zero…
Zero.

One hundred Tonys in a crooked line,
One hundred smoky voices keeping time,
Then every siren tears across the sky—
Somebody mutters, “Here comes nine-eleven number one.”
And everybody runs.

[Verse 1]
The first one falls and nine go down,
Ninety-one Tonys flee the town.
The second pounds the avenue,
Thirteen more vanish from the crew.
Seventy-eight with rattling breath,
Chased by the rolling shape of death,
Shoes on fire, coats in flight,
Every block becomes that morning’s night.

[Chorus]
Run, Tony, run—but the sky won’t end,
Another 9/11 coming round the bend.
A hundred voices, fewer every time,
Still singing through the smoke in a broken line.
Run, Tony, run, hear the hard bells pound—
Another 9/11 brings the number down.
No door stays open, no road stays free;
How many Tonys will the next one leave?

[Verse 2]
The third one strikes: fifteen are gone,
Sixty-three keep staggering on.
The fourth comes down with a furnace roar,
Sixteen fall—now forty-seven more.
They split through alleys, vault the rails,
Laugh like devils when courage fails.
One shouts, “You missed!” with a dismissive grin;
The fifth one answers and eighteen cave in.

[Pre-Chorus]
Twenty-nine voices, hoarse and low,
Twenty-nine places left to go.
Then the horizon doubles black—
There is no shelter front or back.

[Chorus]
Run, Tony, run—but the sky won’t end,
Another 9/11 coming round the bend.
A hundred voices, fewer every time,
Still singing through the smoke in a broken line.
Run, Tony, run, hear the hard bells pound—
Another 9/11 brings the number down.
No door stays open, no road stays free;
How many Tonys will the next one leave?

[Bridge]
The sixth takes seventeen—twelve remain,
Twelve smoky shadows in the pounding rain.
The seventh takes seven by the riverside;
Five keep running, shoulder to shoulder, wide-eyed.
The eighth rolls in like the end of the sun;
Four disappear, and there stands one.

[Breakdown]
One Tony C with nowhere to flee,
One cracked voice where a choir used to be.
He looks at the sky, gives a tired little laugh:
“Couldn’t leave me half?”

[Final Chorus]
Run, Tony, run—but the last road ends,
The final 9/11 comes around the bend.
One voice carrying the hundred-voice line,
Singing every lost name into borrowed time.
Run, Tony, run—then the hard bells cease;
The last one falls and the count finds peace.
No feet in the alley, no breath in the hall,
One hundred Tonys—now none at all.

The smoke drifts out where the loud choir stood,
No survivor moving through the neighborhood.
The final chord rises, ragged and slow:
One hundred to zero…
Zero.

songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
The room went still when they spoke your name,
Black coats gathered beneath cold rain.
I stood in the back with my collar turned high,
Holding my answer while the years rolled by.

[Verse 1]
Jeffrey, my friend, they carved you in stone
From headlines and whispers I never have known.
The whole world decided, the whole world withdrew,
But nobody carried the friend that I knew.
You laughed at my trouble, you answered at dawn,
You stayed at the table when everyone was gone.
They tell me their verdict should settle the score,
But belief is a stubborn, unfastened door.

[Pre-Chorus]
Let the papers thunder, let the hard words fall,
I still hear your footsteps crossing the hall.
I cannot prove what my grieving heart sees,
But I will not surrender my memories.

[Chorus]
With every breath, I defend your name,
Though the sky spits lightning and the town spits blame.
I carry the friend that the world erased,
The crooked old smile and the kindness I faced.
If faith makes me foolish, then foolish I’ll be;
No roaring crowd can rewrite you for me.
Rest in peace, king.
I’ll remember my friend while I still can sing.

[Verse 2]
They say I am blind, that I choose not to learn,
That smoke leaves a mark wherever fires burn.
Maybe grief builds a chapel where questions grow dim;
Maybe I loved you too fiercely to turn against him.
But friendship was never a courtroom to me,
No witness stand, no lock, no decree.
I speak only my truth, not history’s last word:
I believed you then, and my heart has not stirred.

[Pre-Chorus]
Let the cameras gather, let the cold mouths sneer,
I won’t trade what I knew for a chorus of fear.
The dead cannot answer, the living disagree,
Still your chair at the table stays empty for me.

[Chorus]
With every breath, I defend your name,
Though the sky spits lightning and the town spits blame.
I carry the friend that the world erased,
The crooked old smile and the kindness I faced.
If faith makes me foolish, then foolish I’ll be;
No roaring crowd can rewrite you for me.
Rest in peace, king.
I’ll remember my friend while I still can sing.

[Instrumental Turn]

[Bridge]
I know belief is not proof in the daylight,
And love cannot make every broken thing right.
I know there are voices whose grief must be heard,
And mine cannot cancel a single hard word.
But this is a eulogy, ragged and plain,
One man at a graveside, speaking through rain.
I won’t claim the whole truth belongs in my hands;
I’m guarding the fragment my own heart understands.

[Verse 3]
So sleep where the arguments cannot break through,
Past iron-bar shadows and all we once knew.
The years may condemn me for standing this ground;
I’ll take every stone they can carry around.
When breath becomes gravel and melody bends,
I’ll still say your name as I bury my friend.
Not saint and not symbol, not headline or throne—
Just Jeffrey, remembered, and never alone.

[Final Chorus]
With every breath, I defend your name,
Through the last black weather and the last bright flame.
I carry the friend that the world erased,
The crooked old smile and the kindness I faced.
If faith makes me foolish, that burden is mine;
I’ll hold to my memory till I run out of time.
Rest in peace, king.
Hear the final bell and the old church ring.

[Outro]
The rain quits falling; the room grows thin.
No verdict changes where my heart has been.
Goodbye, old friend—now the night can close.
I lay down my anger beside one black rose.
With my last long breath, through the silence I sing:
Rest in peace… king.

[End]

songPlan.title: The Morning Would Not End
songPlan.arrangement: Apocalyptic progressive brass-rock with a muscular moving bass line, pounding live drums, distorted guitars, low piano, emergency-brass stabs and brief half-time breaks. Tony V7 remains the sole mandatory voice profile, multiplied into one hundred individually staggered layers: rough unison leads, smoky octave doubles, muttered side comments and an enormous cracked choir in each chorus. Verses stay rhythmically urgent but melodic; the bridge builds voices in successive waves before the full ensemble locks into sustained harmony. Pace the expanded final chorus so the last sustained syllable of “ends” lands 8–12 seconds before 250 seconds, followed only by one resolved D-minor chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Sirens in the distance,
Red sun through the dust,
One hundred crooked voices say,
“Run because we must.”

[Verse 1]
I woke beneath a paper sky,
A briefcase in my hand,
The avenue was tipping like
A ship that lost the land.
We cleared the first collapsing cloud,
We counted every friend,
Then someone pointed down the road—
The morning came again.

Another flash, another roar,
Another skyline torn,
We ran into a second day
Before the first could mourn.
A hundred Tonys filled the street,
All coughing out the same:
“How many times can history strike
And still retain its name?”

[Pre-Chorus]
Heel against the pavement,
Smoke inside the sun,
Every time we find a door,
Here comes another one.

[Chorus]
The morning would not end,
It kept falling down behind us.
Nine eleven after nine eleven,
Every tower trying to find us.
Hold my sleeve, remember my name,
If the dust turns noon to night.
A hundred voices, one cracked warning:
Keep your people in your sight.

[Verse 2]
We crossed a bridge of ringing phones,
Their screens alive with ghosts,
Past taxis bent like frightened teeth
And diners burning toast.
The third one broke the river’s back,
The fourth one shook the train,
The fifth arrived before our lungs
Could learn to breathe again.

Some Tony laughed from pure despair,
One cursed the falling stone,
One carried someone else’s shoes,
One would not run alone.
We formed a ragged moving wall,
No hero at the head,
Just elbows, coats and open hands
Pulling the living from the dread.

[Pre-Chorus]
Heel against the pavement,
Ash against the tongue,
Every time the sirens fade,
Another has begun.

[Chorus]
The morning would not end,
It kept falling down behind us.
Nine eleven after nine eleven,
Every tower trying to find us.
Hold my sleeve, remember my name,
If the dust turns noon to night.
A hundred voices, one cracked warning:
Keep your people in your sight.

[Bridge]
[Half-time, voices entering in waves]
Number six beyond the tunnel,
Number seven overhead,
Eight came rolling through the harbor,
Nine turned every window red.

Then the hundred stopped together,
Not from courage, not from pride;
There was nowhere left worth running
If we left our own behind.

So we faced the endless thunder,
Linked our arms across the street,
One low note became a hundred,
Shook the rubble at our feet.

[Final Chorus]
The morning has to end,
Though it’s falling down around us.
Nine eleven after nine eleven
Cannot take the hands that found us.
Hold my sleeve, remember my name,
Bring the missing toward the light.
A hundred voices, bruised but breathing,
Keep your people in your sight.

The morning has to end,
Let the final siren leave us.
No more numbers, no more towers,
No more smoke that tries to keep us.
Through the dust we carry daylight,
Through the noise we carry friends.
A hundred Tonys sing one promise:
This is where the morning ends—
The morning ends.

[End]

songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Jeffrey, the room has lost its sound,
Just one old piano, one chair turned around.

[Verse 1]
We wore our younger faces thin,
Chasing every door that might let us in.
You knew my laughter, knew my doubt,
Knew all the words I swallowed down.
But years cast shadows no friend can defend,
And truth keeps speaking after the end.

[Chorus]
Farewell, my lifetime friend,
This is where the roadlines bend.
I grieve the man I thought I knew,
Not every terrible thing proved true.
No song can pardon, no tear amend;
Still, farewell, my lifetime friend.

[Verse 2]
The empty bench remembers hands,
Half-finished tunes and reckless plans.
Now every photograph feels strange,
A frozen smile the years rearrange.
Those left wounded deserve the light;
Their names weigh more than grief tonight.

[Bridge]
I will not polish what became,
Or hide the sorrow beneath your name.
Love can linger, judgment stand;
Both can tremble in one man's hands.

[Final Chorus]
Farewell, my lifetime friend,
No clean beginning, no gentle end.
I mourn the years, condemn the harm,
And leave old ghosts where cold walls are.
One final chord, then silence descends;
Farewell... my lifetime friend.

[End]

songPlan.arrangement: Reflective, bass-forward heartland rock with smoky electric guitar, warm organ, live drums and a lively midtempo pocket. Both duet parts use the mandatory pinned Tony v7 profile: older Tony stays rough, low and smoky; younger Tony uses the same saved identity in a naturally higher register with brighter placement, never a replacement singer. Verses alternate across the stereo field, while choruses bring both voices together in imperfect, slurred harmony. The bridge drops to bass, rim clicks and organ before a full-band final lift. Pace the outro so the final sustained word “spark” lands 8–12 seconds before 3:40, followed by one resolved D-major chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1 — Younger Tony]
I got a half-tank dream and a dashboard glow
Every road says hurry, so I’m ready to go
I’ll outrun every warning, make the hard years wait
Tell me, old man, did we ever get it straight?

[Verse 2 — Older Tony]
Kid, I recognize that match behind your grin
I spent years striking sparks just to watch them give in
You don’t have to win each room or answer every slight
Some doors look like surrender when they’re leading you right

[Pre-Chorus — Younger Tony]
Did we lose our nerve?
Did the fire burn low?

[Pre-Chorus — Older Tony]
No, I learned what deserves it
And what you let go

[Chorus — Duet]
[Younger] If you could reach through the rearview
What would you change in me?
[Older] I’d loosen your fists on the future
And let your good friends see
[Younger] Would you take back the thunder?
[Older] I’d only change its aim
[Duet] Keep the heart, lose the hurry
You don’t have to bleed for your name

[Verse 3 — Younger Tony]
Should I trust that girl who can read every bluff?
Should I call my old man, though the words come out rough?
Should I stay when the money says pack up and run?
Do I ever learn when the damage is done?

[Verse 4 — Older Tony]
Call him Sunday morning; let the silence be strange
Tell her fear wears a costume, but love doesn’t change
Save a little, sleep more, take the long way home
And don’t make being needed mean you can’t stand alone

[Chorus — Duet]
[Younger] If you could reach through the rearview
What would you change in me?
[Older] I’d loosen your fists on the future
And let your good friends see
[Younger] Would you take back the thunder?
[Older] I’d only change its aim
[Duet] Keep the heart, lose the hurry
You don’t have to bleed for your name

[Bridge — Call and Response]
[Younger] Do we get everything we wanted?
[Older] No—and thank God for that
[Younger] Do the wrong turns disappear?
[Older] No, but they stop pulling you back
[Younger] Are you proud of who I become?
[Older] I’m proud you kept becoming
[Duet] Every scar became a window
When we quit calling it nothing

[Final Chorus — Duet]
If we could meet beyond the rearview
With all our years between
I would give you back your courage
You would show me what it means
We would keep a little thunder
But never waste the flame
Keep the heart, lose the hurry
You don’t have to bleed for your name

[Outro — Older, then Younger]
[Older] I wouldn’t erase you, kid
I’d just teach you when to stay
[Younger] Then I’ll leave one light behind me
So you can find your way
[Duet] Same road, two reflections
Still becoming who we are
Keep the heart… lose the hurry…
And carry home the spark
[End]

songPlan.title: Geglash at the Thirteenth Door
songPlan.arrangement: A ten-minute, increasingly dark gothic horror-rock descent using the mandatory isolated Tony v7 voice profile. Begin sparsely with tolling bells, detuned upright piano, dry floor-tom pulses and a prowling electric bass; introduce distorted guitars, pipe organ, bowed metal and dissonant strings door by door. Preserve a strong, lively bass pocket beneath the slow 82 BPM pulse. Tony delivers smoky connected vowels, crooked timing, muttered asides and increasingly frantic sustained phrases while keeping the Geglash hook clear. Choruses grow from restrained rock into dense theatrical horror, followed by a near-silent confession, a crushing half-time breakdown and a final full-band escalation. Pace all sections across the full duration with no long instrumental gaps; sustain the final “farther in” so its last syllable lands about 10 seconds before the end, then resolve on one ominous D-minor chord and allow only its natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Midnight nails its shadow to the stones
Cold wax trembles over little bones
Somewhere in the passage, iron scratches iron
Geglash hears a voice wearing his own

[Verse 1]
He came beneath the dungeon with a lantern burning blue
A rusted little promise and a debt long overdue
The walls were wet with whispers, every brick recalled his name
Every lock had grown a mouth, every mouth pronounced his shame

He passed the empty banquet where the silver plates were clean
Yet starving hands kept reaching from the spaces in between
A child-shaped shadow followed, though it had no feet or face
It dragged a chain of memories through that unforgiving place

[Pre-Chorus]
One step, the candle gutters
Two steps, the ceiling breathes
Three steps, something underneath him
Laughs and tugs his sleeve

[Chorus]
Geglash, don’t look back
There are teeth inside the black
Every demon knows the road you took to get here
Geglash, hold the flame
When the darkness speaks your name
Is it hunting you—or have you brought it near?

[Verse 2]
The first door wore his anger like a mask of hammered tin
It opened on a fighting pit and beckoned him within
A brute with Geglash’s knuckles stood knee-deep in choking dust
Said, “You called your fury justice, but you only fed its lust”

They circled through the torch smoke, two reflections, one old scar
Each blow became a memory of how merciless men are
Geglash dropped his weapon; then the brute began to grin
Without a blade between them, it had nowhere to begin

[Pre-Chorus]
One bell, the vermin scatter
Two bells, the floorboards bleed
Three bells, every buried hunger
Claws awake beneath

[Chorus]
Geglash, don’t look back
There are teeth inside the black
Every demon knows the road you took to get here
Geglash, guard the flame
When the darkness speaks your name
Is it hunting you—or have you brought it near?

[Interlude – The Second Door]
The corridor bends where no corridor should
A clock has a tongue and a dial made of wood
It ticks with the pulse of the people he failed
Then stops as a coffin comes loose from the wall

[Verse 3]
The second door was hunger, dressed in velvet, crowned in flies
It offered him a table piled impossibly high
Red apples full of blackened seeds, warm bread that seemed to sigh
A goblet where his own reflection begged him not to die

Behind the feast, the famished pressed their faces through a grate
He heard their brittle fingernails spell mercy, much too late
The host said, “Take your fill, old friend; survival has no blame”
But every bite upon the board began to call his name

Geglash kicked the table hard; the candles drowned in grease
The starving shapes fell silent, but the silence brought no peace
For hunger is no stranger that a locked door can restrain
It builds a little altar in the hollow under pain

[Chorus – Darker]
Geglash, don’t look back
Now the teeth have found your track
Every demon wears a piece of your old skin
Geglash, shield the flame
You can curse them, you can name them
But the deepest door is waiting from within

[Verse 4]
The third door had no handle, only fingerprints in red
And every print belonged to someone Geglash had left dead
He leaned against the timber; it was warm beneath his hand
A heartbeat knocked in answer like a buried marching band

The doorway split and showed him all the roads he might have tried
The hand he could have offered, all the truths he could not hide
In every world a different face was missing from the crowd
In every world his younger self was laughing much too loud

“Oh, spare me,” Geglash muttered, with a crooked, smoky sneer
“You phantoms trade in yesterday; I’ve paid enough down here”
The laughter died. A softer voice replied behind the frame:
“You never paid the ones you hurt. You only paid in shame.”

[Instrumental Rise]
Low organ coils beneath the bass
The drums begin a funeral pace
A distant choir narrows to one note
The lantern’s blue flame turns blood-red

[Verse 5]
Then all the doors flew open and the corridor went blind
The anger and the hunger and the dead marched close behind
No claws emerged to take him, no great beast opposed his tread
They waited for the sentence he had always left unsaid

“I did it,” Geglash whispered, and the dungeon whispered too
“I chose the cruel and easy road whenever fear broke through
I wore survival like a crown; I made my terror law
And blamed the pit for every shape I willingly became”

The brute removed its battered mask—his own exhausted face
The feast collapsed to ash and flies all vanished without trace
The dead stood still around him, neither pardoning nor kind
No miracle erased the wounds; no prayer rewound the time

[Bridge]
Fear is not a doorway
Hunger is not a chain
They are hands around the lantern
They are teachers without names

You can feed them every heartbeat
You can kneel and call them fate
Or carry what you’ve done with you
And choose before too late

But deep below confession
Where even devils dread to crawl
Something older heard him speaking
Something hungry heard it all

[Breakdown]
Four steps—the lantern shatters
Five steps—the torches die
Six steps—the stone beneath him
Opens like an eye

No step—the dark is endless
No bell—the air is still
A horned shape lifts behind him
And speaks without a will:

“You think your demons needed masks?
You think the truth sets prisoners free?
I only built the thirteenth door.
You brought the other twelve to me.”

[Final Verse]
Geglash stood inside the black with neither steel nor light
The thing before him had no form, yet blotted out the night
It promised him forgetfulness, a warm and dreamless grave
One final little cowardice, and no one left to save

He heard the dead behind him, heard the starving at the grate
He heard his anger pacing like a hound that learned to wait
He could not make them love him; he could not undo the cost
But he could face the thing ahead without pretending he was lost

He struck a spark against the stone; a tiny ember grew
Not holy, clean, or innocent—just something he could do
The horned dark recoiled from it, then multiplied in size
A thousand mouths surrounded him, a thousand borrowed eyes

Still Geglash raised the ember as the ancient ceiling cracked
He did not beg for pardon, and he did not once look back
The dungeon took his shadow, but it could not take his name
He walked into the thirteenth door and carried in the flame

[Final Chorus]
Geglash, face the black
Let its teeth close at your back
Every demon knows the road that brought you here
Geglash, raise the flame
You have spoken every name
Courage isn’t clean—it only walks through fear

Geglash, through the door
Hear the buried darkness roar
Let the hunger bare the emptiness within
Geglash, scarred and stained
You may never break these chains
But tonight you choose which master you will feed

[Final Tag]
The last bell shakes the mortar
The last flame bends but stays
He walks where dawn has never lived
Through miles of eyeless maze

And far above, one raven wakes
As morning bruises red
The thirteenth door groans shut below—
But Geglash is not dead

Not clean
Not saved
Not free from what has been
Still carrying the flame
Still walking farther in

Geglash… farther in

[End]

Strip the beat to bass pulse and filtered chords for the bridge, then build into a layered final chorus. Hey there, baby, I could use just a little help

songPlan.title: Velvet Rims at Midnight
songPlan.arrangement: Jazz-noir setting for the pinned Tony V7 voice: upright bass, brushed drums, smoky piano, muted trumpet, tremolo hollow-body guitar, and restrained cinematic strings. Build from a sparse late-night opening into tense ensemble swells, then place the final sung syllable 8–12 seconds before a resolved minor chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
In the day we sweat it out on the streets
Of a runaway American dream
At night we ride through the mansions of glory
In suicide machines
Sprung from cages on Highway 9
Chrome wheeled, fuel injected, and steppin' out over the line
Oh, baby this town rips the bones from your back
It's a death trap, it's a suicide rap
We gotta get out while we're young
'Cause tramps like us, baby, we were born to run
Yes, girl, we were

[Verse 2]
Wendy, let me in, I wanna be your friend
I wanna guard your dreams and visions
Just wrap your legs 'round these velvet rims
And strap your hands 'cross my engines
Together we could break this trap
We'll run 'til we drop, baby, we'll never go back
Oh, will you walk with me out on the wire?
'Cause, baby, I'm just a scared and lonely rider
But I gotta know how it feels
I want to know if love is wild
Babe, I want to know if love is real

lyrics.text:
[Intro]
September sky, a crooked dream
Smoke in the glass, a split-screen scream
A dead man whispered, “Make it repeat”
I felt the whole world leave its feet

[Verse 1]
Bin Laden’s shadow came out of the news
Selling me thunder, handing me a fuse
Said, “Be my partner, darken the blue”
I laughed like a fool and followed him through
One became many inside my head
Sirens kept counting the living and dead
Every bright window turned into an eye
Every name asked me why, why, why

[Pre-Chorus]
No crown in the rubble
No glory in flame
Only somebody’s family
Calling somebody’s name

[Chorus]
Ash has no anthem, smoke has no throne
You cannot build a kingdom from a graveyard stone
Again and again, the nightmare may call
But murder makes nothing—nothing at all
Ash has no anthem, grief has no side
The lie sounds enormous till the innocent die
I followed the shadow, then broke from its chain
I won’t make that morning happen again

[Verse 2]
He drew me a future in charcoal and red
A calendar crowded with towers in my head
But down on the sidewalk, under the roar
A stranger held open a shattered door
Hands pulled hands from the choking gray
No god of destruction could own that day
The smallest mercy cut through the din
And something long buried woke up within

[Pre-Chorus]
No prize in the panic
No victory won
Just empty chairs waiting
When evening comes

[Chorus]
Ash has no anthem, smoke has no throne
You cannot build a kingdom from a graveyard stone
Again and again, the nightmare may call
But murder makes nothing—nothing at all
Ash has no anthem, grief has no side
The lie sounds enormous till the innocent die
I followed the shadow, then broke from its chain
I won’t make that morning happen again

[Bridge]
I faced that ghost in the furnace glow
Said, “You feed on wounds, but now I know”
He promised forever; I answered, “You lie”
Then tore up the pact beneath the black sky
No more numbers, no grand design
No stolen death dressed up as mine
Let every siren become a vow:
The killing ends here—the choice is now

[Final Chorus]
Ash has no anthem, smoke has no throne
We build from the living, not graveyard stone
Again and again, when the old hatred calls
We carry each other out through the walls
Ash has no anthem, grief has no side
Remember the names, let the truth survive
I buried the shadow and shattered its chain
That morning will never be summoned again

[Outro]
Never again—not in anyone’s name
Never again—I walk out of the flame
Hold to the living through sorrow and rain
That morning will never be summoned again

Begin with ominous clean guitar, moving bass, and restrained floor toms; expand into distorted guitars and forceful melodic choruses. Use ensemble stops around “nothing at all,” a half-time bridge, then a full-band final chorus with sustained lead notes and rough slurred tails. Keep the singer present throughout. Pace the final sustained word “again” to end around 218–222 seconds, followed by one resolved D-minor chord and a natural decay.

lyrics.text:
[Quiet Intro]
Streetlight buzz, midnight breath,
Still got jokes for the angel of death.
(Heh.)
Turn that dirty little six-string loose.

[Riff Entrance]
Yeah—right there.
Boot on the one, let the backbeat bruise.

[Verse 1]
I came up crooked with a straight-faced grin,
Half my trouble outside, half under my skin.
Made bad bets, kept worse friends,
Learned every shortcut got a toll at the end.
I got smoke in my coat, old rain in my shoes,
A talent for finding what I oughta refuse.
Still I walk in loud when the room says hush,
Put a match to regret, watch the whole thing blush.
I ain’t polished, darling, I’m friction and rust;
If you came for a saint, take the next damn bus.

[Hook 1]
Who I am is who I are,
Bent-up frame and a getaway heart.
Who I am is who I are—
Don’t buy this wreck and expect a new car.

[Verse 2]
I shook hands with demons; they complained I cheat,
Said my jokes were cold and my bourbon neat.
I said, “Life’s got a bill?” Put it under my name;
I’ve been paying in scars, but I stayed in the game.
Got a mouth like gravel in a coffee-can roll,
Little loose on the timing, little hard on the soul.
When the microphone sparks, I lean into the flame,
Forget half the lesson, still remember my name.
You can sand these edges till your fingers go numb;
I’ll be rough tomorrow like the day I begun.

[Hook 2]
Who I am is who I are,
Blacktop laugh underneath the stars.
Who I am is who I are—
Don’t tune this engine if you hate the guitar.

[Full Refrain]
So don’t hang your hopes on the man I ain’t,
Don’t paint me clean with somebody else’s paint.
I’ll love too hard, leave the screen door scarred,
Tell the truth too late in the neighbor’s yard.
Life burns down, every fuse, every spark;
I’m spending mine loud till I’m out in the dark.
Who I am is who I are—
If you’re waiting on different, you’ll wait too far.

[Turntable Break]
(Scratch it back.)
Nah—leave that bruise in.

[Verse 3]
I know where it ends: no velvet disguise,
Just a date nobody circles and a debt that arrives.
So I eat when I’m hungry, sing low when I’m hurt,
Keep one clean joke with the mud on my shirt.
I’ve apologized plenty, meant some of it too;
That’s as close to perfection as I’m likely to do.
I got people I failed and a few I pulled through,
A long list of lies—and one promise that’s true:
I won’t fold my shape for a comfortable chair,
Won’t rehearse being tame just to keep you there.
Take the whole cracked package, every burn, every bar,
Or wave from the curb while I follow that guitar.

[Expanded Refrain]
Don’t hang your hopes on the man I ain’t,
Don’t paint me clean with somebody else’s paint.
I’ll love too hard, leave the screen door scarred,
Who I am is who I are.
I’ve danced with the ditch, made the undertaker laugh,
Lost my good sense and recovered about half.
Life burns down, every fuse, every spark;
I’m spending mine loud till I’m out in the dark.
If you need a new me, then you came too late—
This old motor runs mean, but it still runs straight.
Who I am is who I are—
Expect somebody different, you’ll be disappointed hard.

[Late Instrumental Vamp]
(Hit that one!)
Bass walk mean—let the snare talk back.
(Come on.)
Still here, still scarred, still laughing at that.
One more turn—bring the whole thing home.

[Final Refrain]
Don’t hang your hopes on the man I ain’t,
Don’t paint me clean with somebody else’s paint.
I’ll love too hard, leave the screen door scarred,
Who I am is who I are.
Life burns down, every fuse, every spark;
I’m spending mine loud till I’m out in the dark.
No borrowed halo, no brand-new part—
Just a gravel-low voice and a getaway heart.
Who I am is who I are,
Who I am is who I are—
If you’re waiting on different,
you’ll wait too far.

[Final Tag]
Take me whole—or let me ride.
Who I am… is who I are.

lyrics.text:
[Verse 1]
Night shift moon on the window glass
I wake up late while the daylight fades
The room feels small, but the hour moves fast
And the walls know every excuse I've made
There's a restless drum in the radiator
A distant engine calling my name
I pull on my boots, tell the mirror, Later—
Tonight I am stepping out of the frame

[Pre-Chorus]
One small motion, one loose wire
One deep breath can wake the fire

[Chorus]
We're feathers in the floodlights
Turning gold above the street
With a wild heart and a long night
And the whole town under our feet
If tomorrow tries to hold us
We will shake it from our bones
We're feathers in the floodlights
But we don't have to fly alone

[Verse 2]
Downtown hums like a loaded jukebox
Every doorway spills a different sound
I hear my luck in the ticking crosswalk
See a thousand chances spinning around
You come laughing through the midnight traffic
With your coat thrown over one tattooed arm
Nothing polished, nothing cinematic
Just a crooked grin and a five-alarm charm

[Pre-Chorus]
One quick glance and the wires sing
Even tired hearts remember spring

[Chorus]
We're feathers in the floodlights
Turning gold above the street
With a wild heart and a long night
And the whole town under our feet
If tomorrow tries to hold us
We will shake it from our bones
We're feathers in the floodlights
But we don't have to fly alone

[Bridge]
Maybe I have waited years
For a door that wasn't locked
Maybe all those silent fears
Were only shadows on the clock
So take my hand—don't make it pretty
Let the snare crack, let the old amps roar
We can wake this sleeping city
Till we can't remember what we waited for

[Guitar Lift]

[Final Chorus]
We're feathers in the floodlights
Burning bright above the street
With a wild heart and a long night
And the thunder at our feet
Let tomorrow come and find us
With the dawn across our clothes
We're feathers in the floodlights
Going anywhere the warm wind blows

[Final Tag]
No, we don't have to fly alone
Leave the little room behind us
Leave the old excuses home
We're feathers in the floodlights
And tonight—tonight—we're going home

lyrics.text:
[Intro]
Red clock blinking on a concrete wall
One bad signal says the sky might fall
You watch me watching, I count to three
Fear writes the orders for you and me

[Verse 1]
Boot-step rhythm in the underground
Heavy black current, no mercy in the sound
Every little rumor wears a warning light
Every nervous shadow wants to strike tonight
You call it defense when you cross that line
I call it panic with a grand design
We build our towers out of doubt and wire
Then guard the switches that could start the fire

[Pre-Chorus]
Finger on the future, teeth against the past
If everyone goes first, nobody can last

[Chorus]
Before the sirens, before the flash
You make your move, I answer back
Again, again, the same mistake
We hit the world before it wakes
Before the sirens call our names
We feed the fear, we fan the flames
You swear you'll stop what I might do
I strike because I'm scared of you

[Verse 2]
Nine-one-one in the language of the state
Turn a human heartbeat to a target and a date
No face in the window, just a mark upon a screen
Clean little symbols for a dirty little dream
I hear the bassline like a warning in my chest
No one trusts the silence, no one dares to rest
We rehearse disaster till the lie feels true
Then do it all again before the other side can move

[Pre-Chorus]
Finger on the future, teeth against the past
If everyone goes first, nobody can last

[Chorus]
Before the sirens, before the flash
You make your move, I answer back
Again, again, the same mistake
We hit the world before it wakes
Before the sirens call our names
We feed the fear, we fan the flames
You swear you'll stop what I might do
I strike because I'm scared of you

[Breakdown]
Cut the feed
Kill the countdown
Drop the hand
Turn the fear around
No first blow
No righteous machine
There are living hearts behind the screen

[Bridge]
Maybe strength is leaving one switch cold
Maybe courage isn't doing what we're told
Maybe I can meet your frightened stare
And find the same alarm already burning there
The beat keeps pushing, but we choose the road
We can break the circuit, we can drop the load
No victory waits in a preemptive grave
Only one more ghost that paranoia made

lyrics.text:
[Spoken Intro — Tony, low]
Citizens, neighbors, beautiful troublemakers...
I got a platform, a necktie, an’ absolutely no plan B.

[Verse 1 — Lead]
I came down the avenue beneath a paper moon
With a borrowed blue convertible and a brass-band tune
My name was on the banners, though they spelled it three ways
I shook a thousand hands in a smoky purple haze
I promised every pothole it would never ache again
Promised shade in August, promised sunshine in the rain
But when the cameras crowded, I leaned into the call:
I’m runnin’ on a ticket with a little room for all

[Pre-Chorus — Three voices entering]
Raise the crooked crown
Pass the good word down
If the whole thing shakes, we’ll sing it into sound

[Chorus — Three-part harmony]
Drill, baby drill — through the doubt in the hill
Till we strike that river where the better days spill
Stipend checks for all — hear the bright mailbox call
If we’re gonna dream together, dream enough for us all
Oh, vote for the rascal with his heart on the wall
Stipend checks for all

[Verse 2 — Lead with answering voices]
My rival brought a graph that climbed majestically
I brought a choir of Tonys singing close behind me
One took the high road, one took the low
I wandered through the middle where the wild pledges grow
We’ll put a porch on Tuesday, put a jukebox in the square
Make the buses run on laughter and unusually clean air
No lonely little supper, no landlord ten feet tall
And Friday night the treasury buys sandwiches for all

[Pre-Chorus — Three voices]
Raise the crooked crown
Turn the hard luck ’round
When the speeches fade, let the harmony resound

[Chorus — Three-part harmony]
Drill, baby drill — through the doubt in the hill
Till we strike that river where the better days spill
Stipend checks for all — hear the bright mailbox call
If we’re gonna dream together, dream enough for us all
Oh, vote for the rascal with his heart on the wall
Stipend checks for all

[Bridge — Call and response]
[Lead]
But a promise ain’t a bridge till it carries someone home
[Low Tony]
A slogan ain’t a supper, and a throne is still a throne
[High Tony]
So keep me honest, neighbor; ring the bell if I forget
[Lead]
Take my fancy pen away before the ink is dry and set
[All]
No king behind the curtain, no saint upon the stage
Just three smoky voices on a badly folded page
We’ll lose a little swagger, let the plain truth stand up tall
A country is its people, or it isn’t much at all

[Breakdown — Staggered harmony]
Drill...
Baby, drill...
Not for gold, but for the will
Dig beneath the easy line
Find a future we can sign

[Final Chorus — Full band and three voices]
Drill, baby drill — through the doubt in the hill
Till we strike that river where the better days spill
Stipend checks for all — let the bright mailbox call
Put the supper on the table, put some mercy in the law
No, I can’t promise heaven; I can answer when you call
And if I win tomorrow, keep my picture off the wall

[Final Refrain — Sustained three-part harmony]
Stipend checks for all
A little hope for all
Keep the crooked crown small
And make some room for all

[Outro — Lead, then held harmony]
My name is Tony C...
I approve this beautiful mess.

lyrics.text:
[Verse 1]
Morning broke on a colorless plain
Three riders waited in cold silver rain
The judge read names from a weathered page
While the town leaned close to the splintered stage
No saint came down, no pardon arrived
Only the wind and the ones left alive
A black mare trembled, then pulled away
Like she knew what the people were frightened to say

[Pre-Chorus]
The law makes a circle, the blood makes a line
One takes your freedom, one takes your time

[Chorus]
Men be hung, horses go
Over the ridge where the wild winds blow
Men be hung, horses go
No fence can hold what the free ones know
Let the bells fall dumb, let the bitter river flow
Men be hung, horses go

[Verse 2]
Elias laughed with a split-lipped grin
Said, “You call this justice? Then count me in”
Caleb stared at the far red hill
And whispered a name that the night keeps still
Jonah sang low through a throat gone dry
A wandering tune with no goodbye
Then six loose reins slapped dust in the street
And thunder ran out beneath pounding feet

[Pre-Chorus]
The crowd saw a warning, the sky saw a crime
The animals answered by leaving on time

[Chorus]
Men be hung, horses go
Over the ridge where the wild winds blow
Men be hung, horses go
No fence can hold what the free ones know
Let the bells fall dumb, let the bitter river flow
Men be hung, horses go

[Bridge]
Beyond the last field, beyond human claim
The riderless herd bore nobody’s name
They crossed through the sage as the daylight burned
No hand on the reins and no head ever turned
One gave a cry like a cracked old hymn
One kicked high at the gallows wind
And somewhere behind them the ropes went tight
But the herd kept running into the light

[Breakdown]
Who owns the valley?
Who orders the sun?
Who tells a heart
When its running is done?
The judge had an answer
The earth answered slow:
You may capture men
But the horses will go

[Final Chorus]
Men be hung, horses go
Over the ridge where the wild winds blow
Men be hung, horses go
Past every boundary carved below
Let the bells fall dumb, let the bitter river flow
Men be hung, horses go

[Outro]
By dusk there were tracks where the tall weeds grow
Three names in the silence, six shadows below
The town shut its windows; the western sky glowed
Men had been hung
And the horses still rode

Baritone guitar, restless melodic bass, dry drums, tremolo electric guitar, and sparse organ build from tense narrative verses into broad, catchable choruses. Tony delivers smoky connected vowels, crooked timing, muttered verse tails, and sustained melodic hook notes. The bridge expands into pounding toms and layered guitars, followed by a brief ensemble stop before the final chorus. The last vocal lands about 10 seconds before the end, leaving only a resolved E-minor chord and natural decay.

lyrics.text:
[Intro]
Sirens in the cereal, smoke inside the rain
Tony strikes a crooked match—it fizzles in the drain
He points at the calendar, the calendar points back
Before he starts his trouble, trouble jumps the track

[Verse 1]
Tony wore a necktie made of caution tape and spite
Had a foolish little scheme for an unforgiving night
But the elevator buckled, and the ceiling lost its grin
Every door flew outward when he tried to swagger in
He shook his fist at gravity, demanded it explain
The answer hit him sideways like a runaway freight train

[Chorus]
9/11'd again, 9/11'd again
Before he can 9/11, he gets 9/11'd again
His wicked clock is stuttering, his master plan is rain
9/11'd again—9/11'd again

[Verse 2]
He ordered up a thundercloud and signed it Tony C
It landed on his own head with a note marked “delivery”
He built a grand disaster from a shopping cart and string
The cart escaped downhill and crowned him accidental king
He cursed the bent horizon, said the universe had cheated
The universe said nothing, but the whole first verse repeated

[Chorus]
9/11'd again, 9/11'd again
Before he can 9/11, he gets 9/11'd again
The fuse runs to his shoelace, every loss becomes a chain
9/11'd again—9/11'd again

[Post-Chorus]
Again—before the beginning
Again—while the room keeps spinning
Again—his bad idea comes home
And parks itself upon his throne

[Verse 3]
Tony drew a battle map in mustard on the wall
But pigeons ate the borders, so he couldn't start at all
He shouted, “This is sabotage!” and stumbled through the band
The drummer dropped a cymbal; fate applauded where he'd land
His laugh became a cough, his cough became a plea
“How come the whole catastrophe keeps happening to me?”

[Bridge]
Maybe every cruel intention is a boomerang in black
Maybe what you send into the world comes screaming back
The bass walks up, the lights cut out, the room begins to sway
Tony sees the easy answer—and looks the other way

[Breakdown]
9/11'd again
By the plot inside his brain
9/11'd again
By the engine of his pain
He mutters at the wreckage, “I was almost there, my friend”
Then the wreckage mutters louder:
“You were never gonna win.”

[Final Chorus]
9/11'd again, 9/11'd again
Before he can 9/11, he gets 9/11'd again
No glory in the ruin, only echoes down the drain
9/11'd again—9/11'd again

[Outro]
So Tony folds the blueprint and lets the sirens fade
The night rejects his violence and repossesses the parade
He walks home empty-handed through the cold September rain
Done trying to 9/11—never 9/11'd again

originalPrompt.idea: Tony C keeps getting 9/11'd while he's trying to 9/11, frustrating him.
originalPrompt.keep: Lyrics don't have to make logical sense. "9/11'd again" as a phrase must frequently be in the lyrics.

lyrics.text:
[Intro]
Ba-da, mm-ba-dah, window hummin’ low
Autumn got its cold hands everywhere I go

[Verse 1]
Morning on the radiator, barely any heat
Brown leaves scratch a crooked rhythm down the empty street
Coffee tastes like yesterday, daylight’s wearing thin
Old coat on the chair asks where the hell I’ve been
My knees predict the weather, my mirror tells the years
I laugh and call it wisdom, then swallow down the fear
Cats are in the kitchen, plants lean toward the gray
Both of them keep watching like they know I’ll go away

[Pre-Chorus]
Do-ba, dee-ba, time moves slow
Every room gets bigger when there’s nowhere else to go

[Chorus]
Who’s gonna care for my cats and plants
If I lose this tired old dance?
Who’ll turn the pots toward the afternoon
And feed those little fools beneath the moon?
Cold Autumn days, don’t close on me
I still got sparks where no one sees
Sheeeet, ya feel me? I ain’t through
There’s a little green left pushing through

[Verse 2]
Hospital on Monday, plastic bracelet tight
Fluorescent constellations buzzing through the night
Doctor said the word cancer, soft and practiced-clean
One cold syllable cutting through the humming machine
I stared out at the parking lot, rain across the glass
Counted every red tail light and watched the hours pass
Nurse brought me a blanket, said, “Let tomorrow come”
I scatted at the ceiling—bap-ba-daa—and tapped my thumb

[Pre-Chorus]
Mm-da, broken tune, don’t quit
If the heart can miss a doorway, it can find another bit

[Chorus]
Who’s gonna care for my cats and plants
If I lose this tired old dance?
Who’ll know the tabby hates closed doors
Or catch the ivy crawling on the floors?
Cold Autumn days, don’t close on me
I still got sparks where no one sees
Sheeeet, ya feel me? I ain’t through
There’s a little green left pushing through

[Bridge]
Then I dreamed a magic vaccine
Gold as October, bright and strange
It didn’t promise forever
Just one good season’s change
One more supper by the window
One more paw against my hand
One more chance to water roots
And tell somebody where I stand

[Breakdown]
Ba-rum, ba-ray, hear that old heart knock
Crooked little drummer with a busted pocket watch
I called my neighbor Rosie, gave her keys and wrote things down
Not a will of surrender—just some love passed around

[Final Chorus]
We’re gonna care for these cats and plants
We’ll keep alive this stubborn dance
She’ll turn the pots toward afternoon
I’ll feed those little fools beneath the moon
Cold Autumn days can call my name
I’ll answer rough, but I’ll answer just the same
Sheeeet, ya feel me? Here’s what I know
Love is who you teach to help things grow

[Outro]
The first frost shines, the room turns gold
I’m lonely, yes—but not alone
Ba-da, mm-ba-dah, soft and low
I close the window, keep the warm light on

lyrics.text:
[Intro]
Streetlamp glow on the avenue
Five hearts humming, making room for you

[Verse 1]
She does the work, she carries the day
Still sees her name written under the pay
They praise her fire, then bar the door
But equal means equal, not a penny less more
From the shop-floor bell to the boardroom light
Every woman owns her future and her right
No velvet rope, no old excuse
Justice ain't justice when it plays favorites loose

[Pre-Chorus]
Raise every voice they pushed aside
The harmony grows when the circle grows wide

[Chorus]
I've got binders full of women
I've got binders full of women
But names on a page won't set anybody free
Give her equal pay and full authority
I've got binders full of women
I've got binders full of women
Open every doorway, let the whole world see
Rights belong to everyone equally

[Verse 2]
Black and brown neighbors built this town
While loaded rules kept pressing them down
Newcomers working from dawn till late
Should not meet suspicion standing at the gate
Disabled dreamers know what they need
Not pity or promises—access indeed
Poor kids rising with brilliance to spare
Deserve good schools and breathable air

[Pre-Chorus]
No token chair, no borrowed pride
We change the rules with the doors thrown wide

[Chorus]
I've got binders full of women
I've got binders full of women
But names on a page won't set anybody free
Give her equal pay and full authority
I've got binders full of women
I've got binders full of women
Open every doorway, let the whole world see
Rights belong to everyone equally

[Bridge]
Listen close—beneath the old machine
A brand-new rhythm shakes the in-between
Not one at a time, not someday soon
We tune this nation to a fairer tune
A vote, a home, a job, a voice
Dignity never was somebody's choice
It isn't a favor handed down
It's the common ground where freedom is found

[Breakdown]
If one voice trembles, four stand near
Turn that whisper bright and clear
If one door closes, hands unite
Push it open in the morning light

[Final Chorus]
No more binders used for show
Let living talent lead and grow
Equal wages, equal say
Equal shelter, equal way
Every color, faith, and name
Gets the law's protection just the same
Room at every table, keys to every door
We rise together—and we settle for no less anymore

[Outro]
Five hearts humming under one streetlight
Different voices, one shared right
The last chord rings, the old walls fall
Equal means equal—equal for all

lyrics.text:
[Verse 1]
He learned to keep the weather locked behind his teeth
Carry every failure where nobody could see
No hand on his shoulder, no language for the ache
Just a glowing little kingdom saying, Brother, stay awake
They sold him iron answers in a midnight feed
A villain for his loneliness, a throne for every need
Said love was just a market and mercy made you weak
But anger sounds like purpose when you haven't been heard in weeks

[Pre-Chorus]
He wasn't born a weapon
He was looking for a name
For the hollow in the hallway
For the rules without a game

[Chorus]
They say, try that in a small town
Stand tall, never back down
We'll give you back the crown they stole
A code, a cause, a role
But every promise gets smaller
When every wall gets taller
You can't build a life by shutting the whole world out
Try that in a small town

[Verse 2]
He wanted work that mattered, friends who'd call him first
A father who could tell him what to do with all the hurt
A chance to be desired without performing like a king
Some proof that being useful wasn't worth more than being seen
The screen supplied a brotherhood with targets painted red
Easy little certainties to tuck him into bed
Said tenderness was surrender, and doubt was a disease
Then charged another payment for the secret to be free

[Pre-Chorus]
There was truth beneath the sales pitch
Men are starving to belong
But a wound becomes a business
When the cure keeps it raw

[Chorus]
They say, try that in a small town
Stand tall, never back down
We'll give you back the crown they stole
A code, a cause, a role
But every promise gets smaller
When every wall gets taller
You can't build a life by shutting the whole world out
Try that in a small town

[Bridge]
You can lift the weight, learn the trade
Keep your word and still be afraid
You can want respect without demanding control
You can lose, you can grieve, you can ask what you need
Without making an enemy feed your soul
No guru owns the doorway
No stranger holds the key
Brotherhood ain't worship
And strength ain't cruelty

[Breakdown]
Tell me what was missing
A table, a teacher, a place in the crowd?
Tell me what they promised
A kingdom where pain could never speak aloud?
I won't laugh at the hunger
I won't kneel to the lie
A man can need another man
And look him in the eye

[Final Chorus]
They said, try that in a small town
Stand tall, never back down
But nobody needs a stolen crown
To turn his whole life around
Let every promise grow larger
Let every open door start here
Build a life with people, not a bunker made of fear
If the town is worth defending
Let compassion make it strong
There is room beside the fire
You were needed all along

[Outro]
No throne, no target, no final score
Just hands rebuilding what the hurt tore
Say what you need, let the old walls fall
A stronger man can answer when his brothers call
